resolution.

messages: One or more cables are missing from arg1.
records.explanation: One or more cables have been detected as missing from the Fault Tolerant storage controller identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure all cables are properly connected. For information about cabling, see the Owners Manual
available at the support site.

messages: SAS cable arg1 to expander arg2 is not connected.
records.explanation: SAS cables are not connected to the expander correctly.
records.recommended_action:
Check whether or not the SAS cables are connected to the expander. Reconnect the cables and retry
the operation.

messages: Unable to create or update the FCoE uplink, because the firmware version of the I/O Module running the Fabric Manager does not support Native VLAN configuration for FCoE uplinks.
records.explanation: The FCoE uplink cannot be created or updated, because the firmware version of the I/O Module running the Fabric Manager does not support Native VLAN configuration for FCoE uplinks.
records.cause: The FCoE uplink cannot be created or updated, because the firmware version of the I/O Module running the Fabric Manager does not support Native VLAN configuration for FCoE uplinks.
records.recommended_action:
Update the firmware version of the I/O Module running the Fabric Manager and retry the operation.
For information about the recommended I/O Module firmware versions, see the OpenManage
Enterprise-Modular Users Guide available on the support site.

messages: Unable to replicate Multi-Chassis Management data from lead to backup chassis arg1 because of a firmware version mismatch between both the chassis.
records.explanation: The Multi-Chassis Management data cannot be replicated from the lead to the backup chassis identified in the message because of a firmware mismatch between both the chassis.
records.cause: The Multi-Chassis Management data cannot be replicated from the lead to the backup chassis identified in the message because of a firmware mismatch between both the chassis.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the firmware version of both the lead and backup chassis is same and retry the
operation. For information about updating the firmware version of an Multi-Chassis Management
(MCM), see the OpenManage Enterprise-Modular User Guide available on the support site.

messages: Unable to process the request because the uplink for FC Media Type (FCoE, FC Gateway, and Direct Attach) can accept port(s) only from the same IOM.
records.explanation: The request cannot be processed because the uplink for FC Media Type (FCoE, FC Gateway, and Direct Attach) can accept port(s) only from the same IOM.
records.cause: The request cannot be processed because the uplink for FC Media Type (FCoE, FC Gateway, and Direct Attach) can accept port(s) only from the same IOM.
records.recommended_action:
Enter port(s) numbers that are from only the same IOM and then retry the operation. For more
information see the OpenManageEnterprise-Modular Users Guide available on the support site.

messages: Unable to complete the operation because the NIC partition identifier arg1 does not exist.
records.explanation: The operation could not be completed because the NIC partition identifer, identified in the message, does not exist or could not be retrieved.
records.cause: The operation could not be completed because the NIC partition identifer, identified in the message, does not exist or could not be retrieved.
records.recommended_action: Check the NIC partition ID is valid by retrieving it from the NIC identifier. Then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to complete the arg1 operation on the fabric because the firmware version of the I/O module running the fabric manager does not support the configuration feature.
records.explanation: The operation cannot be completed on the fabric because the firmware version of the I/O module running the fabric manager does not support the configuration feature.
records.cause: The operation cannot be completed on the fabric because the firmware version of the I/O module running the fabric manager does not support the configuration feature.
records.recommended_action:
Update the firmware version of the I/O Module running the Fabric Manager and retry the operation.
For information about the recommended I/O Module firmware versions, see the OpenManage
Enterprise-Modular Users Guide available on the support site.

messages: Replication of Chassis Settings will be applied only when IOM Device arg1 is online.
records.explanation: The operation to Replicate Chassis Settings failed as IOM is not online.
records.recommended_action: Please try bring your IOM online. If the issue persists, contact your system administrator.

messages: Replication of Chassis Settings for arg1 was successfully submitted on the IOM Device arg2 with following error(s):arg3.
records.explanation: The operation to Replicate Chassis Settings failed. Retry the operation.
records.recommended_action: The operation to Replicated Chassis Settings failed. Retry the operation.

messages: The Multi Chassis Management Group is restored with basic details after Firmware Update; reconfigure with required details.
records.explanation: An issue is identified with Multi Chassis Management Group and is restored with basic details after Firmware Update.
records.recommended_action:
Manual "Multi Chassis Management Group" configuration is required by using "Edit Group" wizard
from "Group Configuration" of Lead Chassis Dashboard.

messages: Unable to synchronize the primary and secondary CMC removable flash media and the Extended Storage feature is not available.
records.explanation: The Extended Storage feature is not activated if the removable flash media SD Card on the secondary CMC is not functioning properly.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following and retry the operation: 1) In the CMC Web interface, go to Chassis Controller
> Flash Media > Configuration, and verify if the SD card on secondary CMC displays errors. 2) If
errors are displayed, execute the following racadm command: "racadm cmcchangeover". 3) Repair the
removable flash media SD Card by selecting the Chassis Controller > Flash Media > Configuration >
Repair Active Controller Media in the CMC Web interface. Repairing is only allowed on the SD card of
the primary CMC. If the problem persists, replace the card.

messages: Unable to synchronize the data in the Extended Storage removable flash media in the primary and secondary CMCs/MMs.
records.explanation: The data on the Extended Storage removable flash media SD cards is not synchronized when the CMC is unable to determine which card has the latest data.
records.recommended_action:
Disable and then enable the Extended Storage feature. Using racadm, execute the following
commands: "racadm feature -d -c Extended Storage" to disable and then "racadm -a -c Extended
Storage" to enable the feature. NOTE: All the data on the removable flash media SD card is erased
when the feature is disabled.

messages: The Extended Storage feature activation timed out. The feature is not active.
records.explanation: The Extended Storage feature is not activated if the removable flash media SD card on the secondary CMC does not respond within 90 seconds after activation is initiated.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following and retry the operation: 1) In the CMC Web interface, go to Chassis Controller
> Flash Media > Configuration, and verify if the SD card on secondary CMC displays errors. 2) If
errors are displayed, execute the following racadm command: "racadm cmcchangeover". 3) Repair the
removable flash media SD Card by selecting the Chassis Controller > Flash Media > Configuration >
Repair Active Controller Media in the CMC Web interface. Repairing is only allowed on the SD card of
the primary CMC. If the problem persists, replace the card.

messages: Fabric mismatch is detected in the I/O Module arg1.
records.explanation: This error may occur due to any of the following conditions: 1) Invalid I/O Module and mezzanine card configuration, where a newly installed I/O Modules fabric type and the resident mezzanine cards fabric types do not match or are incompatible. 2) Invalid I/O Module and I/O Module configuration, where a newly installed I/O Module has a different or incompatible fabric type from an I/O Module already installed in the fabric.
records.cause: This error may occur due to any of the following conditions: 1) Invalid I/O Module and mezzanine card configuration, where a newly installed I/O Modules fabric type and the resident mezzanine cards fabric types do not match or are incompatible. 2) Invalid I/O Module and I/O Module configuration, where a newly installed I/O Module has a different or incompatible fabric type from an I/O Module already installed in the fabric.
records.recommended_action: Refer to Chassis Management Controller Users Guide for additional information.

messages: The I/O Module arg1 did not boot within the expected time.
records.explanation: The I/O module may have taken more time to boot than was expected or the I/O module did not boot.
records.recommended_action:
Verify the I/O Module is turned on using CMC/MM Web Interface or RACADM CLI and retry the
operation. Otherwise, reinsert the I/O Module and retry the operation. If the issue persists, Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: The LOM riser FRU for slot arg1 FRU ID arg2 is not functioning.
records.explanation: FRU of the LOM riser specified in the message is not functioning or CMC is unable to read it.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Reset iDRAC of the specified server or virtual reseat the server. 2) Reset CMC
and wait for a few minutes. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using
iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual
Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to retrieve the server-arg1 CPU information.
records.explanation: CMC is unable to obtain the CPU information from the server specified in the message. This occurs if there is no communication between CMC and iDRAC.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Reset iDRAC. 2) Reset CMC. If the issue persists, Collect a
SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: Unable to obtain or send link tuning or flex address data to server-arg1.
records.explanation: CMC is unable to obtain the link tuning or flex address information for the newly installed hardware (server, Input Output Module, or Mezzanine card), or is unable to send the link tuning or flex address information to iDRAC.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the currently installed CMC firmware is the latest. Otherwise, update the CMC with
the latest CMC firmware and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to read the FRU information, status = arg1
records.explanation: Unable to read the header of the extended FRU information. This can occur if there is a problem in the communication between the CMC and the server.
records.recommended_action:
Remove and reinsert the server. The CMC will retry the read operation of the FRU information.
If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://
www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze
the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to turn on High Power Management for the server arg1
records.explanation: Unable to turn on the server specified in the message because of an internal CMC error.
records.recommended_action: Reboot CMC and retry the operation. If the issue persists, reseat the server and retry the operation.

messages: The CMC arg1 has reset because the thermal threshold was exceeded.
records.explanation: The CMC specified in the message has reset because of thermal issues.
records.cause: The CMC specified in the message has reset because of thermal issues.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Review the Hardware Log and check if there are fans that are not functioning
properly. 2) Replace the fans that are not functioning properly. 3) If all the fans are functioning,
check the chassis temperature in the CMC Web Interface or by using RACADM. When the fans are
functioning properly and the chassis temperature is too high, the ambient air temperature is too high
or the air inlets are not receiving sufficient air.

messages: Detected a missing process failover condition detected. Process = arg1.
records.explanation: A firmware error has occurred causing a CMC failover. The process identified in the message was not detected. The CMC will restart automatically.
records.recommended_action:
If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://
www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze
the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Issues identified with Process arg1. Failover condition detected.
records.explanation: A firmware error has occurred in the internal firmware process identified in the message. This condition will cause a CMC/MM failover to occur. If the issue persists, contact your service provider.
records.recommended_action:
No response action is required. A failover may result from this condition. If multiple failovers
occur, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Missing kernel module arg1. Failover condition detected.
records.explanation: A firmware error occurred causing the failover. If this condition continues, a failover will result. If multiple failovers occur, contact Service.
records.recommended_action:
No response action is required. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report
using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the
Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: An internal network error occurred.
records.explanation: An internal network error occurred. If none of the external sources have an issue, the CMC/MM may have a hardware issue. If the issue persists, contact your service provider.
records.recommended_action: Reseat the network cable and check the connectivity to the outbound switch.

messages: The coin cell battery in the primary CMC is not working.
records.explanation: The coin cell battery in the primary CMC is not working. The battery needs to be replaced.
records.recommended_action: Replace the coin cell battery in the primary CMC.

messages: The coin cell battery in CMC arg1 is not working.
records.explanation: The coin cell battery in the CMC located in the slot specified in the message is not working. The battery needs to be replaced.
records.recommended_action: Replace the coin cell battery of the standby CMC.

messages: Unable to read the FRU information from the server arg1, status arg2.
records.explanation: CMC cannot read the information about the FRU, because of an internal issue with the CMC and the server. Some information such as model number may not be reported. The server may not power up if the server planar FRU cannot be read.
records.recommended_action:
Remove and reinsert the server. The Chassis Management Controller will retry the read operation
of the FRU information. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using
iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual
Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to retrieve information about the firmware on server in slot arg1, because there is no communication between Chassis Management Controller (CMC) and iDRAC.
records.explanation: Information about the firmware on server in slot identified in the message cannot be retrieved because there is no communication between Chassis Management Controller (CMC) and iDRAC.
records.cause: Information about the firmware on server in slot identified in the message cannot be retrieved because there is no communication between Chassis Management Controller (CMC) and iDRAC.
records.recommended_action:
1) Reset iDRAC by using the graphical user interface (GUI): Click Chassis Overview > Troubleshooting
> Reset Components. In the Reset Server section, from the Reset drop-down menu, select iDRAC
Reset corresponding to the server iDRAC to be reset, and then click Apply Selection. Or, reset
iDRAC by running the following command at the command line interface (CLI): racadm racreset -m
server-n. 2) Reset Chassis Management Controller (CMC) by using the GUI: Click Chassis Overview >
Troubleshooting > Reset Components, and then click Reset/Failover CMC. Or, reset CMC by running
the following command at the CLI: racadm racreset. For more information about the syntax and
parameters used, see the iDRAC 8/7 v2.30.30.30 RACADM CLI Guide and the Chassis Management
Controller Version 5.0 for Dell PowerEdge M1000e RACADM Command Line Reference Guide available
on the support site.

messages: Unable to read the Complex Programmable Logical Device (CPLD) version number of sleeve arg1 because the CPLD version is very old, or the Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to identify the version.
records.explanation: The version number of Complex Programmable Logical Device (CPLD) on the sleeve identified in the message cannot be read because the CPLD version is very old, or the Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to identify the version.
records.cause: The version number of Complex Programmable Logical Device (CPLD) on the sleeve identified in the message cannot be read because the CPLD version is very old, or the Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to identify the version.
records.recommended_action:
Update the CPLD version of sleeve and retry the operation. For more information about the
recommended CPLD versions, see the Chassis Management Controller Users Guide available at the
support site.

messages: Unable to read the Complex Programmable Logical Device (CPLD) version number of sled arg1 because the CPLD version is very old, or the Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to identify the version.
records.explanation: The version number of Complex Programmable Logical Device (CPLD) on the sled identified in the message cannot be read because the CPLD version is very old, or the Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to identify the version.
records.cause: The version number of Complex Programmable Logical Device (CPLD) on the sled identified in the message cannot be read because the CPLD version is very old, or the Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to identify the version.
records.recommended_action:
Update the CPLD version of sled and retry the operation. For more information about the
recommended CPLD versions, see the Chassis Management Controller Users Guide available at the
support site.

messages: Hard drive not detected in the Management Module at slot arg1.
records.explanation: The Management Module at slot identified in the message has not detected one of the hard drives.
records.recommended_action:
If the problem persists for several minutes then do the following : 1) Physically reseat the
Management Module. 2) Perform a Powercycle operation of the Management Module.

messages: Synchronization failed.
records.explanation: Synchronization failure could be due to: Incorrect console FQDN, incorrect iDRAC credentials, or Baseboard Management Controller (BMC) IP not configured in the System Center console.
records.cause: Synchronization failure could be due to: Incorrect console FQDN, incorrect iDRAC credentials, or Baseboard Management Controller (BMC) IP not configured in the System Center console.
records.recommended_action: For more information, check the In-Band and Out-of-Band job details.

messages: CPU arg1 has a thermal trip (over-temperature) event.
records.explanation: The processor temperature increased beyond the operational range. Thermal protection shut down the processor. Factors external to the processor may have induced this exception.
records.recommended_action:
Review logs for fan failures, replace failed fans. If no fan failures are detected, check inlet temperature
(if available) and reinstall processor heatsink.

messages: CPU arg1 has failed the built-in self-test (BIST).
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action:
1) Turn system off and remove input power for one minute. Re-apply input power and turn system
on. 2) Make sure the processor is inserted correctly, if the processor is removable. 3) If the issue still
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: CPU arg1 is stuck in POST.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action:
1) Turn off the server and disconnect input power for one minute. Re-apply input power and turn
system on. 2) Reduce system configuration to minimum memory and remove all PCI devices. If system
completes POST, update system BIOS. Re-install memory and PCI one component at a time to
meet the original configuration. 3) If the issue still persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR)
report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use
the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: CPU arg1 configuration is unsupported.
records.explanation: System is unable to boot or may run in a degraded state.
records.recommended_action: Review product documentation for supported CPU configurations.

messages: Unrecoverable CPU complex error detected on CPU arg1.
records.explanation: System is unable to boot or may run in a degraded state.
records.recommended_action:
1) Turn system off and remove input power for one minute. Re-apply input power and turn
system on. 2) Make sure the processor is seated correctly. 3) If the issue still persists, Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: CPU arg1 is disabled.
records.explanation: System is unable to boot or may run in a degraded state.
records.recommended_action: If unexpected, check presence, and system setup (BIOS) configuration.

messages: CPU arg1 is throttled.
records.explanation: The CPU is throttled due to thermal or power conditions.
records.cause: The CPU is throttled due to thermal or power conditions.
records.recommended_action: Review system logs for power or thermal exceptions.

messages: CPU arg1 terminator is absent.
records.explanation: System is unable to boot or may run in a degraded state.
records.recommended_action: Check presence and reinstall the terminator.

messages: CPU arg1 initialization error detected.
records.explanation: System BIOS was unable to boot the processor.
records.recommended_action:
1) Turn system off and remove input power for one minute. Re-apply input power and turn
system on. 2) Make sure the processor is seated correctly. 3) If the issue still persists, Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: CPU arg1 protocol error detected.
records.explanation: System event log and OS logs may indicate that the exception is external to the processor.
records.recommended_action:
1) Check system and operating system logs for exceptions. If no exceptions are found continue.
2) Turn system off and remove input power for one minute. Re-apply input power and turn
system on. 3) Make sure the processor is seated correctly. 4) If the issue still persists, Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: CPU bus parity error detected.
records.explanation: System event log and OS logs may indicate that the exception is external to the processor.
records.recommended_action:
Check system and operating system logs for exceptions. If no exceptions found, remove input power,
reinstall the processor, then apply input power.

messages: CPU arg1 machine check error detected.
records.explanation: System event log and OS logs may indicate that the exception is external to the processor.
records.recommended_action:
1) Check system and operating system logs for exceptions. If no exceptions are found, continue
to step 2 Otherwise, go to step 3. 2) Update BIOS, if an update is available. 3) If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: CPU arg1 voltage regulator module failed.
records.explanation: System performance may be degraded or the system may fail to operate.
records.recommended_action:
1) Turn system off and remove input power for one minute. Re-apply input power and turn
system on. 2) Make sure the processor is seated correctly. 3) If the issue still persists, Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: A predictive failure detected on CPU arg1 voltage regulator module.
records.explanation: System performance may be degraded or the system may fail to operate.
records.recommended_action:
1) Turn system off and remove input power for one minute. Re-apply input power and turn
system on. 2) Make sure the processor is seated correctly. 3) If the issue still persists, Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: The power input for CPU arg1 voltage regulator module is lost.
records.explanation: System performance may be degraded or the system may fail to operate.
records.recommended_action:
1) Turn system off and remove input power for one minute. Re-apply input power and turn
system on. 2) Make sure the processor is seated correctly. 3) If the issue still persists, Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: The power input for CPU arg1 voltage regulator module is outside of range.
records.explanation: System performance may be degraded or the system may fail to operate.
records.recommended_action:
1) Turn system off and remove input power for one minute. Re-apply input power and turn
system on. 2) Make sure the processor is seated correctly. 3) If the issue still persists, Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: The power input for CPU arg1 voltage regulator module is outside of range, but it is attached to the system.
records.explanation: System performance may be degraded or the system may fail to operate.
records.recommended_action:
1) Turn system off and remove input power for one minute. Re-apply input power and turn
system on. 2) Make sure the processor is seated correctly. 3) If the issue still persists, Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: CPU arg1 voltage regulator module is incorrectly configure.
records.explanation: System performance may be degraded or the system may fail to operate.
records.recommended_action: Review product documentation for proper configuration and installation procedures.

messages: CPU arg1 voltage regulator module is absent.
records.explanation: System performance may be degraded or the system may fail to operate.
records.recommended_action: If removal was unintended, check presence and re-install .

messages: The Machine Check system address reported by the processor is arg1.
records.explanation: The Machine Check system address reported by the processor is indicated in the message.
records.recommended_action:
This event contains a system address of a component related to a failure reported by the CPU. Map
this address to a component in the system to find the source of the error.

messages: A Machine Check event error occurred because the CPU received invalid data (arg1, arg2).
records.explanation: A Machine Check event error occurred because the CPU received invalid data as identified in the message.
records.cause: A Machine Check event error occurred because the CPU received invalid data as identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
If the CPU4001 message is reported after CPU4003, map the address reported in CPU4001 to a
system component. Update the component driver and firmware. Else, no response action is required.

messages: A Machine Check event error occurred because of a timeout while the CPU accessed an external device or component: (arg1, arg2).
records.explanation: A Machine Check event error occurred because of a timeout while the CPU accessed an external device or component as identified in the message.
records.cause: A Machine Check event error occurred because of a timeout while the CPU accessed an external device or component as identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
If the CPU4001 message is reported after CPU4004, map the address reported in CPU4001 to a
system component. Update the component driver and firmware. Else, no response action is required.

messages: A Machine Check error was reported by the CPU: (arg1, arg2).
records.explanation: A Machine Check error was reported by the CPU.
records.recommended_action:
Update the UEFI BIOS. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using
iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual
Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: A diagnostic warning event occurred in the High Bandwidth Memory device at arg1. Perform a cold reboot operation. (Extended ID: arg2).
records.explanation: A diagnostic warning event occurred in the High Bandwidth Memory device at location identified in the message. System will attempt to perform self-healing or self-correction.
records.recommended_action:
Perform a cold reboot to allow server to attempt self-healing or self-correction. If a cold reboot
has already occurred subsequent to this message then no further action is required. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: A diagnostic warning event occurred in the High Bandwidth Memory device at arg1. (Extended ID: arg2).
records.explanation: A diagnostic warning event occurred in the High Bandwidth Memory device at the location identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://
www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze
the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: An unknown diagnostic Warning event occurred in the High Bandwidth Memory device at arg1. (Extended ID: arg2).
records.explanation: An unknown diagnostic Warning event occurred in the High Bandwidth Memory device at the location identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Update iDRAC firmware to the latest version available during the next maintenance cycle. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: A diagnostic critical event occurred in the High Bandwidth Memory device at arg1. (Extended ID: arg2).
records.explanation: A diagnostic critical event occurred in the High Bandwidth Memory device at the location identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://
www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze
the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: An unknown diagnostic Critical event occurred in the High Bandwidth Memory device at arg1. (Extended ID: arg2).
records.explanation: An unknown diagnostic Critical event occurred in the High Bandwidth Memory device at the location identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Update iDRAC firmware to the latest version available during the next maintenance cycle. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: A link width degradation has occurred in the CPU interconnect arg1.
records.explanation: A link width degradation has occurred in the CPU interconnect identified in the message. The system performance may be degraded or the system may stop operating.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Restart the server and verify whether or not the issue persists. 2) If yes, reseat
the processors, and then restart the server. 3) If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection
(TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic
to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: An issue is detected because CPUs are incorrectly installed in the sockets.
records.explanation: An issue is detected because CPUs are incorrectly installed in the sockets. The system cannot be powered on when the CPUs are not properly populated.
records.cause: An issue is detected because CPUs are incorrectly installed in the sockets. The system cannot be powered on when the CPUs are not properly populated.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following and retry the operation: 1) Power off the server and disconnect the input power. 2)
Make sure the CPU is correctly installed if the processor is removable. 3) Connect the input power
and power on the server. 4) If theissue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using
iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual
Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: CPU arg1 is absent
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action: Verify processor installation. If present, reseat the processor.

messages: Unable to update details of the device arg1 because device PSU count is lesser than the total Power Distribution Unit (PDU) outlet assigned to it.

messages: Unable to update details of the device arg1 because device PSU count cannot be more than 8.

messages: Power redundancy sensor transitioned to error state for rack physical group arg1 at location arg2. The total PSUs available are arg3 and the healthy PSUs available are arg4.

messages: The arg1 cache has been discarded.
records.explanation: The controller has flushed the cache and all data in the cache has been lost. This may occur when the system has memory or battery problems that cause the controller to distrust the cache. Although user data may have been lost, this alert does not always indicate that relevant or user data has been lost.
records.cause: The controller has flushed the cache and all data in the cache has been lost. This may occur when the system has memory or battery problems that cause the controller to distrust the cache. Although user data may have been lost, this alert does not always indicate that relevant or user data has been lost.
records.recommended_action: Verify that the battery and memory are functioning properly.

messages: The Key exchange process for the encrypted drive(s) behind arg1 was unsuccessful.
records.explanation: The Key exchange process for the controller identified in the message failed.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure of the following and retry the operation: 1) The iDRAC is able to communicate to the Key
Management Server. 2) The device for which the key is generated is online and responding. 3) The
device for which the key exchange is required is in the same Key Management Server Domain.

messages: iDRAC is unable to successfully communicate with the device arg1, because of one or more of the following reasons: device is incorrectly seated, iDRAC firmware error, device is in a shutdown state or device firmware error.
records.explanation: iDRAC is unable to successfully communicate with the device identified in the message. This issue could have happened because of one or more of the following reasons: device is incorrectly seated, device firmware error, device is in a shutdown state or iDRAC firmware error.
records.cause: iDRAC is unable to successfully communicate with the device identified in the message. This issue could have happened because of one or more of the following reasons: device is incorrectly seated, device firmware error, device is in a shutdown state or iDRAC firmware error.
records.recommended_action:
Ensure that the following are correct, and then retry the operation by running the following command
at the Command Line Interface (CLI): racadm racreset. 1) The device is correctly operating in the
host operating system. 2) The device and iDRAC firmware versions are latest. Also ensure that the
device is properly installed and cabled. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR)
report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use
the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: The storage controller arg1 is unable to communicate to the BMC because of arg2 Error. iDRAC management for this device is unavailable.
records.explanation: The storage controller is unable to communicate to the BMC because of the reason identified in the message. iDRAC management for this device is unavailable.
records.recommended_action:
Run the following RACADM command at the Command Line Interface (CLI) and retry the operation:
racadm racreset. For more information about RACADM commands of iDRAC, see the latest version of
"iDRAC with Lifecycle Controller RACADM CLI Guide" available on the support site.

messages: Single-bit ECC error limit exceeded on the arg1 DIMM.
records.explanation: The storage controller memory identified in the message is not operating correctly.
records.recommended_action:
If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://
www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze
the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: The iDRAC firmware version is not compatible with the storage controller arg1 firmware version, and therefore, the Sideband Management feature is unavailable.

resolution.

messages: The installed version of OpenManage Server Administrator is not compatible with the firmware version installed on one or more current storage controllers. Inventory and management will not be supported for these storage controllers.

Identify and downloadthe OpenManage Server Administrator version that supports this
StorageController firmware version. If the issue persists, contact your serviceprovider.

messages: The installed version of OpenManage Server Administrator is not compatible with arg1 firmware version.
records.explanation: The installed versionof OpenManage Server Administrator is not compatible with this StorageController firmware. Controller inventory and management may be impacted.
records.recommended_action:
Identify and downloadthe OpenManage Server Administrator version that supports this
StorageController firmware version. If the issue persists, contact your serviceprovider.

messages: The fan has stopped functioning on the controller arg1. Part number: arg2.
records.explanation: The controller fan has stopped functioning. The RPM value of the fan may be less than the minimum threshold value that has resulted in a fan failure.
records.recommended_action: Replace the controller if the FAN has stopped functioning.

messages: The current firmware version arg1 is older than the required version arg2 for arg3.
records.explanation: The firmware on the controller identified in the message is not a supported version.
records.recommended_action: Download the supported version from the service provider and install it on the controller.

messages: Unable to open the firmware and driver configuration file arg1 of arg2.
records.explanation: Storage Management is unable to determine whether the system has the minimum required versions of the RAID controller firmware and driver due to one of the following: 1) Incorrect installation directory path to the configuration file. 2) Removed or renamed configuration file.
records.cause: Storage Management is unable to determine whether the system has the minimum required versions of the RAID controller firmware and driver due to one of the following: 1) Incorrect installation directory path to the configuration file. 2) Removed or renamed configuration file.
records.recommended_action: Reinstall Server Administrator Storage Management software on the operating system.

messages: Redundant path disconnected on arg1.
records.explanation: The controller identified in the message has two connectors that are connected to the same enclosure. The communication path on one connector has lost connection with the enclosure. The communication path on the other connector is reporting this loss.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure both the cables are securely attached to the enclosure and controller. For more information
about connecting the cables to the enclosure, see the Cables Attached Correctly section in the PERC
Users Guide. Also, make sure both Enclosure Management Modules (EMMs) are healthy.

messages: A multi-bit Error Correction Code (ECC) error is detected on the arg1. Part number: arg2.
records.explanation: An error involving multiple bits is detected during the Read or Write operation. The error correction algorithm recalculates parity data during read/write operations. If the issue involves a single bit, the algorithm will correct and maintain parity data. In case of multiple bits, the data may be lost. However, in some multi-bit error cases, if issue occurs during Read operation, the data on the drive may be retained. However the data is lost during a Write operation.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the controller. For information about replacing the controller, see the respective PERC Users
Guide available on the support site.

messages: Single-bit ECC error on arg1.
records.explanation: The Dual In-line Memory Module (DIMM) is beginning to malfunction.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the Dual In-line Memory Module (DIMM) to avoid data loss or data corruption. The DIMM is a
part of the controller battery pack. Refer to hardware documentation for information on replacing the
DIMM.

messages: Single-bit ECC error. The arg1 DIMM is critically degraded.
records.explanation: The Dual In-line Memory Module (DIMM) is malfunctioning. Data loss or data corruption may occur.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the DIMM immediately to avoid data loss or data corruption. The DIMM is a part of the
controller battery pack. Refer to the storage hardware documentation for information on replacing the
DIMM.

messages: A foreign configuration was detected on arg1.
records.explanation: The controller has physical disks that were moved from another controller or have been removed and replaced on the current configuration. These physical disks contain virtual disks that were created on the current or other controller. See the storage hardware documentation for Import Foreign Configuration and Clear Foreign Configuration for more information. Foreign configuration is seen when a controller is replaced.
records.recommended_action: Import or clear the detected foreign configuration using a configuration tool or utility.

messages: The NVRAM has corrupted data on arg1.
records.explanation: The NVRAM has corrupted data. This may occur after a power surge, a battery failure, or for other reasons. The controller is reinitializing the NVRAM.
records.recommended_action:
No response action is required as the controller is taking the required corrective action. However, If
this message is generated often (such as during each reboot), then replace the controller.

messages: Bad block replacement error on arg1.
records.explanation: A portion of a physical disk is damaged. See Receive a "Bad Block" Alert with "Replacement," "Sense," or "Medium" Error for more information.
records.recommended_action:
See Receive a "Bad Block" Alert with "Replacement," "Sense," or "Medium" Error for more
information.

messages: The arg1 NVRAM has corrupt data.
records.explanation: The NVRAM has corrupt data. The controller is unable to correct the situation.
records.recommended_action: Replace the controller.

messages: arg1 SAS port report: arg2
records.explanation: The controller detected an issue because of incorrectly connecting the SAS cables to the enclosure or backplane.
records.cause: The controller detected an issue because of incorrectly connecting the SAS cables to the enclosure or backplane.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the SAS cables are firmly attached to the enclosure or backplane. For information
about using SAS cables, see the respective PowerEdge server Installation and Service Manual
available on the support site.

messages: arg1 SAS SMP communications error arg2
records.explanation: The text for this alert is generated by the firmware and can vary depending on the situation. The reference to SMP in this text refers to SAS Management Protocol.
records.recommended_action:
There may be a SAS topology error. See the hardware documentation for information on correct
SAS topology configurations. There may be problems with the cables such as a loose connection
or an invalid cabling configuration. See the Cables Attached Correctly section for more information
on checking the cables. See the hardware documentation for information on correct cabling
configurations. Verify that the firmware version is supported.

messages: Bad block sense error from arg1
records.explanation: A portion of a physical disk is damaged. See Receive a "Bad Block" Alert with "Replacement," "Sense," or "Medium" Error for more information.
records.recommended_action:
See Receive a "Bad Block" Alert with "Replacement," "Sense," or "Medium" Error for more
information.

messages: Physical disks found missing from configuration during boot time on arg1.
records.explanation: The controller has detected a change in the storage configuration between since its last shut down. This can generally happen if some configured physical disks are removed from the system when the system was shutdown.
records.recommended_action: Shut down the system. Re-insert the removed physical disks and re-start the system.

messages: Preserved cache detected on arg1.
records.explanation: The controller has preserved data in the cache from a virtual disk, which it can no longer locate. No data loss has occurred as the controller is saving these operations in its cache.
records.recommended_action:
Check for the existence of a foreign configuration and import if any. Check that enclosures are cabled
correctly.

messages: A configuration command could not be committed to disk on arg1
records.explanation: The controller encountered errors while applying the configuration on the physical disks. The configuration command applied has not taken effect.
records.recommended_action:
Re-issue the failed configuration command or try with a different set of physical disks. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Communication with arg1 has been lost.
records.explanation: The management controller is not communicating with the storage controller identified in the message. This may be because of any one of the following: 1) PCIe subsystem is has stopped functioning 2) An issue in the storage controller 3) An issue in the management controller.
records.cause: The management controller is not communicating with the storage controller identified in the message. This may be because of any one of the following: 1) PCIe subsystem is has stopped functioning 2) An issue in the storage controller 3) An issue in the management controller.

Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: arg1 is running an unsupported firmware version.
records.explanation: The firmware on the controller identified in the message is not supported by this version of the CMC. This may result in degraded functionality.
records.recommended_action:
Update the CMC Firmware to the latest version available or revert the controller firmware to a
previous version.

messages: arg1 is operating at less than optimal bandwidth.
records.explanation: The controller identified in the message experienced a PCIe training error and is operating at less than full bandwidth. Until this issue is resolved, a reduction in the storage performance is expected.
records.recommended_action:
Perform a Powercycle operation on the Chassis. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist
collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/
contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: arg1 firmware does not match the firmware of its peer controller.
records.explanation: The firmware running on the controller identified in the message does not match the firmware version of its peer controller. This can cause issues in a fault tolerant setup.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure each controller is using the same firmware by updating the firmware of the identified
controller.

messages: Bad block extended medium error on arg1.
records.explanation: A portion of a physical disk is damaged. See Receive a "Bad Block" Alert with "Replacement," "Sense," or "Medium" Error for more information.
records.recommended_action:
See Receive a "Bad Block" Alert with "Replacement," "Sense," or "Medium" Error for more
information.

messages: arg1 is unable to communicate with its peer.

records.cause: The controller identified in the message is unable to communicate with its peer. This can be because of a cabling issue.
records.recommended_action:
Check the cabling between the PERC cards and the expanders. If the issue persists, Collect a
SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: Export failed: Insufficient disk space available on the network share. Free up space and retry.
records.explanation: Unable to complete the export operation because the target network share does not have the required free disk space to accommodate the exported data. Ensure sufficient storage is available before retrying the operation.
records.cause: Unable to complete the export operation because the target network share does not have the required free disk space to accommodate the exported data. Ensure sufficient storage is available before retrying the operation.
records.recommended_action:
Ensure adequate free space is available on the destination network share by deleting unnecessary files
or expanding the storage allocation, then rerun the export operation.

messages: Unable to update the firmware because an exception occurred during the update process.
records.explanation: The firmware cannot be updated because an exception occurred during the update process.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure the device is available and retry the operation. If the issue persists, contact your system
administrator.

messages: Unable to retrieve rollback information because an exception occurred.
records.explanation: Firmware rollback information cannot be retrieved because an exception occurred.
records.recommended_action: Retry the operation. If the issue persists, contact your system administrator.

messages: Invalid release identifier provided, unable to create or update catalog for validated firmware solution baseline.
records.explanation: The request cannot be processed because the provided release identifier is invalid.
records.cause: The request cannot be processed because the provided release identifier is invalid.
records.recommended_action: Refer to RESTAPI guide to retrieve validated catalog versions and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to create catalog for validated firmware solution baseline as automatic or manual update is only applicable for latest release identifier arg1.
records.explanation: The request cannot be processed because the provided release identifier is invalid.
records.cause: The request cannot be processed because the provided release identifier is invalid.
records.recommended_action:
Use the latest release identifier that supports automatic or manual updates and retry the operation.
The latest release identifier can be availed by calling get validated catalog version API.

messages: Backup option is only applicable for latest release identifier of validated firmware solution baseline.
records.explanation: The request cannot be processed because the provided release identifier is invalid.
records.cause: The request cannot be processed because the provided release identifier is invalid.
records.recommended_action: Usethe latest release identifier by calling get validated catalog version API and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to retrieve the latest version for the console update.
records.explanation: The console update discovery process was unable to complete. The service failed to check for available updates, download the update bundle, or stage it for installation. Common root causes include network connectivity problems to the update source, proxy misconfiguration, insufficient disk space on the appliance, or an unreachable update repository.
records.cause: The console update discovery process was unable to complete. The service failed to check for available updates, download the update bundle, or stage it for installation. Common root causes include network connectivity problems to the update source, proxy misconfiguration, insufficient disk space on the appliance, or an unreachable update repository.
records.recommended_action:
1)Verify network connectivity between the appliance and the configured update source.2.If a proxy is
configured, validate proxy settings and ensure the update source URL is reachable through it.3.Check
available disk space on the appliance and free up storage if necessary.4.Review the console-update-
manager-service logs for the specific failure reason.5.Retry the Console Update Task.

messages: Pre-upgrade health audit failed. Upgrade cannot proceed.
records.explanation: Console update detects that the appliance is not healthy enough to proceed. The audit checks disk space, CPU and memory.
records.recommended_action:
1) Review the health audit details in the console update logs for the specific failing check.2. Disk
space: Free up space on the appliance or add more disk space.3. CPU/Memory: Wait for high-load
operations to complete, or increase resources if virtualized.4. Retry the upgrade after resolving the
health issue.

messages: A Downstream Port Containment event was detected on the CXL device at PCIE segment arg1, slot arg2.
records.explanation: An error has triggered a Downstream Port Containment event on the CXL device at the location identified in the message. The operating system is automatically notified about this to make an attempt to recover from the issue.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Make sure the device, BIOS, and iDRAC are updated to the latest firmware.
2) Perform an AC power-cycle operation on the server by doing the following: a) Disconnect the

on the support site. Do the following: 1) If the installed device is supported and if the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Historical metadata database pruning failed.
records.explanation: Pruning ensures the historical databasedoes not consume more than its allocated disk space.
records.recommended_action:
Contact your contracted support provider or visit us online at https://www.dell.com/supportto help
debug the problem.

messages: Historical metadata database space usage has exceeded the limited threshold.
records.explanation: Historical metadata database has consumed more than the allocated disk space.
records.recommended_action:
If the problem persists, contact your contracted support provider or visit us online at https://
www.dell.com/support.

messages: CPU arg1 : arg2 exception occurred.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action: Issue is on system board. Recommend flash the latest BIOS and retry the diagnostics.

messages: CPU arg1 - Machine check exception detected.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action: Issue is on system board. Recommend flash the latest BIOS and retry the diagnostics.

messages: Unable to start application processor(s). :OR: CPU arg1 (ID 0xarg2) did not reach test step arg3.:OR: CPU arg4 (ID 0xarg5) recorded unknown test result 0xarg6.:OR: CPU arg7 (ID 0xarg8) data error at address 0xarg9. Expected arg10.
records.explanation: Depends on <Error Reason>. If it is "Unable to start" it usually indicates a software problem. "Cache integrity" could signal a processor cache hardware problem. The other CPU messages could result from hardware or from overheating, if for instance, the fans are marginal or airflow is blocked.
records.recommended_action:
Check temperatures in System Health tab for abnormally high temperatures and make sure airflow
baffles are properly installed in the system, if any. Check fan RPM in System Health tab and verify
actual fans are properly installed.

messages: CPU Stress Thermal condition. Limit arg1C, Actual arg2C.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action: Check fans. Check for obstructed air vents. Check for excessive amounts of dust.

messages: UEFI: Memory error detected. :OR: LEGACY: Memory - integrity test discrepancy.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action:
MemRX not enabled or not supported. Servers UEFI: Power down system and re-seat DIMMS. Retry
test and if no error occurs it was a DIMM connection issue. Client LEGACY: Power down system and
re-seat DIMMS. Retry test and if no error occurs it was a DIMM connection issue. Check for latest
BIOS.

messages: Battery - The battery is reaching the end of its usable life.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action: Replace the battery.

messages: Battery - The battery cannot provide sufficient power.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action: Check battery contacts, plugs and cables. May need to replace battery.

messages: Battery - Charge cycles exceeded maximum limit. :OR: Charger - Charge cycles exceeded maximum limit.
records.explanation: Message "Charger -" changed to "Battery -" in 2/8/2016.
records.recommended_action:
Battery health data indicates the maximum number of charge cycles has been reached. Replace the
battery.

messages: Battery - Not a Dell battery. System will not charge this battery.
records.explanation: Thisis a new battery error code that was added when the detection of non-Dellbatteries was added to ePSA.
records.recommended_action: Replace battery with a Dell branded battery.

messages: Hard Drive arg1 - S/N arg2, arg3 self test unsuccessful arg4.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action:
If <Error Reason> is "terminated" then the disk controller terminated the test so a retry of the test
is advisable. Otherwise the hard drive should be replaced. {In the factory, this test type may also be
DEFT, in addition to DST Short and DST Long. The "terminated" case should not occur in the field,
only in development due to software issues}.

messages: Hard Drive arg1 - S/N arg2, self test did not complete.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action:
Desktops and Servers: Power down the system and check the signal and power connections to the
hard drive. Rerun the diagnostic. If no error occurs then it was a cable or connector issue.

messages: Optical Drive arg1 - Self test: arg2.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action:
This typically is a user error since these drives can be disconnected from the system. If disconnected,
reconnect the optical drive to system board. Check BIOS setup to make sure the SATA port the drive
is connected and has not been disabled. Rerun the diagnostic. If errors persist the optical drive is
defective.

messages: Hard Drive arg1 - S/N arg2, incorrect status = arg3\narg4.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action:
SMART Predictive Failure indicates the hard drive has failed SMART and maybe nearing the end
of its life. Other types of <Error Reason> in this category may indicate an intermittent or firmware
problem, rerun the test again. Desktops, servers: Check the hard disk drive cables and connections.
All systems: If error persists, make sure that hard disk drive firmware and BIOS are current. The
<80000000000000??> value is an EFI error code returned by the driver.

messages: Optical Drive arg1 - Incorrect status = arg2 arg3.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action:
Check the drive cables and connections. If error persists, make sure that drive firmware and BIOS are
current. The <80000000000000??> value is an EFI error code returned by the driver.

messages: Tape Drive arg1 - S/N arg2, incorrect status = arg3\narg4.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action:
Check installation of the tape drive, cables and connections. If the error persists, ensure that drive
firmware is current.

messages: Hard Drive - Not installed.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action:
Power down system and check the signal and power connections to the hard drive. Rerun the
diagnostic. If no error occurs then it was a cable or connector issue. This error is issued for notebooks
which must have a hard disk so it is an error if not found.

messages: The NVMe drive is not detected on the PCI tag arg1, NameSpace ID arg2.
records.explanation: The NVMe drive is not detected on the PCI tag identified in the message. An NVMe drive may be installed but is not working to expose the NVMe pass-through protocol interface.
records.recommended_action: Replace the NVMe drive.

messages: System board - CMOS battery failure detected.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the CMOS battery and retry the diagnostic. If the error persists, make sure the BIOS is
current and retry the diagnostics.

messages: System board - Interval timer not functional.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action: Make sure the BIOS is current and retry the diagnostics.

messages: System board - RTC seconds count is not updating.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action: Make sure the BIOS is current and retry the diagnostics.

messages: System board - Interrupt controller, IRQ = arg1: arg2 not detected.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action: Make sure the BIOS is current and retry the diagnostics.

messages: System board - Data errors.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action:
This is an error message for multiple DIMM failures. Replace the memory one module at a time and
re-run the diagnostics. If issue persists, replace the motherboard.

messages: LCD panel - Unable to use BIOS interface.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action: Make sure that the BIOS is current and retry diagnostics.

messages: Fan - The (arg1) fan failed to respond correctly.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action:
The fan may be faulty, check for obstructions to the fan and vents. Make sure that BIOS is current
and retry the diagnostics.

messages: Fan - The (arg1) fan is running faster than expected.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the diagnostics; if the problem persists, the fan is faulty. Make sure that the BIOS is current and
retry the diagnostics.

messages: Network arg1 - arg2.
records.explanation: UEFI Driver provides a DIAGNOSTIC protocol and this protocol supplies a test that failed. Failure Message may be "Packet loopback test failed" or "Register test failed" or something else. Provided by driver not ePSA.
records.recommended_action:
The Network (Ethernet) device may be faulty. Check for bent pins in the Ethernet connector. Make
sure that Network device firmware is current. Retry test, if still fails, replace the NIC/NDC/LOM
Network device. This may be on the motherboard, or an adapter, or a daughter card, depending on the
system.

messages: Network arg1 - Driver version arg2 outdated. Version arg3 or newer required for "arg4".
records.explanation: Test only warns because UEFI Network Driver is old and has known false failures.
records.cause: Test only warns because UEFI Network Driver is old and has known false failures.
records.recommended_action: Update Network firmware.

messages: Thermal - Thermal trip detected.
records.explanation: BIOS error reported through ePSA.
records.cause: System detected repeated thermal trips due to excessive heat.
records.recommended_action:
System detected repeated thermal trips due to excessive heat. Check for obstructions to the fan and
vents. Make sure BIOS is current and rerun diagnostics. If error persists replace thermal heat sink,
CPU and motherboard.

messages: Fan - The fan failed to respond correctly.
records.explanation: BIOS error reported through ePSA.
records.recommended_action:
BIOS detected repeated issues when setting the fan speed. The fan may be faulty, check for
obstructions to the fan and vents. Make sure the BIOS is current and rerun diagnostics.

messages: Sensor - Error accessing thermal sensor.
records.explanation: BIOS error reported through ePSA.
records.recommended_action:
BIOS error when reading the systems thermal sensor. Make sure the BIOS is current and rerun
diagnostics. If error persists, replace the motherboard.

messages: Heat Sink - Heat sink clip not installed.
records.explanation: BIOS error reported through ePSA.
records.recommended_action: BIOS detected that the heat sink clip was not installed. Connect the heat sink clip properly.

messages: Cables - Check the following cable, arg1.
records.explanation: BIOS error reported through ePSA.
records.recommended_action:
BIOS detected a cable that was not installed. Connect the cable that is described in the string portion
of the message.

messages: Memory - Previous uncorrectable memory error.
records.explanation: BIOS error reported through ePSA.
records.recommended_action:
BIOS detected an un-correctable memory issue on a prior boot. Update to the latest BIOS. Power
down system and reseat DIMMs. Retry test; if no error occurs it was a DIMM connection issue. If error
persists, replace the DIMM.

messages: Hard Drive - Drive error detected.
records.explanation: BIOS error reported through ePSA.
records.recommended_action:
BIOS detected a hard drive issue. Make sure hard drive connection is good, and the drive firmware
and system BIOS are current. If error persists, replace the hard drive.

messages: Fan - Unable to set Manufacturing Mode.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action: Make sure that BIOS is current and rerun the diagnostics.

messages: SMBIOS DIMM configuration did not match.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action: Software error, should not normally occur in field.

messages: Charger - The AC power adapter wattage and type cannot be determined. The battery may not charge.
records.explanation: Added 01/18/2016 to ePSA code.
records.recommended_action: A bad charger or a non-Dell charger is being used on the system.Replace the charger.

messages: Tape Drive arg1 - S/N arg2, data read does not match data written.
records.explanation: Data written on the tape read back differently, not as expected.
records.recommended_action: Use a different tape media.

messages: arg1 Drive arg2 - S/N arg3, incorrect status = arg4\narg5.
records.explanation: A device failed a command and testing cannot complete.
records.recommended_action: Retry test. If failure persists and BIOS is up to date, a hardware problem is indicated.

messages: PERC Battery arg1 - incorrect status = arg2\narg3.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action:
If <Error Reason> is (Battery missing or disconnected) then check the battery cable to the PERC
controller. If <Error Reason> is (Replace battery pack) then replace battery pack. If <Error Reason> is
(Remaining capacity low) then battery pack may need to be replaced soon.

messages: PCIe - Training error PCI Tag-arg1 VendorID-arg2 DeviceID-arg3SVid-arg4SDid-arg5 Bus arg6: Link Degraded, maxLinkWidth = xarg7, negotiatedLinkWidth = xarg8, Slot arg9.
records.explanation: A PCI device is functioning at a lower performance that it should be. If the device is in a physical PCI slot then ", Slot <decimal>" will be appended to the message.
records.recommended_action: Reseat the PCI-Express adapter described and retest.

messages: PCIe - PCI device at PCI tag arg1 is intermittently discoverable.
records.explanation: A PCI Device is not always functioning properly. Sometimes is not discoverable when scanning for PCI devices.
records.recommended_action: Reseat the PCI-Express Adapter described and retest.

messages: Cables - BIOS reports no testable cable/jumper/connector/sensor.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action: Update the BIOS to the latest version.

messages: The operating system of arg1 is not ready for normal function because either the boot synchronization period has timed out or the boot synchronization timeout value is too less.
records.explanation: The operating system of the DPU identified in the message is not ready for normal function because either the boot synchronization period has timed out or the boot synchronization timeout value is too less.
records.cause: The operating system of the DPU identified in the message is not ready for normal function because either the boot synchronization period has timed out or the boot synchronization timeout value is too less.
records.recommended_action:
Increase the DPUOSReadyTimeout value based on your DPU configuration. If the issue persists,
reinstall the DPU operating system and power on the server.

messages: The shutdown operation of the OS of the respective DUPs cannot be completed.
records.explanation: Unable to shut down the OS of the respective Data Processing Units (DPUs) because the DPU shutdown timeout value is less.
records.cause: Unable to shut down the OS of the respective Data Processing Units (DPUs) because the DPU shutdown timeout value is less.
records.recommended_action:
1) Run the following RACADM command at the CLI to get the DPU shutdown timeout
value: racadm get system.dpuGlobalConfiguration.DPUOSShutdownTimeOut.2) Run the following
RACADM command at the CLI to increase the DPU shutdown timeout value: racadm set
system.dpuGlobalConfiguration.DPUOSShutdownTimeOut <enter new value>.3) Retry the Graceful
Shutdown operation of the host device. If the issue persists, reinstall the DPU operating system.

messages: The Embedded Controller (EC) has detected that the arg1 cooling fan is not installed.
records.explanation: The Embedded Controller (EC) has detected that the cooling fan identified in the message is not installed or missing. Operating the system without all required fans installed may impact cooling performance and cause the system to throttle.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Ensure that the cooling fan identified in the message is physically present and the
fan cable connector is securely seated. 2) If the cooling fan is missing, install a compatible cooling fan.
For information about supported cooling fan specification and procedure to install the cooling fan, see
the Installation and Service Manual (ISM) of the respective PowerEdge server available on the support
site. 2) If the issue persists, collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using RMC. Visithttps://
www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamicto use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the
collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: The Embedded Controller (EC) has detected a critical failure of the arg1 cooling fan.
records.explanation: The Embedded Controller (EC) has detected a failure for the cooling fan identified in the message. The fan may have stopped spinning or is operating below the minimum required speed. This condition will severely impact system cooling and may lead to a thermal shutdown to protect components.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Power off the system and disconnect the power cord. 2) Open the chassis
cover and check for any cables, dust, or physical obstructions blocking the specified cooling fan
blades. 3) Reseat the cooling fan to ensure a secure connection to the system board. 4) Power
on the system. 5) If the issue persists, collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using RMC.
Visithttps://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamicto use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: arg1 is sending inconsistent responses to the controller.
records.explanation: The storage controller is not receiving a consistent response from the enclosure due to a firmware problem or an incorrect cabling configuration. If the cables are longer than the specified maximum length, the signals may be degraded.
records.cause: The storage controller is not receiving a consistent response from the enclosure due to a firmware problem or an incorrect cabling configuration. If the cables are longer than the specified maximum length, the signals may be degraded.
records.recommended_action:
Turn off all the enclosures attached to the system, check if the cable configurations are correct and
reboot the system. If the problem persists, update the enclosure firmware to the latest supported
version. Download the latest supported version of the firmware from the service provider. For more
information about cable configuration, see storage enclosure documentation.

messages: Unsupported configuration detected on arg1. arg2 arg3
records.explanation: An unsupported configuration was detected. The SCSI rate of the Enclosure Management Modules (EMMs) are not the same.
records.recommended_action: Replace one of the EMMs with the matching SCSI rate EMM.

messages: Communication with arg1 was lost.
records.explanation: The controller has lost communication with an Enclosure Management Module (EMM). The cables may be loose or defective.
records.cause: The controller has lost communication with an Enclosure Management Module (EMM). The cables may be loose or defective.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure the cables are attached securely. See the storage hardware documentation for more
information on checking the cables. Reboot the system.

messages: arg1 has failed.
records.explanation: An Enclosure Management Module (EMM) has failed. The failure may be caused by a loss of power to the EMM. The EMM self-test may also have identified a failure. There may also be a firmware problem or a multi-bit error.
records.cause: An Enclosure Management Module (EMM) has failed. The failure may be caused by a loss of power to the EMM. The EMM self-test may also have identified a failure. There may also be a firmware problem or a multi-bit error.
records.recommended_action:
Reset the Enclosure Management Module (EMM). See the storage hardware documentation
for information on replacing the EMM. Replace the EMM. If the issue persists, Collect a
SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: Communication with arg1 is intermittent.
records.explanation: The controller is not receiving a consistent response from the enclosure. There could be a firmware problem or an invalid cabling configuration. If the cables are too long, they degrade the signal.
records.recommended_action:
Power down all enclosures attached to the system and reboot . If the problem persists, upgrade
the firmware to the latest supported version. Verify the cable configuration is valid. See the storage
hardware documentation for valid cabling configurations.

messages: arg1 has a hardware error.
records.explanation: The enclosure or an enclosure component is in a Failed or Degraded state.
records.recommended_action:
Verify the health of the enclosure and its components. See the storage hardware documentation for
more information. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
