records.explanation: The external shared adapter cannot be turned on until the Chassis Infrastructure firmware is updated to the latest version supporting the shared adapter.
records.cause: Unable to map/un-map or turn on the external shared adapter because the firmware version of Chassis Management Controller (CMC) Chassis Infrastructure Mainboard is not the latest version supporting the adapter.
records.recommended_action:
Remove the adapter or update the Chassis Infrastructure firmware and then retry the operation. Using
the Chassis Management Controller (CMC) RACADM, run the command "racadm fwupdate -g -u -a
<TFTP server IP Address> -d mainboard.bin -m main_board" to upload the latest firmware version to
the Chassis Infrastructure Mainboard.

messages: Unable to assign a PCIe slot.
records.explanation: The IOV slot management subsystem detected an error which may prevent the physical assignment/ unassignment or turning off of a PCIe slot. The errors can be caused by PCIe training timeouts, false hot plug signals,or installation of an unsupported PCIe adapter card. For a list of supported PCIe adapter cards contact your service provider.
records.cause: The IOV slot management subsystem detected an error which may prevent the physical assignment/ unassignment or turning off of a PCIe slot. The errors can be caused by PCIe training timeouts, false hot plug signals,or installation of an unsupported PCIe adapter card. For a list of supported PCIe adapter cards contact your service provider.
records.recommended_action:
Insert only supported adapter cards into system PCIe slots and make sure they are fully inserted.
Retry the operation.

messages: The Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to allocate arg1 Watt for server-arg2 PCIe adapters.
records.explanation: For each adapter assigned to a server, power is allocated when the server is turned on. If the available power is less than the required power, the Chassis Management Controller (CMC) will not power on the adapters associated with the server.
records.recommended_action:
Using the Chassis Management Controller (CMC) RACADM command line interface, run the command
"racadm config -g cfgChassisPower -o cfgChassisPowerCap <Power cap>" to increase the power cap
or add an additional power supply.

messages: Unable to manage PCIE adapter arg1 located in arg2 arg3.
records.explanation: An error by the Chassis Infrastructure slot management detected an error which may prevent the physical assignment/unassignment or power off of a slot. The errors may be caused by PCIE training timeouts, false hot plug signals, or installation of an unsupported PCIe adapter card. For a list of supported PCIe adapter cards contact your service provider.
records.cause: An error by the Chassis Infrastructure slot management detected an error which may prevent the physical assignment/unassignment or power off of a slot. The errors may be caused by PCIE training timeouts, false hot plug signals, or installation of an unsupported PCIe adapter card. For a list of supported PCIe adapter cards contact your service provider.
records.recommended_action: Make sure that supported adapters are used and installed correctly in the PCIe slot.

messages: Unable to power on PCIe adapter arg1 in arg2 arg3.
records.explanation: The Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to power on adapter. Possible reasons for power failures are: 1) Adapter not an approved adapter. 2) Adapter not fully inserted in the slot 3) Auxiliary power cable not connected (applicable to slot 1 - 3 only). 4) Adapter is damaged.
records.cause: The Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to power on adapter. Possible reasons for power failures are: 1) Adapter not an approved adapter. 2) Adapter not fully inserted in the slot 3) Auxiliary power cable not connected (applicable to slot 1 - 3 only). 4) Adapter is damaged.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure a supported PCIe device is used and that it is properly inserted in the PCIe slot. For a list of
supported devices, If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: PCIe adapter arg1 in slot arg2 was removed while powered on.
records.explanation: The Chassis Management Controller (CMC) has detected the removal of a PCIe adapter card while it was powered on.
records.recommended_action:
Power down the affected server(s) and then power on the server(s). Note: OS reboot only will not
correct this issue.

messages: Unable to update Chassis Infrastructure firmware.
records.explanation: Unable to successfully update Chassis Infrastructure firmware.
records.recommended_action:
Refer to the release notes of the Mainboard update package for recommended action. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Chassis Infrastructure firmware is not valid.
records.explanation: Chassis infrastructure firmware is not valid and must be reinstalled.
records.recommended_action:
Update the Chassis Infrastructure firmware. Using Chassis Management Controller (CMC) RACADM,
run the command "racadm fwupdate -g -u -a <TFTP server IP Address> -d mainboard.bin -m
main_board" to upload the latest firmware version to the Chassis Infrastructure Mainboard.

messages: PCIE AUX power cable arg1.was disconnected while powered on.
records.explanation: The Chassis Management Controller (CMC) detected a power fault in an PCIE AUX power cable after the adapter was powered on. A power fault may be caused by a loose cable connection to the adapter or between the cable and the AUX cable harness.
records.cause: The Chassis Management Controller (CMC) detected a power fault in an PCIE AUX power cable after the adapter was powered on. A power fault may be caused by a loose cable connection to the adapter or between the cable and the AUX cable harness.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure AUX power cable identified in the message is fully plugged into the adapter and the AUX
cable harness.

messages: Fabric arg1 is down.
records.explanation: The Fabric identified in the message is not up and a chassis power cycle is required.
records.recommended_action:
Power cycle the chassis. Using the Chassis Management Controller (CMC) RACADM command line
interface, run the command "racadm chassisaction powercycle".

messages: The PCIe shared adapter in slot arg1 is not supported because the firmware version of the Chassis Infrastructure Mainboard is not the latest.
records.explanation: The PCIe shared adapter in slot identified in the message is not supported because the firmware version of Chassis Management Controller (CMC) Chassis Infrastructure Mainboard is not the latest.
records.cause: The PCIe shared adapter in slot identified in the message is not supported because the firmware version of Chassis Management Controller (CMC) Chassis Infrastructure Mainboard is not the latest.
records.recommended_action:
Remove the adapter or update the Chassis Infrastructure firmware and then retry the operation.
Using Chassis Management Controller (CMC) RACADM, run the command "racadm fwupdate -g -u -a
<TFTP server IP Address> -d mainboard.bin -m main_board" to upload the latest firmware version to
the Chassis Infrastructure Mainboard.

messages: The Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to communicate with the PCIe subsystem.
records.explanation: The Chassis Management Controller (CMC) could not successfully connect to the PCIe subsystem.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Perform an AC Power Cycle operation on the Chassis by disconnecting the
chassis from AC power, wait for 30 seconds, and then reconnect AC power. 2) Turn on at
least one server. Using the Chassis Management Controller (CMC) web interface, select Server
Overview->Power->Control and select the Power On Server option. If the issue persists, Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: The iDRAC Service Module detected a OS to iDRAC Pass-through in the arg1 mode. Switch the OS to iDRAC Pass-through to a USB NIC mode.
records.explanation: The iDRAC Service Module detected a OS to iDRAC Pass-through mode as identified in the message. iDRAC Service Module will automatically connect to iDRAC after the OS to iDRAC Pass-through is configured to the USB NIC mode.
records.recommended_action:
Configure OS to iDRAC Pass-through to the USB NIC mode by running the commands: 1) racadm set
idrac.os-bmc.PTMode usb-p2p 2) racadm set idrac.os-bmc.UsbNicIpAddress <ip address> 3) racadm
set idrac.os-bmc.adminstate enabled.

messages: The iDRAC Service Module is unable to communicate with iDRAC using the OS to iDRAC Pass-through channel.
records.explanation: The iDRAC Service Module could not successfully communicate with iDRAC, because the OS to iDRAC Pass-through channel is not configured in the USB-NIC mode.
records.cause: The iDRAC Service Module could not successfully communicate with iDRAC, because the OS to iDRAC Pass-through channel is not configured in the USB-NIC mode.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the OS to iDRAC Pass-through channel is configured only in the USB-NIC mode,
and then retry the operation. To enable the OS-to-iDRAC Pass-through channel, run the following
command in the order they are listed: 1) racadm set idrac.os-bmc.PTMode usb-p2p 2) racadm set
idrac.os-bmc.UsbNicIpAddress <ip address> 3) racadm set idrac.os-bmc.adminstate enabled.

messages: Unable to prepare the NVMe device arg1 for removal from the PCIe slot arg2 because of one or more of the following reasons: 1) NVMe device is busy, 2) NVMe device is not present or 3) NVMe driver is not installed.
records.explanation: The NVMe device cannot be prepared for removal from (the PCIe slot identified in the message because of one or more of the following reasons: 1) NVMe device is busy, 2) NVMe device is not present or 3) NVMe driver is not present.
records.cause: The NVMe device cannot be prepared for removal from (the PCIe slot identified in the message because of one or more of the following reasons: 1) NVMe device is busy, 2) NVMe device is not present or 3) NVMe driver is not present.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure of the following: 1) That the NVMe device identified in the message is not in use, 2) the
NVMe device is present, and 3) NVMe device drive is installed.

messages: Unable to perform the iDRAC Hard Reset operation either because of an unsupported CPLD firmware version or the iDRAC Hard Reset feature is currently disabled on iDRAC.
records.explanation: The iDRAC Hard Reset operation cannot be performed either because of an unsupported CPLD firmware version or the iDRAC Hard reset feature is currently disabled on iDRAC.
records.cause: The iDRAC Hard Reset operation cannot be performed either because of an unsupported CPLD firmware version or the iDRAC Hard reset feature is currently disabled on iDRAC.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Update the CPLD version by using iDRAC graphical user interface (GUI).
2) To enable the iDRAC Hard Reset feature by running RACADM command, enter the following at the
command line interface (CLI): "racadm set idrac.servicemodule.idrachardreset enabled".

messages: iDRAC is unable to communicate with the iDRAC Service Module (iSM) because the iSM being installed on the host Operating System (OS) is not compatible with current iDRAC firmware version.
records.explanation: iDRAC is unable to communicate with the iDRAC Service Module (iSM) because the iSM being installed on the host Operating System (OS) is not compatible with current iDRAC firmware version.
records.cause: iDRAC is unable to communicate with the iDRAC Service Module (iSM) because the iSM being installed on the host Operating System (OS) is not compatible with current iDRAC firmware version.
records.recommended_action:
Reinstall the latest available iDRAC Service Module (iSM) on the host Operating System (OS) and
retry the operation. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: The operation failed due to an internal iDRAC error.
records.explanation: The requested operation requires memory or file space allocation. The operation failed due to lack of memory or file space in the iDRAC.
records.cause: The requested operation requires memory or file space allocation. The operation failed due to lack of memory or file space in the iDRAC.
records.recommended_action: Retry the operation. If the issue persists, reset iDRAC and retry the operation.

messages: The operation failed due to an internal iDRAC error.
records.explanation: The operation did not complete successfully because of lack of an unknown error in the iDRAC.
records.recommended_action: Retry the operation. If the issue persists, reset the iDRAC.

messages: Failed to change the firmware update mode.
records.explanation: An error occurred while trying to set the firmware update mode.
records.recommended_action:
Verify that the firmware version supports this mode. Also confirm that the command and parameters
are correct. The parameter choices are: 1) Disable (default) 2) Allow version upgrade only 3) Match
firmware of replaced part.

messages: Invalid firmware update mode.
records.explanation: The value provided for the update mode parameter is invalid.
records.recommended_action:
Verify that the correct firmware update mode was entered. The choices are: 1) Disable (default) 2)
Allow version upgrade only 3) Match firmware of replaced part.

messages: Unable to retrieve Lifecycle Controller Log records.
records.explanation: Unable to retrieve Lifecycle Controller Log records because of an issue internal to the firmware.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Try the operation again 2) AC power cycle the system 3) apply the latest
firmware update packages for Lifecycle Controller and iDRAC.

messages: An instance of Lifecycle Controller system configuration wipe is already running.
records.explanation: The Lifecycle Controller system configuration wipe operation is currently running. The operation deletes user information from system hardware and resets BIOS, iDRAC and Lifecycle Controller to default settings. The current operation and system restart must complete before the operation can be attempted again.
records.recommended_action:
Wait for the Lifecycle Controller system configuration wipe operation that is currently running to
complete before requesting another operation.

messages: Unable to generate an SSL Certificate because of internal firmware issues.
records.explanation: An SSL Certificate cannot be generated because of internal firmware issues.
records.recommended_action:
Ensure the security attributes are correct and retry the operation. If the issue persists, reboot iDRAC
using one of the following methods and then retry the operation:1) On the Redfish Interface: Invoking
the iDRACReset action in DelliDRACCardService.2) On the iDRAC User Interface: Click Dashboard
> Reboot iDRAC.For information about validating these attributes, see the iDRAC Users Guide and
Redfish API Guide available on the support site.

messages: A leak is detected on arg1 arg2.
records.explanation: A leak has been detected on the system. There is an issue with the liquid cooling system.
records.recommended_action: Remove system input power and disconnect server liquid hoses from the rack manifold.

messages: A leak is detected on arg1 arg2.
records.explanation: A leak has been detected on the system. There is an issue with the liquid cooling system.
records.recommended_action: Remove system input power and disconnect server liquid hoses from the rack manifold.

messages: An error is detected in the leak detection sensor of the arg1.
records.explanation: An error is detected in the leak detection sensor of the device identified in the message. There is no functional leak detection.
records.recommended_action:
If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://
www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze
the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: A leak is detected on arg1 arg2.
records.explanation: A leak has been detected on the system. There is an issue with the liquid cooling system.
records.recommended_action: Remove system input power and disconnect server liquid hoses from the rack manifold.

messages: The health of the Liquid Cooling pump arg1 is critical.
records.explanation: The Liquid cooling pump is not performing optimally. The liquid pipe maybe installed improperly or there is a leak in the liquid pipe.
records.recommended_action:
If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://
www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze
the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: An error is detected in the leak detection sensor of the arg1.
records.explanation: An error is detected in the leak detection sensor of the device identified in the message. There is no functional leak detection.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Locate the rack. 2) Locate the sensor identified in the message. 3) Inspect the
sensor as described in the Installation and Service Manual (ISM) of the Integrated Rack model on the
support site.

messages: The arg1 leak detection sensor is disconnected.
records.explanation: The leak detection sensor identified in the message is disconnected.
records.recommended_action:
If leak sensor disconnection is not expected, locate the rack and inspect the specific sensor indicated
in the message. Ensure the cable is connected fully and properly. For more information see the
Installation and Service Manual (ISM) specific to the device model available on the support site.

messages: Resource allocation failure.
records.explanation: Unable to allocate the resource because of lack of memory or file space in the iDRAC.
records.cause: Unable to allocate the resource because of lack of memory or file space in the iDRAC.
records.recommended_action: Reset iDRAC and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to connect the server in slot arg1 to the IOM in slot arg2 port arg3, because the IOM port is down.
records.explanation: The server identified in the message could not be successfully connected to the external network, because the network connection is not functional.
records.cause: The server identified in the message could not be successfully connected to the external network, because the network connection is not functional.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following, and then retry the operation: 1) Check whether or not the external network
cable is functioning. 2) Reinstall or replace network cable of the IOM and port identified in the
message.

messages: Resource allocation failure.
records.explanation: The operation did not complete successfully because of lack of memory or file space in iDRAC firmware.
records.cause: The operation did not complete successfully because of lack of memory or file space in iDRAC firmware.
records.recommended_action: Reset iDRAC and retry the operation.

messages: Multi-bit memory errors are detected on the memory device at location(s) arg1. Immediately replace the DIMM.
records.explanation: The memory has an uncorrectable error. System performance may be degraded and the operating system and/or applications may fail as a result of this.
records.recommended_action: Immediately replace the DIMM.

messages: A hardware fault was detected with an NVRAM card and it may need to be replaced.
records.explanation: One or more issues or faults were detected with an NVRAM card and the card may need to be replaced.
records.recommended_action: Contact your service provider / tech support to resolve the issue.

messages: The memory health monitor feature has detected a degradation in the DIMM installed in arg1. Reboot system to initiate self-heal process.
records.explanation: The memory health monitor feature has detected a degradation in the DIMM installed in the slot identified in the message. Reboot system to initiate self-heal process.
records.recommended_action:
The system memory health must be improved by initiating the self-heal process. To start the process,
restart the system.

messages: Memory RAID redundancy is lost. Check memory device at location(s) arg1.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action:
Re-install the memory component. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR)
report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use
the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Memory RAID redundancy is degraded. Check memory device at location(s) arg1.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action:
Re-install the memory component. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR)
report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use
the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Memory device status is unknown. Memory device location: arg1, Possible memory module event cause: arg2.
records.explanation: The memory module may not be correctly seated, wrongly configured, or has failed.
records.recommended_action:
Review the Embedded System Management (ESM) Log for memory exceptions. Re-install the memory
modules at the identified location .

messages: Memory device status is non-critical. Memory device location: arg1, Possible memory module event cause: arg2.
records.explanation: The memory module may not be correctly seated, wrongly configured, or has failed.
records.recommended_action:
Review the Embedded System Management (ESM) Log for memory exceptions. Re-install the memory
modules at the identified location .

messages: Memory device status is critical. Memory device location: arg1, Possible memory module event cause: arg2.
records.explanation: The memory module may not be correctly seated, wrongly configured, or has failed.
records.recommended_action:
Review the Embedded System Management (ESM) Log for memory exceptions. Re-install the memory
modules at the identified location .

messages: Memory device has failed. Memory device location: arg1, Possible memory module event cause: arg2.
records.explanation: The memory module failed because of an irrecoverable error.
records.recommended_action:
Review the Embedded System Management (ESM) Log for memory exceptions. Remove the old
memory module and install a new memory module at the identified location .

messages: A diagnostic warning event occurred in the memory device at arg1. Update device firmware. (Extended ID: arg2).
records.explanation: A diagnostic warning event occurred in the memory device at location identified in the message. Update the firmware for the memory device to enable new features or address known issues.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: An unknown diagnostic warning event occurred in the memory device at arg1. (Extended ID: arg2).
records.explanation: An unknown diagnostic warning event occurred in the memory device at location identified in the message. iDRAC firmware must be updated to properly decode this event.
records.recommended_action:
Update iDRAC firmware to the latest version available. If the issue persists, Collect a
SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: A hardware mismatch detected for memory riser.
records.explanation: No detailed description available.
records.recommended_action: Review product documentation for proper memory riser installation and configuration.

messages: A critical diagnostic event occurred in the memory device at arg1. Update device firmware. (Extended ID: arg2).
records.explanation: A critical diagnostic event occurred in the memory device at location identified in the message. Update the firmware for the memory device to enable new features or address known issues.
records.recommended_action:
Update the memory device firmware to enable new features and resolve any known issues. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Correctable memory error logging disabled for a memory device at location arg1.
records.explanation: Errors are being corrected but predicitive failure algorith is unable to run at optimal conditions. please update BIOS to fix issue.
records.recommended_action: Please update to latest BIOS an update was added which aliviates this issue.

messages: Memory interconnect degraded.
records.explanation: An issue is detected in the propagation of signals between the processor and the memory.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Reseat the memory riser and restart the server. 2) If the issue is
not resolved by preceding action, reseat the processor and restart the server. 3) If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Intel QPI interconnect arg1 has a correctable error.
records.explanation: A correctable error was detected in propagation of signals between processors through the Intel QPI interconnect interconnect identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Restart the server and check whether the issue persists. 2) If the issue
is not resolved by the preceding action, reseat the processors and restart the server. 3) If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Intel QPI interconnect arg1 has degraded.
records.explanation: A link degradation was detected in propagation of signals between processors through the Intel QPI interconnect interconnect identified in the message. The system will continue to operate at reduced performance.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Restart the server and check whether the issue persists. 2) If the issue
is not resolved by the preceding action, reseat the processors and restart the server. 3) If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Intel SMI 2 Memory interconnect arg1 has degraded.
records.explanation: A link degradation was detected in propagation of signals between processor and memory through the Intel SMI 2 memory interconnect identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Reseat the memory riser and restart the server. 2) If the issue is
not resolved by preceding action, reseat the processor and restart the server. 3) If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Intel QPI interconnect arg1 has a non-recoverable issue.
records.explanation: A non-recoverable link issue was detected in propagation of signals between processors through the Intel QPI interconnect interconnect identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Restart the server and check whether the issue persists. 2) If the issue
is not resolved by the preceding action, reseat the processors and restart the server. 3) If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Intel SMI 2 Memory interconnect arg1 has a non-recoverable issue.
records.explanation: A non-recoverable link issue was detected in propagation of signals between processor and memory through the Intel SMI 2 memory interconnect identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Reseat the memory riser and restart the server. 2) If the issue is
not resolved by preceding action, reseat the processor and restart the server. 3) If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: A correctable memory error has occurred in Dual In-line Memory Module (DIMM) device arg1.
records.explanation: The memory device identified in the message has encountered a correctable memory error. This may be an early indicator of a possible future uncorrectable error.
records.recommended_action:
This is a correctable error. Review log information and if multiple correctable errors have occurred
on the DIMM identified in the message, re-install the memory device. If the issue persists, Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: Multi-bit memory errors detected on a Dual In-line Memory Module (DIMM) device arg1.
records.explanation: The memory device identified in the message has encountered a uncorrectable error. System performance may be degraded. The operating system and/or applications may fail as a result.
records.recommended_action:
Re-install the memory component identified in the message. If the issue persists, Collect a
SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: The Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device in the slot arg1 is about to reach the end of supported life duration.
records.explanation: The NVDIMM device in the slot, identified in the message, is about to reach the end of supported life duration.
records.recommended_action:
During the next scheduled maintenance, replace the Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module
(NVDIMM) device. For more information about the usage of NVDIMMs, see the system Owners
Manual on the support site.

messages: The Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) in slot arg1 is running the backup firmware image because the primary firmware has issues.
records.explanation: The NVDIMM in the slot identified in the message is running the backup firmware image because the primary firmware image has issues.
records.cause: The NVDIMM in the slot identified in the message is running the backup firmware image because the primary firmware image has issues.
records.recommended_action:
Update the Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module(NVDIMM) to the latest firmware. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: A Non-Critical event was detected on the Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device in the slot arg1.
records.explanation: The NVDIMM device identified in the message has encountered a Non-Critical event.
records.recommended_action:
If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://
www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze
the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: The Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device in the slot arg1 is not responding and is disabled.
records.explanation: The NVDIMM device in the slot identified in the message is not responding and is disabled.
records.recommended_action:
Remove and reinstall the Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: The Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device is of unsupported configuration and unable to operate as currently configured.
records.explanation: An NVDIMM device is of unsupported configuration and unable to operate as currently configured.
records.recommended_action:
Review the memory configuration and make sure the configuration is as per memory rules defined in
the system Owners Manual on the support site.

messages: The Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device in the slot arg1 is not responding.
records.explanation: The NVDIMM device in the slot identified in the message is not responding.
records.recommended_action:
Remove and reinstall the Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: The Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device in the slot arg1 cannot be configured to save data during a power loss because of an issue in the NVDIMM.
records.explanation: The NVDIMM device in the slot identified in the message cannot be configured to save data during a power loss because of an issue in the NVDIMM.
records.recommended_action:
Remove and reinstall the Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: The Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) devices are placed in write-protect mode because the system may not provide sufficient power to save data in case of power loss.
records.explanation: The NVDIMM devices are placed in write-protect mode because the server may not provide sufficient power or the battery is not sufficiently charged to save data in case of power loss.
records.cause: The NVDIMM devices are placed in write-protect mode because the server may not provide sufficient power or the battery is not sufficiently charged to save data in case of power loss.
records.recommended_action:
Review any preceding power or battery entries in the log and resolve the issues. Refer to your
documentation for details on how to view the log.

messages: The Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device in the slot arg1 has reached the end of supported life duration and is placed in write-protect mode.
records.explanation: The NVDIMM device in the slot identified in the message has reached the end of supported life duration and is placed in write-protect mode.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device. For information about
removing and reinstalling the NVDIMM, see the system Owners Manual on the support site.

messages: The Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device in the slot arg1 has lost persistency and is placed in write-protect mode.
records.explanation: The NVDIMM device in the slot identified in the message has lost persistency and is placed in write- protect mode.
records.recommended_action:
Remove and reinstall the Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: The Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device in the slot arg1 was unable to be initialized.
records.explanation: The NVDIMM device in the slot identified in the message was unable to clear its storage media as part of the initialization process and is disabled.
records.recommended_action:
Remove and reinstall the Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: A Critical event was detected on the Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device in the slot arg1.
records.explanation: The NVDIMM device in the slot identified in the message has encountered a critical error. System performance may be degraded. The operating system and/or applications may fail as a result.
records.recommended_action:
Remove and reinstall the Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to complete the erase operation on the non-volatile DIMM with serial number arg1 in slot arg2.
records.explanation: The erase operation could not be completed for the DIMM identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation. If the issue persists, contact your service provider. It is also recommended that
the system be upgraded to the latest BIOS.

messages: The system memory has detected an error on a memory transaction at the location arg1. Reboot the system for auto-healing.
records.explanation: The system has detected a memory error which cannot be immediately corrected.The OS has been notified of the memory error location.Recommended action is to warm reboot the system to initiate auto-healing and to reinitialize memory for optimized performance.
records.recommended_action:
Perform a warm reboot to allow server to attempt self-healing or self-correction. If a warm reboot
has already occurred subsequent to this message then no further action is required. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to update firmware on a Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device in the slot arg1.
records.explanation: Unable to update firmware for the NVDIMM identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation. If the issue not resolved, replace the NVDIMM, or If the issue persists,Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: The SmartFabric ID arg1 is invalid.
records.explanation: The SmartFabric identified in the message is invalid. The SmartFabric validation criteria such as design, fabric node inventory, I/O module placement requirements, and inter-node connectivity are inconsistent.
records.recommended_action:
For more information about the configuration, inventory, and placement requirements, see the
predefined System Architecture documentation available on the support site.

messages: Unable to complete the SmartFabric validation operation because the I/O Module information is not available.
records.explanation: The SmartFabric validation can not be completed because the I/O Module information is not available.
records.cause: The SmartFabric validation can not be completed because the I/O Module information is not available.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that all the I/O Modules are in the chassis, discovered in OpenManage Enterprise-Modular,
and healthy.

messages: The SmartFabric is not healthy because the I/O Module arg1 is not healthy.
records.explanation: The SmartFabric is not healthy because the I/O Module identified in the message is not healthy.
records.recommended_action: Fix the health of the I/O Module.

messages: The SmartFabric is not healthy because the I/O Module arg1 is offline or can not be communicated with.
records.explanation: The SmartFabric is not healthy because the I/O Module identified in the message is offline or cannot be communicated with.
records.cause: The SmartFabric is not healthy because the I/O Module identified in the message is offline or cannot be communicated with.
records.recommended_action: Make sure that the I/O Module is online and healthy.

messages: Invalid BIOS password.
records.explanation: The input BIOS password used in the operation is invalid.
records.recommended_action: Use a valid BIOS password and retry.

messages: Cannot authenticate specified BIOS password.
records.explanation: The old BIOS password used to change the password is incorrect.
records.recommended_action: Enter the correct old password for the BIOS and retry the operation.

messages: The arg1 Port arg2 network link is down.
records.explanation: The network link is down. Either the network cable is not connected or the network device is not working.
records.recommended_action:
Verify that the network port is enabled and if the port has Activity/Speed LEDs, that they are lit.
Check the network cable, network cable connections, and the attached network switch.

messages: Unable to determine current NIC state.
records.explanation: For the requested operation, enable the NIC to get the NIC details.
records.recommended_action: Check if the NIC is disabled. If disabled, enable the NIC.

messages: The operational status of I/O Module arg1 might have ended.
records.explanation: The operational status of the I/O Module identified in the message has ended. Possible reasons could be that the MCM Group maintenance is in progress or Management Module maintenance is in progress or Fabric maintenance is in progress or Node maintenance is in progress.
records.cause: The operational status of the I/O Module identified in the message has ended. Possible reasons could be that the MCM Group maintenance is in progress or Management Module maintenance is in progress or Fabric maintenance is in progress or Node maintenance is in progress.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the I/O Module, management interface configuration and physical connectivity
are appropriate for the node. Also ensure that all the ongoing MCM Group maintenance and
Management Module maintenance and Fabric maintenance and Node maintenance have completed
before proceeding further.

messages: Unable to detect the I/O Module arg1 because of physical connection and operational issues.
records.explanation: The I/O Module identified in the message cannot be detected because of physical connection and operational issues.
records.cause: The I/O Module identified in the message cannot be detected because of physical connection and operational issues.
records.recommended_action: Make sure that the physical presence and operations of the I/O Module are correct.

messages: Unable to perform a simple I/O module swap operation because the replacement I/O module software version arg1 is different from the fabric software version arg2.
records.explanation: A simple I/O module swap operation cannot be performed because the replacement I/O module software version is different from the fabric software version as identified in the message.
records.cause: A simple I/O module swap operation cannot be performed because the replacement I/O module software version is different from the fabric software version as identified in the message.
records.recommended_action: Make sure that the software versions of replacement I/O module and fabric are the same.

messages: The Restore operation of the I/O Module arg1 is not started because the node is offline.
records.explanation: IO Module identified in the message is OFFLINE in Fabric Manager during Smart Fabric restore operation, Fabric might be restored as unhealthy state.
records.cause: The Restore operation of the I/O Module arg1 is not started because the node is offline.
records.recommended_action:
Once OME-M restore is completed, Verify and ensure the following: 1) Node is correctly inserted in
the slot. 2) make the IO Module identified in the message online by performing a power on or power
cycle activity for the IO Module.

messages: Unable to either create or enable the server interface profile because the NIC bonding configuration feature is not permitted on the partition interface.
records.explanation: The server interface profile cannot be either created or enabled because the NICbonding configuration feature is not permitted on the partition interface.
records.cause: The server interface profile cannot be either created or enabled because the NICbonding configuration feature is not permitted on the partition interface.
records.recommended_action: Enter False as the value of the NIC bonding attribute for the partition interface.

messages: Unable to apply the Fabric Lifecycle configuration because the lead I/O module arg1 lifecycle activity is in progress.
records.explanation: The Fabric Lifecycle operation cannot be applied because the lead I/O modules lifecycle activity is in progress.
records.cause: The Fabric Lifecycle operation cannot be applied because the lead I/O modules lifecycle activity is in progress.
records.recommended_action: Wait for the Lifecycle activity of the lead I/O module to complete and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to retrieve the I/O Module because the I/O Module does not exist.
records.explanation: The I/O Module can not be retrieved because the I/O Module does not exist in the inventory.
records.cause: The I/O Module can not be retrieved because the I/O Module does not exist in the inventory.
records.recommended_action: Enter a valid I/O Module value and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to start the I/O Module Lifecycle operation because a Lifecycle operation is already in progress on the I/O Module.
records.explanation: The Lifecycle operation cannot be started on the I/O Module because a Lifecycle operation is already in progress on the I/O Module.
records.cause: The Lifecycle operation cannot be started on the I/O Module because a Lifecycle operation is already in progress on the I/O Module.
records.recommended_action: Wait for the pending Lifecycle operation to completed and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to start the lifecycle operation on the I/O Module because the I/O Module is offline.
records.explanation: The lifecycle operation cannot be started on the I/O Module because the I/O Module is offline.
records.cause: The lifecycle operation cannot be started on the I/O Module because the I/O Module is offline.
records.recommended_action: Wait for the I/O Module to come back online and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to perform upgrade operation because the I/O Module is part of a SmartFabric.
records.explanation: The upgrade operation on a I/O Module that is part of a SmartFabric is not permitted.
records.cause: Unable to perform upgrade operation because the I/O Module is part of a SmartFabric.
records.recommended_action:
Perform fabric upgrade to upgrade the I/O Modules or delete the SmartFabric and retry the operation
again.

messages: Unable to apply the configuration because the I/O Module is not in fabric mode.
records.explanation: The configuration cannot be applied because the I/O Module is not in the fabric mode.
records.cause: The configuration cannot be applied because the I/O Module is not in the fabric mode.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the I/O Module belongs to a fabric mode by creating a fabric between the I/O
Modules and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to apply the Node Lifecycle configuration because the lead I/O module arg1 Lifecycle activity is in progress.
records.explanation: The Node Lifecycle configuration cannot be applied because the lead I/O Modules lifecycle activity is in progress.
records.cause: The Node Lifecycle configuration cannot be applied because the lead I/O Modules lifecycle activity is in progress.
records.recommended_action: Wait for the Lifecycle activity of lead I/O module to complete and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to process the request because the provided image stream is not valid.
records.explanation: The request can not be processed because the given image stream is not a valid firmware image.
records.cause: The request can not be processed because the given image stream is not a valid firmware image.
records.recommended_action: Provide a valid image stream and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to save the image file because necessary disk space is unavailable.
records.explanation: The image file cannot be processed because necessary disk space is unavailable.
records.cause: The image file cannot be processed because necessary disk space is unavailable.
records.recommended_action: Delete the current image file from /var/os10-image location and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to start the lifecycle operation on the I/O Module because the I/O Module arg1 is offline.
records.explanation: The lifecycle operation on the I/O Module cannot be started because the I/O Module identified in the message is offline.
records.cause: Unable to start the lifecycle operation on the I/O Module because the I/O Module arg1 is offline.
records.recommended_action: Wait for the I/O Module to be available online and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to create or update the fabric because the I/O Module arg1 is offline.
records.explanation: The fabric cannot be created or updated because the I/O Module identified in the message is offline.
records.cause: The fabric cannot be created or updated because the I/O Module identified in the message is offline.
records.recommended_action: Wait for the I/O Module to be available online and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to perform the Startup Backup operation on the I/O Module arg1 because: arg2.
records.explanation: The Startup Backup cannot be performed on the IOM because of the reason identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the I/O Module, management interface configuration, and physical connectivity are
appropriate for the node, and then retry the operation. If the issue persists, contact your service
provider.

messages: Unable to perform the Startup Restore operation because the number of online IOM nodes in the Startup Backup file does not match the number of online nodes on the target IOMs.
records.explanation: The Startup Restore operation cannot be performed because the number of online IOM nodes in the Startup Backup file does not match the number of online nodes on the target IOMs.
records.cause: The Startup Restore operation cannot be performed because the number of online IOM nodes in the Startup Backup file does not match the number of online nodes on the target IOMs.
records.recommended_action: Make sure the number of online nodes on the target IOMs is same as the Startup Backup file.

messages: Unable to perform the Startup Restore operation because the service tag of online IOM nodes in the Startup Backup file does not match the number of online nodes on the target IOMs.
records.explanation: The Startup Restore operation cannot be performed because the service tag of online IOM nodes in the Startup Backup file does not match the service tag of online nodes on the target IOMs.
records.cause: The Startup Restore operation cannot be performed because the service tag of online IOM nodes in the Startup Backup file does not match the service tag of online nodes on the target IOMs.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure the service tag of online IOM nodes on the target IOMs is same as the service tag of online
IOM nodes in the Startup Backup file.

messages: Unable to perform the Startup Restore operation on the I/O Module arg1 because: arg2.
records.explanation: The Startup Restore cannot be performed on the IOM because of the reason identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the I/O Module, management interface configuration, and physical connectivity are
appropriate for the node, and then retry the operation. If the issue persists, contact your service
provider.

messages: Unable to periodically Backup the Startup configuration of the I/O Module arg1 because: arg2.
records.explanation: The Startup configuration of the I/O Module (IOM) cannot be periodically backed up because of the reason identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the I/O Module, management interface configuration, and physical connectivity are
appropriate for the node. If the issue persists, contact your service provider.

messages: Unable to restore the Startup configuration data of I/O Module (IOM) arg1 because the periodic Startup Backup file of the IOM is not available in the file storage.
records.explanation: The Startup configuration data of I/O Module (IOM) identified in the message cannot be backed up because the periodic Startup Backup file of the IOM is not available in the file storage.
records.cause: The Startup configuration data of I/O Module (IOM) identified in the message cannot be backed up because the periodic Startup Backup file of the IOM is not available in the file storage.
records.recommended_action:
If the backup file is available, restore the startup configuration data manually by running the following
command at the CLI: "copy scp://admin:admin@hostip/<SERVICETAG>.xml config://startup.xml".

messages: Unable to sync periodically backed up startup configuration file to the I/O Module arg1 because: arg2.
records.explanation: The Startup Backup file that is periodically backed up cannot be synced to the IOM because of the reason identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the I/O Module, management interface configuration, and physical connectivity are
appropriate for the node. If the issue persists, contact your service provider.

messages: Unable to restore the backed up configuration data because the number of IOM nodes in the backup file does not match with current number of IOM nodes.
records.explanation: The backed up configuration data cannot be restored because the number of IOM nodes in the backup file does not match with current number of IOM nodes.
records.cause: The backed up configuration data cannot be restored because the number of IOM nodes in the backup file does not match with current number of IOM nodes.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the number of IOM nodes in the backup file is the same as the number of IOM nodes in
the current configuration and retry the restore operation.

messages: Unable to restore the backed up configuration data because the Service Tag(s) of IOM nodes in the backup file does not match with Service Tag(s) of current IOM nodes in the cluster.
records.explanation: The backed up configuration data cannot be restored because the Service Tag(s) of IOM nodes in the backup file does not match with Service Tag(s) of current IOM nodes in the cluster.
records.cause: The backed up configuration data cannot be restored because the Service Tag(s) of IOM nodes in the backup file does not match with Service Tag(s) of current IOM nodes in the cluster.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following and retry the operation: (1) Make sure that the Service Tag(s) of the nodes present
in the current configuration are the same as backup file.

messages: The version of OS10 in the target IOM(s) doesnt support backup and restore feature.
records.explanation: Theversion of OS10 in the target IOM(s) doesnt support backup and restorefeature.
records.recommended_action: Ensurethe version of OS10 installed on the target IOM(s) supports backup and restorefeature.

messages: Unable to validate the topology because a different type of IOM is found in the slot pair.
records.explanation: The topology validation failed because of a different type of IOM found in the slot pair in the chassis.
records.cause: The topology validation failed because of a different type of IOM found in the slot pair in the chassis.
records.recommended_action: Make sure that the IOMs of the same type occupy the same slot pair in a chassis.

messages: Unable to validate the MX7116n Fabric Expander Module because the slot number of the MX7116n Fabric Expander Module and the slot number of the Network IOM are different.
records.explanation: The MX7116n Fabric Expander Module validation failed because the MX7116n Fabric Expander Module slot number and the Network IOM slot number are different.
records.cause: The MX7116n Fabric Expander Module validation failed because the MX7116n Fabric Expander Module slot number and the Network IOM slot number are different.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the slot number of the MX7116n Fabric Expander Module and the slot number of the
Network IOM are the same like (A or B) [1]----(A or B) [1] and (A or B) [2]----(A or B) [2]. Mezz cards
can be different either A or B but slot number should be same.

messages: Exposing ISO image as internal device to the server failed.
records.explanation: Unable to expose the ISO image as an internal CD device to the host system because the ISO file is no longer present, network errors are preventing access to the ISO file, or iDRAC may not be responsive.
records.cause: Unable to expose the ISO image as an internal CD device to the host system because the ISO file is no longer present, network errors are preventing access to the ISO file, or iDRAC may not be responsive.
records.recommended_action: 1) Rerun the command. 2) Reset iDRAC and rerun the command.

messages: The fork() command for a child process to perform the task failed.
records.explanation: Failed to execute fork() system call to perform the task in a child process. iDRAC may be unresponsive.
records.recommended_action: Reset iDRAC and rerun the command.

messages: Unable to boot to ISO image.
records.explanation: Booting to ISO has failed. Either BIOS was unable to boot to the ISO image or the provider did not get a response in 5 minutes from BIOS on successful boot to ISO image.
records.recommended_action:
1) Make sure that a POST error did not result in user interaction (Press F1 to continue or F2 to run
BIOS setup). 2) Reset iDRAC and rerun the command.

messages: Unable to detach USB device containing operating system drivers.
records.explanation: Detaching the USB device (that contains drivers for the operating system installation) from the host has failed. The device may be detached, or iDRAC may not be operating normally.
records.recommended_action: Reset iDRAC to detach this device automatically.

messages: Installed BIOS version does not support this method.
records.explanation: The system has an older version of BIOS that does not support this method. Install the latest version of BIOS to use this method.
records.recommended_action: Update the BIOS to version 1.2 or later and then rerun the command.

messages: Cannot access Lifecycle Controller Driver Pack partition.
records.explanation: Driver Pack partition in Lifecycle Controller is not accessible. The Lifecycle Controller or the iDRAC might be unresponsive.
records.recommended_action:
Reset the iDRAC and rerun the command. If the command fails again, check if the iDRAC is functional
and accessible on the system.

messages: Unable to run the command because an invalid firmware image file name is entered.
records.explanation: The command cannot be run because an invalid firmware image file name is entered.
records.cause: The command cannot be run because an invalid firmware image file name is entered.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that a valid firmware image file is entered. The file must not contain any file path
components such as forward slash (/) or period (.).

messages: Setting Boot to PXE through IPMI failed.
records.explanation: The BIOS boot order set to PXE using a standard IPMI command has failed.
records.recommended_action: 1) Check BIOS PXE settings. 2) Rerun the command. 3) Reset iDRAC and rerun the command.

messages: Unable to boot to ISO image because of Secure Boot policy.
records.explanation: Unable to boot to ISO image because of Secure Boot policy.
records.cause: Unable to boot to ISO image because of Secure Boot policy.
records.recommended_action:
If the Secure Boot feature is not desired, disable it in System Setup > System BIOS > Security
Settings page. Otherwise, do the following: 1) review the Secure Boot Policy Summary in F2 System
Setup > System BIOS > Security Settings page. The boot option must be authorized by a public key
or hash value in the Authorized Signature Database. 2) If the boot option is not authorized but it can
be trusted, enter System Setup > System BIOS > Security Settings page, set Secure Boot Policy to
Custom, and add a entry for the boot option in the Authorized Signature Database (System Setup >
System BIOS > Security Settings > Custom Policy Settings > Authorized Signature Database > Import
Database Entry).

messages: Unable to update the drive firmware because the drive is not in a locked state and is potentially vulnerable to unexpected data access.

messages: Predictive failure reported for arg1. Part Number = arg2
records.explanation: The physical disk Self Monitoring Analysis and Reporting Technology (SMART) system has indicated a predictive failure condition as a result of one or more attributes exceeding reliability thresholds. This may be an indication of imminent disk failure. Even though the disk may not have failed yet, it is strongly recommended that the disk be replaced as soon as possible to avoid data loss or unavailability.
records.cause: The physical disk Self Monitoring Analysis and Reporting Technology (SMART) system has indicated a predictive failure condition as a result of one or more attributes exceeding reliability thresholds. This may be an indication of imminent disk failure. Even though the disk may not have failed yet, it is strongly recommended that the disk be replaced as soon as possible to avoid data loss or unavailability.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the physical disk. For a non-redundant VD, first perform a validated backup, then delete the
VD, replace the disk, recreate the VD, and restore from the backup. For a redundant VD, force the
disk offline. If a hot spare is configured, rebuild will begin. Otherwise, remove the disk and replace it
with a new disk. If a rebuild does not start automatically, assign the new disk as a Global Hot Spare
and the rebuild will start. Search "Predictive Failure" on support.dell.com for more information.

messages: SMART FPT exceeded for arg1. Part Number = arg2
records.explanation: A disk on the specified controller has received a SMART alert (predictive failure) indicating that the disk is likely to fail in the near future.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the disk that has received the SMART alert. If the physical disk is a member of a non-
redundant virtual disk, then back up the data before replacing the disk. Removing a physical disk that
is included in a non-redundant virtual disk causes the virtual disk to fail and may cause data loss.

messages: Insufficient space available on arg1 to perform a copyback operation.
records.explanation: This message is generated if a physical disk does not have enough space to do a copyback operation.
records.recommended_action: Replace the physical disk with a larger physical disk, and then restart the copyback operation.

messages: SMART configuration change for arg1.

records.recommended_action:

redundant virtual disk, then back up the data before replacing the disk. Removing a physical disk that

messages: SMART warning for arg1. Part Number = arg2
records.explanation: A disk has received a SMART alert (predictive failure). The disk is likely to fail in the near future.

messages: The arg1 is not supported because it is not supplied by an authorized hardware provider.

records.cause: The arg1 is not supported because it is not supplied by an authorized hardware provider.

messages: SMART warning temperature for arg1. Part Number = arg2
records.explanation: A disk has reached an unacceptable temperature and received a SMART alert (predictive failure). The disk is likely to fail in the near future.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following:1) Determine why the physical disk reached an unacceptable temperature. For
example, a fan failure, incorrect thermostat settings, or the room temperature may be too hot or
cold. 2) Verify that the fans in the server or enclosure are working. 3) If the physical disk is in an
enclosure, check the thermostat settings and examine whether the enclosure is located near a heat
source. Verify the enclosure has enough ventilation and that the room temperature is not too hot.
Refer to the enclosure documentation for more diagnostic information. 4) If you cannot identify why
the disk has reached an unacceptable temperature, then replace the disk. If the physical disk is a
member of a non-redundant virtual disk, then back up the data before replacing the disk. Removing
a physical disk that is included in a non-redundant virtual disk causes the virtual disk to fail and may
cause data loss.

messages: The rebuild operation is abruptly stopped because of a media error on the physical disk drive arg1.

messages: SMART warning degraded for arg1. Part Number = arg2

records.recommended_action:

redundant virtual disk, then back up the data before replacing the disk. Removing a physical disk that
is included in a non-redundant virtual disk will cause the virtual disk to fail and may cause data loss.

messages: The Physical Drive (PD) arg1 is not correctly functioning. Part number arg2.
records.explanation: The RAID Controller is unable to read-write data to the PD identified in the message because the PD is not functioning. The PD is either failed or removed from the server while communicating with the RAID controller.
records.cause: The RAID Controller is unable to read-write data to the PD identified in the message because the PD is not functioning. The PD is either failed or removed from the server while communicating with the RAID controller.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) If the Physical Drive (PD) was removed at the time of event, this event is
expected. Else, replace the PD. 2) If it is a non-redundant Virtual Drive (VD), delete the VD, reinsert
the PD, recreate the VD, and then restore the data from backup. 3) If it is a redundant VD, the data
rebuild operation will automatically start if a hot-spare is already configured. If it does not start, assign
a PD as a global hot-spare so the rebuild operation is automatically started.

records.cause: The controller cannot to communicate with a disk that is assigned as a global hot spare. The disk either failed or was removed. There may also be a bad or loose cable.
records.recommended_action:

replace the disk and reassign the global hot spare.

records.recommended_action:

messages: The only hot spare available is a SATA disk arg1.
records.explanation: The only physical disk available to be assigned as a hot spare is using SATA technology. The physical disks in the virtual disk are using SAS technology. Because of this difference in technology, the hot spare cannot rebuild data if one of the physical disks in the virtual disk fails.
records.cause: The only physical disk available to be assigned as a hot spare is using SATA technology. The physical disks in the virtual disk are using SAS technology. Because of this difference in technology, the hot spare cannot rebuild data if one of the physical disks in the virtual disk fails.
records.recommended_action:

spare.

messages: The only hot spare available is a SAS disk arg1.
records.explanation: The only physical disk available to be assigned as a hot spare is using SAS technology. The physical disks in the virtual disk are using SATA technology. Because of this difference in technology, the hot spare cannot rebuild data if one of the physical disks in the virtual disk fails.
records.cause: The only physical disk available to be assigned as a hot spare is using SAS technology. The physical disks in the virtual disk are using SATA technology. Because of this difference in technology, the hot spare cannot rebuild data if one of the physical disks in the virtual disk fails.
records.recommended_action:
Add a SATA disk that is large enough to be used as the hot spare and assign the new disk as a hot
spare.

messages: The arg1 is not supported.
records.explanation: The physical device may not have a supported version of the firmware or the physical device may not be supported.
records.recommended_action:
If the physical device is supported, then update the firmware to a supported version. If the physical
device is not supported, then replace the physical device with one that is supported.

messages: The clear operation on arg1 failed.
records.explanation: A Clear task was being performed on a physical disk but the task was interrupted and did not complete successfully. The controller may have lost communication with the disk, the disk was removed, or the cables may be loose or defective.
records.cause: A Clear task was being performed on a physical disk but the task was interrupted and did not complete successfully. The controller may have lost communication with the disk, the disk was removed, or the cables may be loose or defective.
records.recommended_action:
Verify that the disk is present and not in a Failed state. Make sure the cables are attached securely.
See the storage hardware documentation for more information on checking the cables. Restart the
Clear task.

messages: Patrol Read found an uncorrectable media error on arg1. Part Number = arg2
records.explanation: The Patrol Read task has encountered an error that cannot be corrected. There may be a bad disk block that cannot be remapped.
records.cause: The Patrol Read task has encountered an error that cannot be corrected. There may be a bad disk block that cannot be remapped.
records.recommended_action:
Backup your data from the disk. Start disk initialization and wait for it to complete, then restore the
data from the backup to the disk.

messages: The dedicated hot-spare drive arg1 does not cover all the virtual drives that form the disk group.
records.explanation: The dedicate hot-spare either does not meet bus protocol, media type, or does not have sufficient storage space to cover all the virtual drives that form the disk group.
records.recommended_action: Assign a drive with matching bus protocol, media type, and sufficient storage space.

messages: arg1 is removed.
records.explanation: A physical disk has been removed from the disk group. This alert can also be caused by loose or defective cables or by problems with the enclosure.
records.cause: A physical disk has been removed from the disk group. This alert can also be caused by loose or defective cables or by problems with the enclosure.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) If a physical disk was removed from the disk group, either replace the
disk or restore the original disk. Identify the disk that was removed by locating the disk that has a
red "X" for its status. 2) Perform a rescan after replacing or restoring the disk. 3) If a disk was not
removed from the disk group, then check for cable problems. Refer to product documentation for
more information on checking the cables. 4) Make sure that the enclosure is powered on. 5) If the
problem persists, check the enclosure documentation for further diagnostic information.

messages: Hot spare arg1 SMART polling has failed.arg2 : Part Number = arg3
records.explanation: The controller firmware attempted to do SMART polling on the hot spare but could not complete the SMART polling. The controller may have lost communication with the hot spare.
records.cause: The controller firmware attempted to do SMART polling on the hot spare but could not complete the SMART polling. The controller may have lost communication with the hot spare.
records.recommended_action:
Verify the health of the disk assigned as a hot spare. Replace the disk and reassign the hot spare.
Make sure the cables are attached securely. See the storage hardware documentation for more
information on checking the cables.

messages: A redundant path is broken.
records.explanation: The controller has two connectors that are connected to the same enclosure. The communication path on one connector has lost connection with the enclosure. The communication path on the other connector is reporting this loss.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure the cables are attached securely. See the Cables Attached Correctly section for more
information on checking the cables. Make sure both Enclosure Management Modules (EMMs) are
healthy.

messages: Insufficient space available on the arg1 to perform a rebuild.
records.explanation: The physical disk inserted is too small for the rebuild to occur.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the physical disk with one of correct protocol (SAS, SATA) with at least the required size.
Force rebuild if it does not start automatically.

messages: arg1is incompatible.
records.explanation: A user attempted to replace a disk with another disk that is using an incompatible technology. For example, replaced one side of a mirror with a SAS disk when the other side of the mirror is using SATA technology.
records.recommended_action: Refer to the hardware documentation for information on replacing disks.

messages: Error occurred on arg1 : arg2. Part Number = arg3
records.explanation: The reason for the error can vary depending on the situation. The firmware error code is indicated in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Verify the health of attached devices. Review the Lifecycle log for significant events. Replace faulty
hardware, if required. Make sure the cables are attached securely. Refer to the storage hardware
documentation for more information on checking the cable connections.

messages: The rebuild of arg1 failed due to errors on the source physical disk.
records.explanation: It is not possible to rebuild data that resides on a defective disk. Resolving this issue may require a rebuild of the virtual disk and then a data restore.
records.cause: The rebuild of arg1 failed due to errors on the source physical disk.
records.recommended_action:
1) If possible, generate the SupportAssist and TTY log reports necessary for resolving or
troubleshooting this issue. 2) Perform a Verified Data Backup operation if a recent backup is
unavailable. 3) If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: A bad disk block on arg1 cannot be reassigned during a write operation.
records.explanation: The physical disk has failed to complete a write operation due to one or more bad blocks. Attempts to reassign the block have failed. Loss of data and redundancy may have occurred.
records.cause: The physical disk has failed to complete a write operation due to one or more bad blocks. Attempts to reassign the block have failed. Loss of data and redundancy may have occurred.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the physical disk. If VD is online, first perform a backup. For a non-redundant VD, delete the
VD, replace the disk, recreate the VD, then restore data from a backup. For a redundant VD, force the
disk offline. If a hot spare is configured, rebuild will begin. Otherwise, remove the disk and replace it
with a new disk. If a rebuild does not start automatically, assign the new disk as a Global Hot Spare
and the rebuild will start. Search "Troubleshooting RAID" on support.dell.com for more information.

messages: An unrecoverable disk media error occurred on arg1. Part Number = arg2
records.explanation: The rebuild or recovery operation encountered an unrecoverable disk media error.
records.recommended_action: Replace the disk.

messages: An unsupported physical disk drive has been detected.
records.explanation: The physical disk does not comply with the standards set by service provider and is not supported.
records.recommended_action: Replace the physical disk with a supported physical disk.

messages: Rebuild not possible on arg1. Part Number = arg2
records.explanation: Physical disk inserted is of the incorrect protocol. SAS or SATA mixing is not supported in the same virtual disk.
records.recommended_action: Remove drive, insert correct protocol type, and force a rebuild as imposed for controller and system.

messages: arg1 has degraded. Part Number = arg2
records.explanation: A physical disk has reported an error condition and may be degraded. The physical disk may have reported the error condition in response to a check consistency or other operation.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the degraded physical disk. Identify the disk that is degraded by locating the disk that has a
red "X" for its status. Perform a rescan after replacing the disk.

messages: Copyback failed from arg1 to arg2.
records.explanation: The physical disk participating in the copyback operation failed.
records.recommended_action: Replace the disk and retry the operation.

messages: Security subsystem errors detected for arg1.
records.explanation: Errors were detected with security related operations on the disk. The data on the disk might not be retrieved or stored successfully. In addition, the security of the stored data might be at risk.
records.recommended_action:
Verify the disk is a Secure Encrypted Disk and is not locked. If it is not, replace the disk with a Secure
Encrypted Disk. See the storage hardware documentation for more information.

messages: Power state change failed on arg1. (from arg2 to arg3)
records.explanation: When physical drives in spun down power state are configured, the drives should transition to spun up power state. If the drive is not functioning properly, this transition could fail.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the physical disk and try again. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR)
