from the chassis. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Chassis Management Controller is unable to send power allocation information to arg1-arg2 at priority arg3.
records.explanation: This situation occurs if the iDRAC is found to be turned off after power allocation information is sent by the CMC or if the communications between the CMC and iDRAC is non functional.
records.recommended_action:
Perform a Virtual Reseat of the component identified in the message. Using the CMC Web UI, go to
Chassis Overview > Troubleshooting > Reset Components, and then select slot for the component
identified in the message and apply the Virtual Reseat.

messages: Chassis Management Controller unable to turn on arg1-arg2 at priority arg3 because of insufficient power. Minimum power needed is arg4 AC Watt, but only arg5 AC Watt is available.
records.explanation: The request to turn on the component identified in the message was not successful because insufficient power is available at the identified priority for the component.
records.cause: The request to turn on the component identified in the message was not successful because insufficient power is available at the identified priority for the component.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure there is enough power supply to distribute power. Using the CMC Web UI, go to Chassis
Overview > Power > Power Budget Status. In the Total Input Power Available For Allocation field view
the available power. To add more power, insert more PSUs or remove unused components from the
chassis.

messages: The System Input Power Cap is too low to be enforced using the current Power Supply configuration.
records.explanation: The current Power Cap setting cannot be enforced. This may be the result of changing the redundancy mode or by changing the PSUs. The power cap setting must be increased to be usable.
records.cause: The current Power Cap setting cannot be enforced. This may be the result of changing the redundancy mode or by changing the PSUs. The power cap setting must be increased to be usable.
records.recommended_action:
Increase the Power Cap value. To increase the Power Cap do one of the following: 1) Using CMC
Web interface: Select "Chassis Overview" -> Power -> Configuration and then adjust System Input
Power Cap values. 2) Run the following RACADM command at the command line interface: "config -g
cfgChassisPower -o cfgChassisPowerCap <value>".Try setting the power cap above the lower bound
displayed on the power configuration page.

messages: Unable to turn on I/O Module arg1 due to insufficient chassis power.
records.explanation: Unable to turn on the I/O Module identified in the message due to insufficient chassis power.
records.cause: Unable to turn on the I/O Module identified in the message due to insufficient chassis power.
records.recommended_action:
Utilize the Chassis Management Controller/Management Module (CMC/MM) web interface to check
available power and I/O Module power requirements. If sufficient power is available, restart the
CMC/MM and retry the operation. If sufficient power is not available due to an insufficient number of
PSUs, add additional PSU(s) and reinsert the I/O Module.

messages: Unable to power on server arg1 because of iDRAC communication issue.
records.explanation: The Chassis Management Controller is unable to communicate with the Server iDRAC service processor and the server could not be powered on. This situation may occur when iDRAC is rebooting.
records.cause: Unable to power on server arg1 because of iDRAC communication issue.
records.recommended_action:
Wait for three minutes and then retry the operation. If the issue persists, remove and reinsert the
server and wait for the iDRAC to finish restarting.

messages: Unable to power on the server arg1 before power on timer expired.
records.explanation: Unable to power on the server before the power on timer has expired. This happens if the server did not show power on status change within 30 seconds after the power on operation was initiated. This issue may also occur when iDRAC is rebooting.
records.recommended_action:
The Server may need more time to power on. Wait for ten seconds and check the power status. If the
server was not powered on, retry the operation. If the issue persists, remove and reinsert the server,
wait for the iDRAC to complete startup, and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to turn on Server arg1 due to I/O fabric inconsistency.
records.explanation: The Server identified in the message did not turn on due to a fabric mismatch between the I/O Module and the Mezzanine card on the Server.
records.cause: The Server identified in the message did not turn on due to a fabric mismatch between the I/O Module and the Mezzanine card on the Server.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the hardware compatibility between the I/O Module (IOM) and the Mezzanine (Mezz)
card is correct. Check the M1000e Hardware Manual for correct component compatibility.

messages: Unable to turn off the Server arg1 due to iDRAC communication issue.
records.explanation: The Chassis Management Controller is unable to communicate with the iDRAC service processor for the Server identified in the message and the Server could not be turned off. This situation may occur when iDRAC is rebooting.
records.cause: Unable to turn off the Server arg1 due to iDRAC communication issue.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Wait for a few minutes for the iDRAC service processor to complete startup. 2)
Retry the operation. 3) If the issue persists, reset the iDRAC and wait a few minutes for the iDRAC
startup to complete before retrying the operation.

messages: Unable to turn off the Server arg1 before the Power Off timer expired.
records.explanation: Unable to turn off the Server before the Power Off timer has expired. This happens if the Server did not show "power off" status change within 30 seconds after the operation was initiated. This situation may also occur when iDRAC is rebooting.
records.recommended_action:
The Server may need more time to turn off. Wait for ten seconds and check the power status. If the
Server was not turned off, retry the operation. If the issue persists, remove and reinsert the Server,
wait for the iDRAC to complete startup, and retry the operation.

messages: Server arg1 did not gracefully shutdown before the timer expired.
records.explanation: The server identified in the message did not gracefully shutdown before the CMC shutdown timer expired. This happens if the server did not show power off status change within 60 seconds after the operation was initiated, or if the OS in the server has not successfully shutdown.
records.recommended_action:
Check if the OS in the server identified in the message has successfully shutdown, if not, manually
complete the shutdown or wait for the shutdown to complete normally. If the issue persists, perform a
forced power down of the server identified in the message.

messages: Unable to communicate to the iDRAC, when trying to power cycle the server arg1.
records.explanation: The Chassis Management Controller is not able to communicate with the iDRAC on the server identified in the message. Therefore, the server could not be power cycled. This situation may occur when iDRAC is rebooting.
records.recommended_action:
Wait for few minutes, and then retry the operation. If the issue persists, do one of the following: 1)
Reset the iDRAC, 2) Perform a Virtual Reseat of the server, 3) Remove and re-insert the server.

messages: The Chassis Management Controller is unable to communicate to the iDRAC, when trying to hard reset the server arg1.
records.explanation: The Chassis Management Controller is not able to communicate with the iDRAC on the server identified in the message. Therefore the server could not be hard reset. This situation may occur when iDRAC is restarting.
records.recommended_action:
Wait for three minutes, and then retry the operation. If the issue persists, remove and reinsert the
server and wait for the iDRAC to finish restarting before retying the operation.

messages: Chassis Management Controller is unable to turn on the iDRAC on server-arg1 because power required is less than available power.
records.explanation: The Chassis Management Controller is unable to turn on the iDRAC because power required is less than available power.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure there is enough power supply to distribute power. Go to, the Chassis Overview > Power >
Power Budget Status. In the Total Input Power Available For Allocation field, view the available power.
To add more power, insert more PSUs or remove unused components from the chassis. Remove and
reinsert the server when enough power is available.

messages: Servers are turned off to allocate power to the newly inserted hard disk drives.
records.explanation: Before inserting hard disk drives, always make sure the Chassis has enough available power. Otherwise operating servers may be turned off.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure there is enough power supply to distribute power. Go to, the Chassis Overview > Power >
Power Budget Status. In the Total Input Power Available For Allocation field, view the available power.
To add more power, insert more PSUs or remove unused components from the chassis.

messages: Chassis Management Controller is unable to set the Enhanced Cooling Mode because the requested power arg1 AC Watt is more than available power arg2 AC Watt.
records.explanation: The available power is not sufficient to enable the Enhanced Cooling Mode feature.
records.cause: Chassis Management Controller is unable to set the Enhanced Cooling Mode because the requested power arg1 AC Watt is more than available power arg2 AC Watt.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure there is enough power supply to enable the Enhanced Cooling Mode feature. Go to, the
Chassis Overview > Power > Power Budget Status. In the Total Input Power Available For Allocation
field view the available power. To add more power, insert more PSUs or remove unused components
from the chassis.

messages: Chassis Management Controller is unable to turn on server arg1 due to insufficient power for the arg2.
records.explanation: The turn-on request for the server identified in the message did not succeed because of insufficient power to the chassis component identified in the message.
records.cause: The turn-on request for the server identified in the message did not succeed because of insufficient power to the chassis component identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
The Chassis Management Controller (CMC) will retry turning on the server and the corresponding
components associated to the server after a predefined interval. If the issue persists, refer to the
Managing and Monitoring Power section in the CMC User Guide for more information on configuring
power management settings.

messages: Chassis Management Controller is unable to turn on server-arg1 because PSU redundancy is lost and the available power is insufficient.
records.explanation: The Chassis Management Controller cannot turn on the server identified in the message, because PSU redundancy is lost or PSUs are removed. Sufficient power is not available for the operation.
records.cause: The Chassis Management Controller cannot turn on the server identified in the message, because PSU redundancy is lost or PSUs are removed. Sufficient power is not available for the operation.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure there is enough power supply to distribute power. Go to, the Chassis Overview > Power >
Power Budget Status. In the Total Input Power Available For Allocation field, view the available power.
To add more power, insert more PSUs or remove unused components from the chassis. When enough
power is available, retry the operation.

messages: The Power Supply Unit (PSU) arg1 is turned off because it is not supported by the Chassis.
records.explanation: The identified Power Supply Unit (PSU) is turned off because it is not supported by the Chassis.
records.cause: The identified Power Supply Unit (PSU) is turned off because it is not supported by the Chassis.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the PSU identified in the message with an appropriate unit, and then retry the operation. For
a list of PSUs that are compatible, consult the system Owners Manual or If the issue persists, Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: The Power Supply Unit (PSU) arg1 is turned off because it is not compatible with the other PSUs used in the Chassis.
records.explanation: The Power Supply Unit (PSU) identified in the message is turned off because it is not compatible with the other PSUs in the Chassis.
records.cause: The Power Supply Unit (PSU) identified in the message is turned off because it is not compatible with the other PSUs in the Chassis.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the PSU with an appropriate unit, and then retry the operation. For a list of PSUs
that are compatible, consult the system Owners Manual or If the issue persists, Collect a
SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to send power allocation information to the component arg1-arg2.
records.explanation: CMC could not successfully send the power allocation information to the component identified in the message, because either iDRAC is stopped after the power allocation was sent by CMC or the communication between CMC and iDRAC has ended.
records.cause: CMC could not successfully send the power allocation information to the component identified in the message, because either iDRAC is stopped after the power allocation was sent by CMC or the communication between CMC and iDRAC has ended.
records.recommended_action:
Perform a Virtual Reseat operation of the component, and then retry the operation. To virtually reseat
a component, log in to the CMC Web interface, select Chassis Overview > Troubleshooting > Reset
Components > select the option corresponding to the component, and then click Virtual Reseat.

messages: Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to turn on the component arg1-arg2 because of insufficient power. The minimum required power is arg3 AC Watts, but only arg4 AC Watts is available.
records.explanation: CMC could not successfully turn on the component identified in the message, because of insufficient power available.
records.cause: CMC could not successfully turn on the component identified in the message, because of insufficient power available.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure there is sufficient power available, and then retry the operation. To view the available
power, on the CMC Web interface, click Chassis Overview > Power > Power Budget Status. The
available power is displayed in the Total Input Power Available For Allocation field. To increase
available power, add more PSUs or remove unused components from the Chassis.

messages: Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to turn on the component arg1-arg2 because of insufficient power.
records.explanation: CMC could not successfully turn on the component identified in the message, because of insufficient power available.
records.cause: CMC could not successfully turn on the component identified in the message, because of insufficient power available.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure there is sufficient power available, and then retry the operation. To increase available
power, add more PSUs, use PSUs with higher voltage inputs or a higher power rating, remove unused
components from the Chassis, or change the redundancy policy to Redundancy Alerting Only or
Non-redundant.

messages: Unable to turn on the server arg1 because of an inconsistency between the I/O module and mezzanine card.
records.explanation: The server identified in the message could not be successfully turned on because of incompatibility between the I/O module and mezzanine card.
records.cause: The server identified in the message could not be successfully turned on because of incompatibility between the I/O module and mezzanine card.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the I/O module and mezzanine card are compatible. For information about
compatibility of hardware components, see the Modular System Chassis Hardware Manual.

messages: Unable to turn on the server arg1 because of an inconsistency between the chassis and server components.
records.explanation: The server identified in the message could not be successfully turned on because of incompatibility between the chassis PCIe components and mezzanine card.
records.cause: The server identified in the message could not be successfully turned on because of incompatibility between the chassis PCIe components and mezzanine card.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the chassis PCIe components and mezzanine card are compatible. For information
about compatibility of hardware components, see the Modular System Chassis Hardware Manual
available at the support site.

messages: Unable to turn on serverarg1 because the required power arg2 AC Watts exceeds the subsystem Connector Limit arg3 AC Watts for IO modules, Blowers and Servers.
records.explanation: The server identified in the message cannot be turned on if the Connector Limit for the subsystems identified in the message is exceeded .
records.cause: Unable to turn on serverarg1 because the required power arg2 AC Watts exceeds the subsystem Connector Limit arg3 AC Watts for IO modules, Blowers and Servers.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure the system operates within the subsystem Connector Limit for the components specified.
To review power budget information select Chassis Overview -> Power -> Budget Status. Turn off
unused components within the subsystem to make power available for the server to turn on or turn
off low priority servers and try the operation again.

messages: Unable to set the chassis power property arg1.
records.explanation: The chassis power property identified in the message cannot be set.
records.recommended_action:
If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://
www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze
the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: The arg1 firmware in the server slot arg2 does not support the storage sled.
records.explanation: The firmware identified in the message does not support the storage sled.
records.recommended_action:
Update the firmware identified in the message to the supported latest available version. See the latest
iDRAC User Guide for information on the versions that support the storage sled.

messages: The arg1 firmware in the server slot arg2 does not support additional PCIe slots.
records.explanation: The firmware identified in the message does not support the PCIe reassignment operation.
records.recommended_action:
Update the firmware identified in the message to the supported latest available version. See the latest
iDRAC User Guide for information on the versions that support the PCIe reassignment.

messages: Unable to turn on the storage sled controller arg1 in slot arg2 because the arg3 module is not functioning.
records.explanation: The Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to turn on the storage sled controller identified in the message. The Chassis storage sled controller is unable to turn on due to a configuration or hardware issue.
records.recommended_action:
Remove the storage sled identified in the message, re-insert it and observe whether the issue is
resolved. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit
https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to
analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: The Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to turn on the storage sleds associated with server in slot arg1 because the iDRAC firmware version in the server does not support the chassis storage module.
records.explanation: The Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to turn on the storage sled controller identified in the message because iDRAC version installed on the server is not compatible.
records.cause: The Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to turn on the storage sled controller identified in the message because iDRAC version installed on the server is not compatible.
records.recommended_action:
Update the iDRAC firmware identified in the message to the supported latest available version and
retry the operation. For information about the supported firmware versions, refer to the Chassis
Management Controller users Guide available at the support site.

messages: The Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to turn on the storage sled controller installed on server in slot arg1 because the server does not have a Mezzanine card.
records.explanation: The Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to turn on the storage sled controller installed on the server in the slot identified in the message because the server does not have a Mezzanine card. A Mezzanine card position is identified with the following numbers: For quarter-width server, the position number is 1. For half-width server mezzanine C & B maps to position numbers 1 & 2 respectively. For full-width server, Mezzanine C & B on the upper- or left part of the server maps to position numbers 1 & 2 respectively. Mezzanine C & B on the lower- or right part of the server maps to position numbers 3 & 4 respectively.
records.cause: The Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to turn on the storage sled controller installed on the server in the slot identified in the message because the server does not have a Mezzanine card. A Mezzanine card position is identified with the following numbers: For quarter-width server, the position number is 1. For half-width server mezzanine C & B maps to position numbers 1 & 2 respectively. For full-width server, Mezzanine C & B on the upper- or left part of the server maps to position numbers 1 & 2 respectively. Mezzanine C & B on the lower- or right part of the server maps to position numbers 3 & 4 respectively.
records.recommended_action:
Install a Mezzanine card in the Mezzanine card slot of the server identified in the message, and then
retry the operation.

messages: Unable to turn on the server arg1 because of an inconsistency between the I/O module and mezzanine card.
records.explanation: The server identified in the message could not be successfully turned on because of incompatibility between the I/O module and mezzanine card.
records.cause: The server identified in the message could not be successfully turned on because of incompatibility between the I/O module and mezzanine card.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the I/O module and mezzanine card are compatible. For information about
compatibility of hardware components, see the Modular System Chassis Hardware Manual.

messages: Unable to turn off chassis power.
records.explanation: Chassis power state transition did not complete successfully. This may be due to one of the following: 1) Unable to turn off one or more servers, 2) A firmware update may be in progress.
records.cause: Chassis power state transition did not complete successfully. This may be due to one of the following: 1) Unable to turn off one or more servers, 2) A firmware update may be in progress.
records.recommended_action: Check the hardware logs for more information. If the issue persists, contact your service provider.

messages: The Microcontroller Unit (MCU) firmware update operation is in progress.
records.explanation: The Microcontroller Unit (MCU) firmware update operation is in progress.
records.recommended_action: Do not initiate any power operations while the MCU firmware update operation is in progress.

messages: Firmware update of the MCU arg1 has failed.
records.explanation: The firmware update of the Microcontroller Unit (MCU) identified in the message has failed. This may be due to network connection issues or unavailability of power.
records.cause: The firmware update of the Microcontroller Unit (MCU) identified in the message has failed. This may be due to network connection issues or unavailability of power.
records.recommended_action:
Inspect the component source of the MCU identified in the message and try the update again. If the
issue persist, refer to the Users Guide of the product model available in the support site.

messages: Resource allocation failure.
records.explanation: The operation did not complete successfully because of lack of memory or file space in the iDRAC.
records.cause: The operation did not complete successfully because of lack of memory or file space in the iDRAC.
records.recommended_action: Reset the iDRAC and retry the operation.

messages: There are no batteries to be displayed.
records.explanation: Batteries cannot be displayed. This error may occur if the host system is powered off or there is a bad or disconnected cable for batteries connected to the controller.
records.recommended_action:
1) Check if the host system is powered off or shutdown. 2. Verify that the batteries are connected
properly.

messages: There are no virtual disks to be displayed.
records.explanation: Virtual disks cannot be displayed. This error may occur if the host system is powered off or there are no virtual disks created.
records.recommended_action: 1) Check if the host system is powered off or shutdown. 2. Check if virtual disks are created.

messages: Unable to display the enclosures data because the host system is powered off, or the enclosure adapter cable is disconnected or damaged.
records.explanation: Enclosures data cannot be displayed either because the host system is powered off, any enclosure is not connected to the controller, or there is a damaged or disconnected adapter cable of the enclosure.
records.cause: Enclosures data cannot be displayed either because the host system is powered off, any enclosure is not connected to the controller, or there is a damaged or disconnected adapter cable of the enclosure.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: On the Enclosure page: 1. Check if the host system is powered on. 2. Check if the
storage enclosure is powered on. 3. Ensure that the adapter cables are properly connected and there
is no damage. 4) iDRAC may provide limited support to enclosures that are attached to the storage
controller. On the Physical Disks page, perform the tasks that are recommended for the Enclosure
page. Note that in case of physical devices, iDRAC may provide limited support to physical devices
attached to the storage controller.

messages: Unable to find the requested resource.
records.explanation: The requested information cannot be displayed, because the system did not find any matching resource. This occurs because the system is turned off, resource is not present, or the resource is removed or deleted. For example, resources such as physicals disks, vFlash SD card, SSL certificate or custom signing certificate.
records.cause: The requested information cannot be displayed, because the system did not find any matching resource. This occurs because the system is turned off, resource is not present, or the resource is removed or deleted. For example, resources such as physicals disks, vFlash SD card, SSL certificate or custom signing certificate.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following and retry the operation: 1) Turn on the system. 2) Make the resource
available.

messages: Converting physical disk drives to RAID-compatible will overwrite any OS-created RAID arrays.
records.explanation: Converting physical disk drives to RAID-compatible will overwrite any OS-created RAID arrays.
records.recommended_action: Make sure that there are no OS-configured RAID arrays, and then click OK.

messages: One or more of the following storage controllers on the server is not managed by iDRAC : arg1.
records.explanation: One or more of the storage controllers on the server is not managed by iDRAC.
records.recommended_action:
Use vendor utilities that support the storage controllers. For more information about supported vendor
utilities, see the vendors website.

messages: Unable to perform OS to iDRAC Pass-Through with the current system configuration.
records.explanation: The integrated NICs in the system do not support OS to iDRAC Pass-Through.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure the integrated NICs are enabled from BIOS setup and support OS to iDRAC Pass-Through,
then retry the operation. To access BIOS setup, press F2 during system startup. For more information
about OS to iDRAC Pass-Through, see iDRAC7 Users Guide.

messages: The iDRAC will restart when the iDRAC firmware update is complete. All current user sessions will be closed.
records.explanation: The message appears in Job Queue page when the iDRAC firmware update job status is downloading. Communication to the iDRAC will be lost when the iDRAC restarts to complete the firmware update.
records.recommended_action:
Reconnect iDRAC communications session after iDRAC is restarted. The iDRAC will be ready for login
once the restart is complete.

messages: Cancelling the firmware update operation will delete all the uploaded firmware files. Do you want to continue?
records.explanation: Cancelling the firmware update operation will cancel all firmware updates selected and delete all uploaded firmware files.
records.recommended_action:
Select Yes to cancel the firmware update operation and delete all uploaded firmware files. Select No
to dismiss the message and continue the firmware update operation.

messages: The iDRAC firmware rollback will cause an iDRAC restart and all current user sessions will be closed.
records.explanation: The message appears in Firmware Rollback page when the iDRAC firmware rollback action completed successfully.
records.recommended_action:
Reconnect iDRAC communications sessions after iDRAC is restarted. The iDRAC will be ready for login
once the restart is complete.

messages: The Enclosure Split Mode configuration process is started. However, the setting will be applied only during the next AC power cycle operation of the Chassis. This may result in loss of configuration and/or access to physical disk drive(s).
records.explanation: The Enclosure Split Mode configuration process is started. However, the setting will be applied only during the next AC power cycle operation of the Chassis. This may result in loss of configuration and/or access to physical disk drive(s).
records.recommended_action: Press OK to continue.

messages: The Clear Foreign Configuration operation will delete the foreign virtual disk information from the controllers associated physical disk drives. Clearing will remove metadata associated with the virtual disks, making the physical disk drives available for creating new virtual disks. To remove foreign data, perform an initialization operation.
records.explanation: Clear foreign configuration will delete the foreign virtual disk information from the controllers associated physical disk drives. Clearing will remove metadata associated with the virtual disks, making the physical disk drives available for creating new virtual disks. To remove foreign data, perform an initialization operation.
records.recommended_action: Press OK to continue.

messages: Resetting the selected PERC controllers configuration will delete all the virtual disks (VDs) and unassign hot-spares from the associated controller.
records.explanation: Resetting the selected PERC controllers configuration will delete all the virtual disks (VDs) and unassign hot-spares from the associated controller.
records.recommended_action: Press OK to continue.

messages: This setting will be applied after the server has been turned off and turned on again. This may result in loss of configuration and/or access to physical disk drive(s).
records.explanation: This setting will be applied after the server has been turned off and turned on again. This may result in loss of configuration and/or access physical disk drive(s) or virtual disk(s) being marked offline. This may also result in some disk(s) being identified as foreign disks. Foreign physical disk drive(s) or virtual disk(s) can be imported or cleared.
records.recommended_action: Press OK to continue.

messages: Initializing the virtual disk will permanently delete data from the virtual disk.
records.explanation: Initializing the virtual disk will permanently delete data from the virtual disk.
records.recommended_action: Press OK to continue.

messages: Deleting the virtual disk will remove the virtual disk from the controllers configuration.
records.explanation: Deleting the virtual disk will remove the virtual disk from the controllers configuration. If the specified virtual disk is a boot device, the server will not boot unless another boot device is selected in BIOS.
records.recommended_action: If the specified virtual disk is a boot device, the server will not boot. Press OK to continue.

messages: Server iDRAC user credentials and/or BIOS passwords are not currently set to default credentials. The USB Configuration XML feature is not available unless default credentials are set.
records.explanation: The USB Configuration XML feature is not available if the iDRAC user credentials and BIOS passwords are not set to default values.
records.recommended_action: Reset the iDRAC user credentials and BIOS passwords to default and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to create a virtual disk on the selected disk drives, because Lifecycle Controller is not enabled.
records.explanation: Unable to create a virtual disk on the selected disk drives, because Lifecycle Controller is not enabled.
records.cause: Unable to create a virtual disk on the selected disk drives, because Lifecycle Controller is not enabled.
records.recommended_action:
To enable Lifecycle Controller, reboot the server. During server startup, press F2 to enter System
Setup. Go to iDRAC Settings -> Lifecycle Controller, select Enable, and save the changes. Retry the
operation after the server has restarted.

messages: Unable to assign and un-assign physical disk drives as global hotspare(s), because Lifecycle Controller is not enabled.
records.explanation: Unable to assign and un-assign physical disk drives as global hotspare(s), because Lifecycle Controller is not enabled.
records.cause: Unable to assign and un-assign physical disk drives as global hotspare(s), because Lifecycle Controller is not enabled.
records.recommended_action:
To enable Lifecycle Controller, reboot the server. During server startup, press F2 to enter System
Setup. Go to iDRAC Settings -> Lifecycle Controller, select Enable, and save the changes. Retry the
operation after the server has restarted.

messages: Unable to retrieve the hardware overview information because the server is turned off.
records.explanation: The iDRAC is unable to retrieve hardware overview related information while the server is turned off.
records.cause: Unable to retrieve the hardware overview information because the server is turned off.
records.recommended_action: Turn the server on to view the hardware overview information.

messages: Failed to program the Chassis assigned MAC address for the NIC.Integrated.arg1.
records.explanation: Failed to program the Chassis assigned MAC address for the NIC.Integrated in the specified slot number.
records.recommended_action: Reseat the server and retry.

messages: The firmware version arg1 of the Chassis Management Controller/Management Module is earlier than the required version arg2.
records.explanation: The Chassis Management Controller/Management Module firmware version identified in the message is earlier than the version required to support the server.
records.recommended_action:
Update the Chassis Management Controller/Management Module firmware to the required version
identified in the message.

messages: The Quick Sync communication is no longer functioning.
records.explanation: The Quick Sync communication or the connection to the iDRAC is no longer functioning.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Remove and reseat the bezel. 2) Turn the bezel on by pressing the activation
button. 3) Try the Quick Sync feature again. If the issue persists, contact your technical support
provider.

messages: The Prepare to Remove operation will stop any activity on the PCIe SSD device so that it can be removed safely. The device is safe to remove when the disk shows the safe to remove LED pattern.
records.explanation: The Prepare to Remove operation will stop any activity on the PCIe SSD device so that it can be removed safely. The device is safe to remove when the disk shows the safe to remove LED pattern.
records.recommended_action: Press OK to continue.

messages: Unable to perform Prepare to Remove or Secure Erase operations on the selected PCIe SSD disk drive(s), because Lifecycle Controller is not enabled.
records.explanation: Unable to perform Prepare to Remove or Secure Erase operations on the selected PCIe SSD disk drive(s), because Lifecycle Controller is not enabled. Retry the operation after the server has restarted.
records.cause: Unable to perform Prepare to Remove or Secure Erase operations on the selected PCIe SSD disk drive(s), because Lifecycle Controller is not enabled. Retry the operation after the server has restarted.
records.recommended_action:
To enable Lifecycle Controller, reboot the server. During server startup, press F2 to enter System
Setup. Go to iDRAC Settings -> Lifecycle Controller, select Enable, and save the changes. Retry the
operation after the server has restarted.

messages: Unable to perform virtual disk (VD) operations, because Lifecycle Controller is not enabled.
records.explanation: Unable to perform virtual disk(VD) operations, because Lifecycle Controller is not enabled.
records.cause: Unable to perform virtual disk(VD) operations, because Lifecycle Controller is not enabled.
records.recommended_action:
Enable the Lifecycle Controller and retry the operation. To enable Lifecycle Controller, restart the
server. During server startup, press F2 to enter System Setup. Go to iDRAC Settings -> Lifecycle
Controller, select Enable, and save the changes.

messages: Unable to retrieve the fan information.
records.explanation: Fan information cannot be displayed. This situation may occur if the server is powered off.
records.recommended_action:
Power on the server. If the server is already powered on, wait for a few minutes and refresh the page.
If the problem persists, contact your service provider.

messages: USB Management Port is currently disabled in BIOS configuration.
records.explanation: The requested operation using the USB Management Port cannot be completed because the port is disabled in BIOS configuration.
records.cause: The requested operation using the USB Management Port cannot be completed because the port is disabled in BIOS configuration.
records.recommended_action: Enable the USB Management Port in BIOS configuration to use this feature.

messages: Unable to perform a firmware update because a valid catalog file is not available on the network share.
records.explanation: Unable to perform a firmware update because a valid catalog file is not available on the network share.
records.cause: Unable to perform a firmware update because a valid catalog file is not available on the network share.
records.recommended_action: Make sure that a valid catalog file is available on the network share and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to assign USB NIC IP address arg1 to the OSBMC device because only Link Local IP address can be allowed.
records.explanation: The USB NIC IP address identified in the message cannot be assigned to the OSBMC device because only Link Local IP address can be allowed.
records.cause: The USB NIC IP address identified in the message cannot be assigned to the OSBMC device because only Link Local IP address can be allowed.
records.recommended_action:
Enter appropriate Link Local IP address, and then retry the operation. For information about supported
IP addresses, refer to the iDRAC Users Guide available at the support site.

messages: Unable to assign USB NIC IP address arg1 to the OSBMC device because IP address setting conflicts with existing network interface IP.
records.explanation: The USB NIC IP address identified in the message cannot be assigned to the OSBMC device because IP address setting conflicts with existing network interface IP.
records.cause: The USB NIC IP address identified in the message cannot be assigned to the OSBMC device because IP address setting conflicts with existing network interface IP.
records.recommended_action:
Enter an unique IP address for OSBMC USB NIC that is not the same as another NICs IP address,
and then retry the operation. For information about supported IP addresses, refer to the iDRAC Users
Guide available at the support site.

messages: Unable to modify the BIOS configuration settings because the Lifecycle Controller or Collect System Inventory on Restart (CSIOR), or both the features are disabled.
records.explanation: The BIOS configuration settings cannot be modified because the Lifecycle Controller or Collect System Inventory on Restart (CSIOR), or both the features are disabled.
records.cause: The BIOS configuration settings cannot be modified because the Lifecycle Controller or Collect System Inventory on Restart (CSIOR), or both the features are disabled.
records.recommended_action:
Enable the Lifecycle Controller and Collect System Inventory on Restart (CSIOR) features, and then
retry the operation. To enable these features: Press F2(System Setup) when the company logo is
displayed. On the System Setup page, click iDRAC Settings > Lifecycle Controller. Select Enabled
corresponding to Lifecycle Controller and CSIOR.

messages: Unable to display the BIOS attributes either because attributes are not present in the registry, a Lifecycle Controller Wipe operation has been performed, or there is an internal error.
records.explanation: The BIOS attributes cannot be displayed either because attributes are not present in the registry, a Lifecycle Controller Wipe operation has been performed, or there is an internal error.
records.cause: The BIOS attributes cannot be displayed either because attributes are not present in the registry, a Lifecycle Controller Wipe operation has been performed, or there is an internal error.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation after doing the following: 1) Start the server. 2) Press F2 (System Setup)
when the company logo is displayed. 3) On the System Setup page, click iDRAC Settings; Lifecycle
Controller. Select Enabled corresponding to Lifecycle Controller and CSIOR. 4) After Lifecycle
Controller and CSIOR are enabled, restart the system and make sure that the inventory collection
operation completes successfully.

messages: Unable to import or store the file because of insufficient disk space on iDRAC local storage.
records.explanation: The file cannot be imported because of insufficient disk space on iDRAC local storage.
records.cause: The file cannot be imported because of insufficient disk space on iDRAC local storage.
records.recommended_action: Delete the unused files by invoking the ClearTransferSession method, and then retry the operation.

messages: The OS to iDRAC pass-through cannot be enabled.
records.explanation: The OS to iDRAC pass-through cannot be enabled, because the NIC is in Dedicated mode.
records.cause: The OS to iDRAC pass-through cannot be enabled, because the NIC is in Dedicated mode.
records.recommended_action:
Change the iDRAC NIC mode to shared mode using "racadm set idrac.nic.selection <value>", and retry
the operation.

messages: NIC objects are not available in the current system configuration.
records.explanation: NIC objects are not available if NIC devices are not installed in the system, or if some iDRAC services are busy.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure the NIC devices are correctly installed in the system and retry the operation after the
Collect System Inventory On Restart (CSIOR) feature has updated the system inventory.

messages: Unable to create the configuration job.
records.explanation: Configuration jobs are created only if at least one object on the device or component (for example, NIC.Slot.1 or BIOS) has a pending value to be applied.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that there is at least one object on the specified device or component that has a pending
value, and retry the operation.

messages: Successfully accepted the RAID storage configuration operation. The change is in pending state.
records.explanation: The requested RAID storage operation was successfully accepted and now must be applied by creating a RAID storage configuration job.
records.recommended_action:
To apply the configuration operation, create a configuration job, and then restart the server. To create
the required commit and reboot jobs, run the jobqueue command. For more information about the
jobqueue command, enter the RACADM command "racadm help jobqueue".

messages: Specifying ftp.dell.com as the catalog source for the Automatic Update feature may result in frequent system firmware updates because the catalog on ftp.dell.com changes often.
records.explanation: Individual component firmware updates may occur frequently and cause changes to the catalog on ftp.dell.com. Specifying ftp.dell.com as the catalog source for the Automatic Update feature may result in frequent system firmware updates.
records.cause: Specifying ftp.dell.com as the catalog source for the Automatic Update feature may result in frequent system firmware updates because the catalog on ftp.dell.com changes often.
records.recommended_action:
Creating a custom repository using the Repository Manager tool allows control of the frequency of
component firmware updates.

messages: Unable to set iDRAC.PCIeVDM.DenyFQDD attribute because the FQDD is already available in the PCIe Vendor Defined Message (VDM) deny list.
records.explanation: TheiDRAC.PCIeVDM.DenyFQDD attribute cannot be set because the FQDD is already available in the PCIe Vendor Defined Message (VDM) deny list.
records.cause: TheiDRAC.PCIeVDM.DenyFQDD attribute cannot be set because the FQDD is already available in the PCIe Vendor Defined Message (VDM) deny list.
records.recommended_action: Enter a valid and unique FQDD and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to delete the FQDD from the PCIe Vendor Defined Message (VDM) deny list because the FQDD is unavailable in the list.
records.explanation: The FQDD cannot be deleted from the PCIe Vendor Defined Message (VDM) deny list because the FQDD is unavailable.
records.cause: The FQDD cannot be deleted from the PCIe Vendor Defined Message (VDM) deny list because the FQDD is unavailable.
records.recommended_action: Enter a valid and unique FQDD and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to delete the pending values for the specified device because the iDRAC internal storage is in use by a currently running job.
records.explanation: Unable to clear the pending state from the attributes for a RAID object. A job is currently running and iDRAC internal storage is in use.
records.cause: Unable to delete the pending values for the specified device because the iDRAC internal storage is in use by a currently running job.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation after any currently running jobs have completed. Jobs can be monitored by
running the racadm command "racadm jobqueue view".

messages: Unable to perform the operation because Fibre Channel (FC) attributes are not available in the current server configuration.
records.explanation: Fibre Channel (FC) objects are not available if Fibre Channel devices are not installed in the server, or if some iDRAC services are busy.
records.cause: Unable to perform the operation because Fibre Channel (FC) attributes are not available in the current server configuration.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Power off and remove AC or DC power from the server. 2) Make sure the Fibre
Channel devices are correctly installed in the server. 3) Restart the server to allow the Collect System
Inventory On Restart (CSIOR) feature to update the server inventory. 4) Retry the operation.

messages: Unable to modify the BootOnce object.
records.explanation: The BootOnce object could not be modified, because the FirstBootDevice object is set to either F10, F11, or BIOS.
records.cause: The BootOnce object could not be modified, because the FirstBootDevice object is set to either F10, F11, or BIOS.
records.recommended_action:
Configure the FirstBootDevice object to values other than F10, F11, or BIOS and retry the set
operation for the BootOnce object. For more information about possible FirstBootDevice values, run
the RACADM command "racadm help idrac.serverboot.firstbootdevice".

messages: Unable to complete requested operation because an Type A/A USB cable is connected to the front panel USB port and the iDRAC is emulating a NIC device.
records.explanation: Unable to complete requested operation because a Type A/A USB cable is connected to the front panel USB port and the iDRAC is emulating a NIC device.
records.cause: Unable to complete requested operation because a Type A/A USB cable is connected to the front panel USB port and the iDRAC is emulating a NIC device.
records.recommended_action:
To change the USB Management Port mode setting, remove the Type A/A USB cable from the front
panel USB port and change the port mode settings.

messages: Unable to change USB Management Port mode.
records.explanation: USB Management Port state cannot be changed because of an unknown hardware or firmware issue.
records.recommended_action:
To change the Management Port mode settings do the following: If a device is present, remove and
reinsert the USB device from the front panel USB Management port and retry the operation. If the
issue persists restart the iDRAC and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to import the specified file to iDRAC.
records.explanation: The file import operation has failed because of large file size.
records.cause: The file import operation has failed because of large file size.
records.recommended_action:
The file import operation has timed out, because the file is invalid or is exceeding the permissible size.
Retry the operation with a valid file.

messages: Unable to update the LCD panel firmware either because of connection issues or the LCD bezel is damaged.
records.explanation: The LCD panel firmware cannot be updated either because of connection issues or the LCD bezel is damaged.
records.cause: The LCD panel firmware cannot be updated either because of connection issues or the LCD bezel is damaged.
records.recommended_action: Remove the LCD bezel and reinstall. If the issue persists, replace the LCD bezel.

messages: Unable to complete the operation because the Secure Boot policy is set to Standard.
records.explanation: The operation cannot be completed because the Secure Boot policy is set to Standard.
records.cause: The operation cannot be completed because the Secure Boot policy is set to Standard.
records.recommended_action:
Reset the Secure Boot policy to Custom by running the following RACADM command at the command
line interface (CLI), and then retry the operation:"racadm set bios.syssecurity.securebootpolicy
Custom". For more information, see the RACADM CLI Reference Guide available on the support site.

messages: Unable to display the properties of Secure Boot Certificate because the certificate data entered does not exist.
records.explanation: The properties of Secure Boot Certificate cannot be displayed because the certificate data entered does not exist.
records.cause: The properties of Secure Boot Certificate cannot be displayed because the certificate data entered does not exist.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that valid certificate data exists and retry the operation. For more information, see the
RACADM CLI Reference Guide available on the support site.

messages: Unable to export the Secure Boot certificate data to remote share because of insufficient storage space.
records.explanation: The Secure Boot certificate data cannot be exported to remote share because of insufficient storage space.
records.cause: The Secure Boot certificate data cannot be exported to remote share because of insufficient storage space.
records.recommended_action: Make sure that the remote share has sufficient storage space and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to export the Secure Boot certificate data because the size of exported file is greater than 25 MB.
records.explanation: The Secure Boot certificate data cannot be exported because the size of exported file is greater than 25 MB.
records.cause: The Secure Boot certificate data cannot be exported because the size of exported file is greater than 25 MB.
records.recommended_action:
Export the certificate to a network file share (NFS) folder that has a storage space of 25 MB and
greater.

messages: Unable to initiate the arg1 firmware update.
records.explanation: A new firmware update job cannot be initiated while an existing firmware update job is still in one of these states: "New", "Downloading", or "Running".
records.recommended_action: Wait until the existing firmware update jobs are completed or scheduled before retrying the operation.

messages: Unable to update arg1 firmware because of internal issues.
records.explanation: The firmware of the component identified in the message cannot be updated because of internal issues.
records.recommended_action:
Reset the management module by using the Management Module Graphical User Interface (GUI), and
then retry the operation. If the issue persists, contact your service provider.

messages: Unable to perform the requested httpbioscert operation. The current version of the BIOS does not support it.
records.explanation: The httpbioscert operations are not supported on any BIOS other than BIOS 2.4.2 currently.
records.recommended_action: Run the command racadm update -f to update the BIOS to the latest version, and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to schedule the BIOS Live Scan job because of internal issues.
records.explanation: The BIOS Live Scan job cannot be scheduled because of internal issues.
records.recommended_action:
For information about the issue, see the Lifecycle Logs by running the "racadm lclog view" command
at the Command Line Interface (CLI).

messages: Unable to schedule the BIOS Live Scan job because a BIOS Live Scan is already scheduled.
records.explanation: The BIOS Live Scan job cannot be scheduled because a BIOS Live Scan is already scheduled.
records.cause: The BIOS Live Scan job cannot be scheduled because a BIOS Live Scan is already scheduled.
records.recommended_action:
Wait for the current schedule to complete and create the new schedule. Else, run the "racadm
biosscan -s 0" command at the Command Line Interface (CLI) to delete the current schedule, and
then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to delete the BIOS Live Scan job because of internal issues.
records.explanation: The BIOS Live Scan job cannot be deleted because of internal issues.
records.recommended_action:
Running the "racadm lclog view" command to view the Lifecycle Logs and get information about the
reason for the issue.

messages: Unable to schedule the BIOS Live Scan job because either the freuquency or date or time entered is invalid.
records.explanation: The BIOS Live Scan job cannot be scheduled because the start frequency or time entered is invalid.
records.cause: The BIOS Live Scan job cannot be scheduled because the start frequency or time entered is invalid.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the input values are correct and retry the operation. For information about valid
options, run the following racadm command:"racadm help biosscan".

messages: Unable to import the HTTP Boot certificate for the BIOS boot device because one or more of the following reasons: 1) The input file is either corrupted, invalid, or cannot be detected. 2) Insufficient space in the certificate store. 3) internal issues.
records.explanation: The HTTP Boot certificate for the BIOS boot device cannot be imported because one or more of the following reasons: 1) The input file is either corrupted, invalid, or cannot be detected. 2) Insufficient space in the certificate store. 3) Unknown internal issues.
records.cause: The HTTP Boot certificate for the BIOS boot device cannot be imported because one or more of the following reasons: 1) The input file is either corrupted, invalid, or cannot be detected. 2) Insufficient space in the certificate store. 3) Unknown internal issues.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following and retry the operation: 1) Enter valid parameters and retry the operation. 2) If the
issue persists, enable some free storage space in the certificate store by deleting a few certificates,
restart iDRAC, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to export the HTTP Boot certificate for the BIOS boot device because one or more of the following reasons: 1) Insufficient space in the destination. 2) The file is not available. 3) Destination folder is inaccessible. 4) Internal issues.
records.explanation: The HTTP Boot certificate cannot be exported for the BIOS boot device because one or more of the following reasons: 1) Insufficient space in the destination folder. 2) The certificate file is not available. 3) Destination folder cannot be accessed. Insufficient access rights. 5) Unknown internal issues.
records.cause: The HTTP Boot certificate cannot be exported for the BIOS boot device because one or more of the following reasons: 1) Insufficient space in the destination folder. 2) The certificate file is not available. 3) Destination folder cannot be accessed. Insufficient access rights. 5) Unknown internal issues.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following and retry the operation: 1) Make sure that the destination folder has sufficient
storage space and not of read-only type. 2) The parameters entered are valid. 3) If the issue persists,
restart iDRAC, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to delete the HTTP Boot certificate for the BIOS boot device because of either insufficient space in the certificate store or an internal issue.
records.explanation: The HTTP Boot certificate cannot be deleted for the BIOS boot device because of either insufficient space in the certificate store or an internal issue.
records.cause: The HTTP Boot certificate cannot be deleted for the BIOS boot device because of either insufficient space in the certificate store or an internal issue.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation. If the issue persists, make sure that the destination folder has sufficient storage
space by deleting a few certificates, restart iDRAC, and then retry the operation.

messages: There is no image to be displayed.
records.explanation: There is no image to be displayed when there is an firmware incompatiblity or storage services having issue.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following and retry the operation: 1. Make sure that the latest iDRAC firmware and backplane
firmware is installed. 2. Verify that the adapter cables are properly connected and there are no bent
pins. 3. Restart the server. To restart, click Configuration > Power Management > Power Control >
Power Cycle System (cold boot). Else, run the RACADM command at the Command Line Interface
(CLI): racadm serveraction powercycle. 4. Reset iDRAC to its initial state. To reset, click Maintenance
> Diagnostics > Reset iDRAC to Factory Defaults. Else, run the RACADM command at the Command
Line Interface (CLI): racadm racresetcfg.

messages: The Cryptographic Erase operation will be performed on the selected PCIe SSD immediately. This will erase all data.
records.explanation: The Cryptographic Erase operation performed on a PCIe SSD overwrites data in all blocks in an encrypted manner. All the data on the PCIe SSD device will be permanently lost. The changes become effective immediately.
records.recommended_action: To continue, click OK.

messages: Unable to change auto-negotiation property for the NIC.
records.explanation: The auto-negotiation property for the iDRAC NIC can be changed only if the NIC is in dedicated mode. To change the NIC mode to dedicated, an iDRAC Enterprise license is required.
records.recommended_action:
Change the NIC mode to dedicated mode by using "racadm set idrac.nic.selection <1 | Dedicated>",
and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to start the system configuration profile export or import operation.
records.explanation: The request to perform a system profile export or import operation cannot be started because a firmware update operation is already in progress.
records.cause: The request to perform a system profile export or import operation cannot be started because a firmware update operation is already in progress.
records.recommended_action: Wait until the update operation is completed or cancel the update operation, and retry.

messages: Unable to set the NIC to Auto Dedicated NIC mode.
records.explanation: The "Auto Dedicated NIC" mode cannot be set for a NIC if the NIC selection mode is set to "Dedicated NIC".
records.recommended_action:
To set the NIC to Auto Dedicated NIC mode, set NIC selection mode to "Shared NIC", and retry the
operation.

messages: Unable to initiate the arg1 firmware update.
records.explanation: A new firmware update job cannot be initiated while an existing firmware update job is still in one of these states: "New", "Downloading", or "Running".
records.recommended_action:
Wait until the existing firmware update jobs are completed or scheduled before retrying the operation.
To monitor the status of the existing jobs, use the "racadm jobqueue view" command.

messages: Unable to apply the arg1 firmware update.
records.explanation: Only Windows-based Update Package (.exe extension), iDRAC Firmware (.d7 extension), Personality Module Firmware (.pm extension), Lifecycle Controller firmware repair package (.usc) are supported for the firmware update operation.
records.recommended_action: For the list of supported files, use "racadm help update".

messages: Unable to apply the arg1 update.
records.explanation: If Lifecycle Controller is disabled, the firmware update operation cannot continue.
records.recommended_action:
Enable Lifecycle Controller using the "racadm set
lifecyclecontroller.lcattributes.lifecyclecontrollerstate 1" command, and retry the operation.

messages: IPv6 cannot be enabled.
records.explanation: IPv6 cannot be enabled if iDRAC NIC is disabled.
records.recommended_action:
Enable iDRAC NIC using "racadm set iDRAC.NIC.Enable < 1 | Enabled >" command and retry the
operation.

messages: arg1 value has dropped below the lower critical limit.
records.explanation: To update the user that the sensor value is less than the lower critical threshold.
records.recommended_action: Inspect the sensor in described in the message.

messages: arg1 value has exceeded the upper critical limit.
records.explanation: To update the user that the sensor value is greater than the upper critical threshold.
records.recommended_action: Inspect the sensor described in the message.

messages: The Fan Test could not be run because the Enhanced Rear Door Heat Exchanger must be in the "Off" state.
records.explanation: The Fan Test could not be run because the Enhanced Rear Door Heat Exchanger must be in the "Off" state.
records.cause: The Fan Test could not be run because the Enhanced Rear Door Heat Exchanger must be in the "Off" state.
records.recommended_action: Transition the Enhanced Rear Door Heat Exchanger to the "Off" state.

messages: The eRDHx thermal controls are arg1.
records.explanation: The eRDHx thermal controls are in the Mode indicated in the message. eRDHx fans are not running, liquid cooling valve is closed, effectively eRDHx is no longer cooling the rack.
records.recommended_action:
Immediate attention is needed if the current mode of eRDHx is not intentionally set. In this mode,
eRDHx is no longer cooling the rack. All systems in the rack must be in power off state. This mode is
intended for maintenance purpose only.

messages: Fan redundancy is lost.
records.explanation: One of more fans have failed or have been removed or a configuration change occurred which requires additional fans.
records.recommended_action: Remove and re-install failed fans or install additional fans.

messages: Fan redundancy is degraded.
records.explanation: One of more fans have failed or have been removed or a configuration change occurred which requires additional fans.
records.recommended_action: Remove and re-install failed fans or install additional fans.

messages: The fans are not redundant. Insufficient resources to maintain normal operations.
records.explanation: One of more fans have failed or have been removed or a configuration change occurred which requires additional fans.
records.recommended_action: Remove and re-install failed fans or install additional fans.

messages: Power supply redundancy is lost.
records.explanation: The current power operational mode is non-redundant because of a power supply exception, a power supply inventory change, or a system power inventory change. The system was previously operating in a power redundant mode.
records.cause: The current power operational mode is non-redundant because of a power supply exception, a power supply inventory change, or a system power inventory change. The system was previously operating in a power redundant mode.
records.recommended_action: Check the event log for power supply failures. Review system configuration and power consumption.

messages: Power supply redundancy is degraded.
records.explanation: The current power operational mode is non-redundant because of a power supply exception, a power supply inventory change, or a system power inventory change. The system was previously operating in a power redundant mode.
records.cause: The current power operational mode is non-redundant because of a power supply exception, a power supply inventory change, or a system power inventory change. The system was previously operating in a power redundant mode.
records.recommended_action: Check the event log for power supply failures. Review system configuration and power consumption.

messages: The power supplies are not redundant. Insufficient resources to maintain normal operations.
records.explanation: The system may power down or operate in a performance degraded state.
records.recommended_action:
Check the event log for power supply failures. Review system configuration and power consumption
and upgrade or install power supplies accordingly.

messages: Unable to determine the redundancy status of the power supply units.
records.explanation: One of the power supply units have failed.
records.recommended_action: Replace the failed power supply with a new power supply.

messages: Unable to determine the redundancy status of the fans.
records.explanation: One or more fans are non-functional or may have failed.
records.recommended_action: Check that all fans are working properly. Replace any non-functional fan with a new fan.

messages: Unable to extract payloads from Update Package.
records.explanation: The firmware payloads in the Update Package cannot be extracted. This may be because the file is not valid or the security signature cannot be verified.
records.cause: The firmware payloads in the Update Package cannot be extracted. This may be because the file is not valid or the security signature cannot be verified.
records.recommended_action: Re-acquire the Update Package from the service provider.

messages: Reinstall or Rollback cannot be performed since no applicable firmware was found on the Lifecycle Controller.
records.explanation: Reinstall or Rollback cannot be performed since no applicable firmware was found on the Lifecycle Controller.
records.recommended_action: Directly update to the desired version.

messages: Version compatibility check was not successful.
records.explanation: The version compatibility check of the firmware update package was not successful for the device specified.
records.recommended_action:
The version compatibility check was not successful for the device specified. Verify that the firmware
version pre-requisites specified in the release notes are satisfied.

messages: Firmware update in progress.
records.explanation: A firmware update operation is currently in progress.
records.recommended_action: Check the firmware update job status. Wait for the current job to complete.

messages: Unable to update the Chassis firmware because of an issue in the network communication between iDRAC and CMC/MM.
records.explanation: The Chassis firmware cannot be updated because of an issue in the communication between iDRAC and CMC/MM.
records.cause: The Chassis firmware cannot be updated because of an issue in the communication between iDRAC and CMC/MM.
records.recommended_action:
Verify the status of CMC/MM by accessing the CMC/MM and making sure it is functioning and
responding and then retry the operation. For more information about troubleshooting a CMC/MM
issue, see the CMC/MM User Manual. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR)
report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use
the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to update the firmware because communication with Chassis Management Controller (CMC) or Management Module (MM) took more time than the specified duration.
records.explanation: The firmware cannot be updated because communication with Chassis Management Controller (CMC) or Management Module (MM) took more time than the specified duration.
records.cause: The firmware cannot be updated because communication with Chassis Management Controller (CMC) or Management Module (MM) took more time than the specified duration.
records.recommended_action:
Ensure that CMC or MM is functioning and responding, and then retry the operation. For more
information about troubleshooting a CMC or MM issue, see the respective Users Guide version of
Chassis Management Controller or Management Module available on the support site. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to update the Chassis firmware, Chassis Management/Management Module at Server is not set to Monitor and Configure.
records.explanation: The Chassis firmware cannot be updated because the Chassis Management/Management Module at Server (CMAS) attribute is incorrectly set. The CMAS attribute must be set to Monitor and Configure on the CMC/MM in order to update CMC/MM firmware from and iDRAC.
records.cause: The Chassis firmware cannot be updated because the Chassis Management/Management Module at Server (CMAS) attribute is incorrectly set. The CMAS attribute must be set to Monitor and Configure on the CMC/MM in order to update CMC/MM firmware from and iDRAC.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the Chassis Management at Server attribute is set to Monitor and Configure, and then
retry the operation. To set the correct attribute using Chassis Management Controller/Management
Module (CMC/MM) GUI, navigate to Chassis Overview, then Setup, then General, and then click on
the Chassis management at Server attribute to select the correct value.

messages: Unable to update the Chassis firmware, Allow CMC/MM Updates Through OS and Lifecycle Controller is set to Disabled.
records.explanation: Unable to update the Chassis firmware because the Allow CMC/MM Updates Through OS and Lifecycle Controller setting is set to Disabled.
records.cause: Unable to update the Chassis firmware because the Allow CMC/MM Updates Through OS and Lifecycle Controller setting is set to Disabled.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the Allow CMC Updates Through OS and Lifecycle Controller setting is set to Enabled,
and then retry the operation. Using the iDRAC Web UI, select iDRAC > Update, click on the Settings
tab, select Enabled for the setting and then click Apply button.

messages: Unable to update the Chassis firmware because an update operation is already in progress.
records.explanation: The Chassis firmware cannot be updated because an update operation is already in progress.
records.cause: The Chassis firmware cannot be updated because an update operation is already in progress.
records.recommended_action: Wait until the current update operation is completed, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to install Lifecycle Controller firmware.
records.explanation: Unable to install Lifecycle Controller firmware.
records.recommended_action:
Reinstall the iDRAC7 firmware (DUP) to repair Lifecycle Controller. For more information, see
Lifecycle Controller Users Guide.

messages: Unable to complete the firmware update operation because the specified firmware image is for a component that is not in the target system inventory or the component is disabled for performing the update.
records.explanation: Unable to complete the firmware update operation because the specified firmware image is for a component that is not in the target system inventory or the component is disabled for performing the update.
records.cause: Unable to complete the firmware update operation because the specified firmware image is for a component that is not in the target system inventory or the component is disabled for performing the update.
records.recommended_action:
1) Identify and download the firmware version that corresponds to the component being updated in
the target system inventory, and retry the operation. For a list of supported firmware versions, refer
to the iDRAC Users Guide available on the support site.2) Enable the component if disabled, and retry
the operation.

messages: Unable to complete the firmware update operation because the specified firmware image is not compatible with the target system model.
records.explanation: Unable to complete the firmware update operation because the specified firmware image is not compatible with the target system.
records.cause: Unable to complete the firmware update operation because the specified firmware image is not compatible with the target system.
records.recommended_action:
Identify and download the firmware version that corresponds to the system model being updated, and
retry the operation. For a list of supported firmware versions, refer to the iDRAC Users Guide available
on the support site.

messages: Unable to complete the firmware update operation because the specified firmware image is out of date.
records.explanation: Unable to complete the firmware update operation because the specified firmware image is out of date.
records.cause: Unable to complete the firmware update operation because the specified firmware image is out of date.
records.recommended_action:
Identify and download the firmware version that is up to date, and retry the operation. For a list of
supported firmware versions, refer to the iDRAC Users Guide available on the support site.

messages: Unable to complete the job because of an error during iDRAC firmware update.
records.explanation: The operation cannot be completed because of an error during iDRAC firmware update.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to complete the job because of an error with iDRAC reboot during iDRAC firmware update.
records.explanation: The operation cannot be completed because of an error with iDRAC reboot during iDRAC firmware update.
records.cause: The operation cannot be completed because of an error with iDRAC reboot during iDRAC firmware update.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to complete the job because of an error during iDRAC firmware rollback.
records.explanation: The operation cannot be completed because of an error during iDRAC firmware rollback.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: The device arg1 with version arg2 does not match the current package version arg3.
records.explanation: The device firmware version does not match the current package version as identified in the message. This situation occurs when the management firmware includes an update package for the device.
records.recommended_action: Update the management module firmware again and check the logs for errors.

messages: Unable to complete the operation arg1 because the iDRAC processors are currently overloaded by other tasks.
records.explanation: The operation identified in the message cannot be completed because the iDRAC processors are overloaded by other tasks.
records.cause: The operation identified in the message cannot be completed because the iDRAC processors are overloaded by other tasks.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to update the iDRAC firmware because the of a timeout during the iDRAC firmware update process.
records.explanation: The iDRAC firmware cannot be updated because the of a timeout during the iDRAC firmware update process.
records.cause: The iDRAC firmware cannot be updated because the of a timeout during the iDRAC firmware update process.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to update the arg1 firmware because the required license is currently not installed on the target system.
records.explanation: The firmware of the component identified in the message cannot be updated because the required license is currently not installed on the target system.
records.cause: The firmware of the component identified in the message cannot be updated because the required license is currently not installed on the target system.
