records.explanation: The configuration operation could not be performed because the specified span count is not valid.
records.cause: The configuration operation could not be performed because the specified span count is not valid.
records.recommended_action: Enter a valid span count, and then retry the operation.

messages: The iDRAC Service Module version present on the server OS does not support the requested PCIe SSD (NVMe) device operation.
records.explanation: The iDRAC Service Module version present on the server OS does not support the requested PCIe SSD (NVMe) device operation.
records.recommended_action:
Update the Dell iDRAC Service Module (ISM) to the version that supports the requested operation on
the PCIe SSD (NVMe) device.

messages: The requested RAID configuration operation is not allowed because the controller is currently in HBA mode.
records.explanation: The requested RAID configuration operation will not be allowed because the RAID controller is currently in HBA mode.
records.cause: The requested RAID configuration operation will not be allowed because the RAID controller is currently in HBA mode.
records.recommended_action:
In order to perform a RAID configuration operation, change the controller mode to RAID and retry
the operation. For switching to RAID mode using the F2 System Setup utility, go to Device Settings
> "RAID Controller "> Controller Management > Advanced Controller Management > Switch to RAID
mode.

messages: The operation cannot be performed because the enclosure configuration mode (Split or Unified) change request is pending.
records.explanation: The requested operation could not be completed because there is an operation pending to change the enclosure configuration mode (Split or Unified). This operation is exclusive because it involves changing the RAID backplane topology.
records.cause: The requested operation could not be completed because there is an operation pending to change the enclosure configuration mode (Split or Unified). This operation is exclusive because it involves changing the RAID backplane topology.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Create a job to complete the pending enclosure mode change request
operation, allow the job to complete, restart the server, and then retry the operation. 2) Cancel any
pending operations on the RAID controller, and then retry the operation.

messages: Enclosure configuration mode (Split/Unified) cannot be changed because there are already pending operations.
records.explanation: The requested operation could not be completed because at least one other pending operation was found on the RAID controller. This operation needs exclusivity because it involves changing RAID backplane topology.
records.cause: The requested operation could not be completed because at least one other pending operation was found on the RAID controller. This operation needs exclusivity because it involves changing RAID backplane topology.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Create a job to complete the pending operations, allow the job to complete,
and then retry the operation. 2) Cancel any pending operations on the RAID controller, and then retry
the operation.

messages: The requested operation requires a reboot type that does not match the reboot type required for pending operations.
records.explanation: The requested operation cannot be performed because it involves server reboot type which is different than the reboot type of pending operations. Combining operations with different reboot types for the same RAID controller is not supported by iDRAC.
records.cause: The requested operation cannot be performed because it involves server reboot type which is different than the reboot type of pending operations. Combining operations with different reboot types for the same RAID controller is not supported by iDRAC.
records.recommended_action: Cancel any pending operations on the RAID controller and then retry the operation.

messages: The Physical Disk(s) specified are too small to create a Virtual Disk of the requested size.
records.explanation: The Physical Disk(s) specified are too small to create a Virtual Disk of the requested size.
records.recommended_action:
Specify Physical Disk FQDD IDs of physical disk drive(s) that have a larger disk space, and retry the
operation.

messages: Unable to create the job because another job is currently running
records.explanation: The requested job cannot be run because another job is currently running. Two options for running jobs on multiple storage controllers are: 1) Run the jobs on each controller individually. Wait for each job to complete before starting the configuration and job creation on the next controller. 2) Schedule multiple jobs to run at a later time using the scheduling options.
records.cause: The requested job cannot be run because another job is currently running. Two options for running jobs on multiple storage controllers are: 1) Run the jobs on each controller individually. Wait for each job to complete before starting the configuration and job creation on the next controller. 2) Schedule multiple jobs to run at a later time using the scheduling options.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the currently running job is completed, and then retry the operation. If necessary,
recreate the configuration and the job. For information about running jobs on multiple storage
controllers, see the iDRAC Online Help or iDRAC Users Guide.

messages: Unable to change the high availability (HA) mode of RAID storage because the servers are turned on.
records.explanation: The high availability (HA) mode of RAID storage cannot be changed because the servers are turned on.
records.cause: The high availability (HA) mode of RAID storage cannot be changed because the servers are turned on.
records.recommended_action: Turn off all the servers in the chassis and retry the operation.

messages: A device arg1 is in an unknown state.
records.explanation: The controller cannot communicate with a device. The state of the device cannot be determined. There may be a bad or loose cable, or a missing device, or a problem with the driver or firmware.
records.cause: The controller cannot communicate with a device. The state of the device cannot be determined. There may be a bad or loose cable, or a missing device, or a problem with the driver or firmware.
records.recommended_action:
See the storage hardware documentation for information on checking the cables. Check for problems
with any enclosures attached to the system. Verify that the controller has a supported version of the
driver and firmware. Rebooting the system may resolve this problem.

messages: Access to shared storage will not be available, because the RAID controller is unable to turn on.
records.explanation: The RAID controller was detected, however it is unable to turn on. Access to shared storage will not be available.
records.cause: Access to shared storage will not be available, because the RAID controller is unable to turn on.
records.recommended_action: Update the Chassis Infrastructure firmware.

messages: Unable to start the operation because the hard disk drives (HDDs) have the RAID controller in mixed RAID mode.
records.explanation: The operation cannot be performed because the HDDs have the RAID controller in mixed RAID mode.
records.cause: The operation cannot be performed because the HDDs have the RAID controller in mixed RAID mode.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following to separate the mixed RAID mode and retry the operation. 1) Group the hard disk
drives (HDDs) into to Windows and Linux metadata categories by observing the RAIDType property on
the Physical Disk page of iDRAC graphical user interface (GUI). 2) Convert a group of selected HDDs
to non-RAID mode by running the ConvertToNonRAID method or RACADM command, or by setting
the RAIDPDState to NonRAID in the Server Configuration Profile.

messages: Unable to convert the physical disk drive to Ready status because either the input value is not supported or the controllers current RAID mode does not allow the input value.
records.explanation: The physical disk drive cannot be converted to Ready status because either the input value is not supported or the controllers current RAID mode does not allow the input value. The RAIDMode may not match the RAIDType or the SoftwareRAIDMode requested.
records.cause: The physical disk drive cannot be converted to Ready status because either the input value is not supported or the controllers current RAID mode does not allow the input value. The RAIDMode may not match the RAIDType or the SoftwareRAIDMode requested.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the input value is correct and retry the operation. If RAIDMode has a value then the
requested RAIDType or SoftwareRAIDMode value must match.

messages: Unable to start the operation because the operation is not supported on the NVMe RAID drives.
records.explanation: The operation cannot be started because the operation is not supported on the NVMe RAID drives. Either the drive is behind hardware RAID controller or the RAIDMode may not match the RAIDType or the SoftwareRAIDMode requested.
records.cause: The operation cannot be started because the operation is not supported on the NVMe RAID drives. Either the drive is behind hardware RAID controller or the RAIDMode may not match the RAIDType or the SoftwareRAIDMode requested.
records.recommended_action:
Set the NVMeMode attribute of BIOS to NonRAID and retry the operation. To set the NonRAID mode,
see the staged objects example of setting Single-Object in the SET command section of the iDRAC
RACADM CLI Reference guide available on the support site. To verify the setting by using iDRAC
Graphical User Interface (GUI), click Configuration > BIOS Settings > NVMe Settings. No response
action is required if the NVMe drives are behind hardware RAID controller, because this operation is
not supported.

messages: The fault-tolerant pair of RAID controllers arg1 and arg2 can have issues in their PCIe fabric because both controllers are on the same PCIe fabric.
records.explanation: The two RAID controllers are on the same PCIe Fabric. This means that an issue with a single PCIe switch or Mezzanine card could result in the loss of all storage functionality from this pair of controllers.
records.cause: The fault-tolerant pair of RAID controllers arg1 and arg2 can have issues in their PCIe fabric because both controllers are on the same PCIe fabric.
records.recommended_action: Change the slot location of one of the RAID Controllers.

messages: CEM Storage Management has lost communication with the arg1.
records.explanation: Storage Management has lost communication with a controller. This may occur if the connectivity between the controller and iDRAC is disrupted or any underlying hardware problems are encountered.
records.recommended_action:
Reboot the system or iDRAC. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report
using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the
Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to initialize the virtual disk because the RAID controller selected does not support the initialization mode.
records.explanation: The virtual disk cannot be initialized because the RAID controller selected does not support the initialization mode.
records.cause: The virtual disk cannot be initialized because the RAID controller selected does not support the initialization mode.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the RAID controller selected for the operation supports the initialization mode, and
they retry the operation. For more information about supported RAID controllers, see the specific
documentation of RAID controller. Also, refer to the Dell Lifecycle Controller Remote Services Quick
Start Guide available at the support site.

messages: A firmware update was applied to a drive that requires a DC power cycle (cold boot). If the drive is in an external enclosure, the updated firmware will only be activated after a DC power cycle of the enclosure.
records.explanation: A drive firmware update was applied but requires a DC power cycle (cold boot) to activate. If the drive is internal to the system performing the update, no further action is required. If the drive is in an external enclosure, the enclosure must be turned off and then turned on in order for the updated drive firmware to activate.
records.recommended_action:
If the drive is internal to the system performing the update, no further action is required. If the drive
is in an external enclosure, the enclosure must be turned off and then turned on in order for the
updated drive firmware to activate. After turning off the external enclosure, wait for drives to spin
down before turning the enclosure back on. The drive firmware will activate after the enclosure is
turned back on.

messages: Unable to update the firmware of the physical disk drive arg1 because an incorrect firmware image file is used.
records.explanation: The firmware package being used to update the physical disk drive is not valid for the drive model identified in the message. The firmware package contains the drive component id in the list of supported drives, but the firmware image is not valid for the drive model identified in the message.
records.cause: Unable to update the firmware of the physical disk drive arg1 because an incorrect firmware image file is used.
records.recommended_action:
Acquire the correct firmware image file for the drive model identified in the message, and then retry
the operation. The correct image file can be found by using the drive model information and searching
the support site for related firmware.

messages: Unable to run the command to reconfigure the Virtual Disk because the storage controller does not support reconfiguration operations.
records.explanation: The storage controller does not support reconfiguration operations.
records.cause: Unable to run the command to reconfigure the Virtual Disk because the storage controller does not support reconfiguration operations.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure of the following and retry the operation: 1) The latest version of Lifecycle Controller
firmware is installed, 2) The storage controller supports reconfiguration process. For information
about the supported storage controller versions, see the Lifecycle Controller Users Guide available on
the support site.

messages: Unable to start the reconfiguration operation on the virtual drive because a reconfiguration operation is either in pending state or already running.
records.explanation: The reconfiguration operation cannot be started on the virtual drive because a reconfiguration operation is either in pending state or already running.
records.cause: The reconfiguration operation cannot be started on the virtual drive because a reconfiguration operation is either in pending state or already running.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Commit and run the pending reconfiguration operation and retry the
operation. 2) Cancel the currently running or pending reconfiguration operation and retry the new
reconfiguration operation.

messages: Unable to perform the reconfiguration operation because the storage controller does not support reconfiguring a Virtual Disk that has more than one span.
records.explanation: Certain RAID levels require a Virtual Disk to have more than one span. Reconfiguration operation on these Virtual Disks is not supported by the storage controller.
records.cause: Unable to perform the reconfiguration operation because the storage controller does not support reconfiguring a Virtual Disk that has more than one span.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the Virtual Disk has a single span and retry the reconfiguration operation. For
information about the RAID levels that have a single span, see the Lifecycle Controller Users Guide
available at the support site.

messages: Unable to perform the reconfiguration operation because the Virtual Disk size specified is invalid.
records.explanation: Expansion of storage capacity of a Virtual Disk is limited by the disk space of its physical disks and the Virtual Disk RAID level. Based on these two values there is a maximum limit on the capacity expansion size of a Virtual Disk.
records.cause: Unable to perform the reconfiguration operation because the Virtual Disk size specified is invalid.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the Virtual Disk size specified for the reconfiguration operation is less than or equal
to the maximum possible value. For information about the maximum possible value, see the Lifecycle
Controller Users Guide available at the support site.

messages: Unable to perform the reconfiguration operation because a reconfiguration operation is already in progress for the Virtual Disk.
records.explanation: The storage controller only allows one reconfiguration operation at a time on a Virtual Disk. A new reconfiguration operation cannot be requested until the currently executing reconfiguration operation is complete or is canceled.
records.cause: Unable to perform the reconfiguration operation because a reconfiguration operation is already in progress for the Virtual Disk.
records.recommended_action:
There are two possible actions. 1) Wait for the current reconfiguration operation to complete and then
retry the new reconfiguration operation. 2) Cancel the current reconfiguration operation and then
start the new reconfiguration operation.

messages: Unable to start the reconfiguration operation because the requested reconfiguration operation is invalid.
records.explanation: The storage controller does not support online capacity expansion and RAID level migration of a Virtual Disk at the same time.
records.recommended_action:
There are two Reconfiguration operations possible on a Virtual Disk 1) Online Expansion of the storage
capacity 2) RAID level migration . Only one of the above two operations can be specified in a
Reconfiguration operation. Make sure that only one of the above two operation types is requested
and retry the operation. Also make sure that if provided, the Virtual Disk size is at least 1% of the
maximum expansion size possible. Also make sure that if provided, the new Virtual Disk RAID level is
different from the existing raid level.

messages: Unable to complete the operation because one or more physical disk drives selected for the operation are currently used by another operation.
records.explanation: The operation cannot be completed because one or more physical disk drives selected for the operation is currently used by another operation.
records.cause: The operation cannot be completed because one or more physical disk drives selected for the operation is currently used by another operation.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following and retry the operation: 1) Wait for the current operation to complete. 2)
Select a drive that is free for the operation.

messages: Unable to create RAID on the selected controller because the controller is in enhanced HBA mode.
records.explanation: Unable to create RAID on the selected controller because the controller is in enhanced HBA mode.
records.cause: Unable to create RAID on the selected controller because the controller is in enhanced HBA mode.
records.recommended_action: Retry the operation using other supported controllers.

messages: The firmware on the arg1 controller is successfully updated. However, to make the update effective, AC power cycle the host device.
records.explanation: The firmware on the controller identified in the message is successfully updated. However, to make the update effective, AC power cycle the host device.
records.recommended_action: AC Power cycle the host device.

messages: Unable to update the firmware on the arg1 controller because the controller key change operation is pending.
records.explanation: The firmware on the controller identified in the message cannot be successfully updated because the controller key change operation is pending.
records.cause: The firmware on the controller identified in the message cannot be successfully updated because the controller key change operation is pending.
records.recommended_action:
To complete the controller key change operation, perform a power cycle by running the following
RACADM command at the Command Line Interface (CLI): "racadm serveraction powercycle".

messages: The soft Secure Boot mode is detected on the arg1 controller.
records.explanation: PERC controller is in soft secure boot. This is not a factory config and will need to be replaced with a PERC controller which has hard secureboot enabled.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the PERC by using a PERC that has hard Secure Boot enabled. For information about
replacing a PERC card, see the respective servers Installation and Service Manual available on the
support site. Also, see the relevant QRL PowerEdge server micro videos.

messages: Unable to use the physical drive arg1 because the drive selected is not unmap-capable for virtual drive configuration.
records.explanation: The physical drive identified in the message cannot be used because the drive selected is not unmap- capable for virtual drive configuration.
records.cause: The physical drive identified in the message cannot be used because the drive selected is not unmap- capable for virtual drive configuration.
records.recommended_action: Replace the physical drive with an unmap-capable drive, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to create the unmap-enabled Virtual Drive (VD) arg1 because either the controller is not unmap-capable or the controllers unmap state is disabled.
records.explanation: The unmap-enabled Virtual Drive (VD) identified in the message cannot be created because either the controller is not unmap-capable or the controllers unmap state is disabled.
records.cause: The unmap-enabled Virtual Drive (VD) identified in the message cannot be created because either the controller is not unmap-capable or the controllers unmap state is disabled.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the controller supports the unmap feature and the controller unmap state is enabled.
To make sure, run the following RACADM command at the Command Line Interface (CLI): "racadm
storage get controllers -o -p UnmapSupport,UnmapState".

messages: The dedicated hot-spare drive arg1 is no longer useful for the arg2 Virtual Drive (VD) because the unmap state of the VD is currently enabled.
records.explanation: The dedicated hot-spare drive identified in the message is no longer useful for the Virtual Drive (VD) because the unmap state of the VD is currently enabled.
records.cause: The dedicated hot-spare drive identified in the message is no longer useful for the Virtual Drive (VD) because the unmap state of the VD is currently enabled.
records.recommended_action: Replace the existing dedicated hot-spare drive with an unmap-capable physical drive.

messages: Unable to use the non-Unmap-capable physical drive arg1 for the rebuilding operation.
records.explanation: The non-Unmap-capable physical drive identified in the message cannot be used for rebuilding operation.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure the physical drive used for rebuild operation is "Unmap-capable for VD configuration", and
then retry the operation. To check if the drive is unmap-capable, run the following command at the
Command Line Interface (CLI): "racadm storage get pdisks -o -p UnmapCapabilityForVDConfig".

messages: Unable to use the non-Unmap-capable physical drive arg1 for the copy-back operation.
records.explanation: The non-Unmap-capable physical drive identified in the message cannot be used for copy-back operation.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure the physical drive used for copy-back operation is "Unmap-capable for VD configuration",
and then retry the operation. To check if the drive is unmap-capable, run the following command at
the Command Line Interface (CLI): "racadm storage get pdisks -o -p UnmapCapabilityForVDConfig".

messages: Unable to discover the physical drive installed on the enclosure arg1, slot arg2, arg3, because of incompatibility issues.
records.explanation: The physical drive identified in message cannot be discovered because of incompatibility issues. Some of the issues because of which a device cannot be discovered are as follows: 1) Missing namespace in NSID 1. 2) No namespace is created. 3) Logical Block Addressing (LBA) size is not either one of these: 512 B or 4K. 4) When the Protection Information (PI) feature is enabled.
records.cause: The physical drive identified in message cannot be discovered because of incompatibility issues. Some of the issues because of which a device cannot be discovered are as follows: 1) Missing namespace in NSID 1. 2) No namespace is created. 3) Logical Block Addressing (LBA) size is not either one of these: 512 B or 4K. 4) When the Protection Information (PI) feature is enabled.
records.recommended_action:
1) Resolve the issue by using the instructions provided on the interface (for example, HII or PERC
CLI).2) Else, if a resolution is not suggested by the interface because the interface does not support,
do the following: 2a) Restart the server. 2b) When the company logo is displayed, press F2. 2b)
Click Device Setting > Select the RAID Controller > Main Menu > Hardware Components > Enclosure
Management. 3) If the issue persists, remove the NVMe drive identified in the message, and replace it
with a working drive. If the issue is not resolved, contact your service provider. For more information
about repairing issues in NVMe drives, see the relevant PERC Users Guide available on the support
site.

messages: Redundancy lost.arg1
records.explanation: A virtual disk or enclosure has lost data redundancy. In the case of a virtual disk, one or more physical disks included in the virtual disk have failed. Due to the failed physical disk or disks, the virtual disk is no longer maintaining redundant (mirrored or parity) data. The failure of an additional physical disk will result in lost data. In the case of an enclosure, more than one enclosure component has failed. For example, the enclosure may have suffered the loss of all fans or all power supplies.
records.cause: A virtual disk or enclosure has lost data redundancy. In the case of a virtual disk, one or more physical disks included in the virtual disk have failed. Due to the failed physical disk or disks, the virtual disk is no longer maintaining redundant (mirrored or parity) data. The failure of an additional physical disk will result in lost data. In the case of an enclosure, more than one enclosure component has failed. For example, the enclosure may have suffered the loss of all fans or all power supplies.
records.recommended_action:
Identify and replace the failed components. To identify the failed component, select the Storage
object and click the Health subtab. The controller status displayed on the Health subtab indicates
whether a controller has a failed or degraded component. Click the controller that displays a Warning
or Failed status. This action displays the controller Health subtab which displays the status of
the individual controller components. Continue clicking the components with a Warning or Failed
status until you identify the failed component. See Storage Health for more information. See the
enclosure documentation for information on replacing enclosure components and for other diagnostic
information.

messages: iDRAC is unable to discover PowerEdge RAID Controller(s) (PERCs) over sideband because of PCIe- VDM channel issues.
records.explanation: iDRAC is unable to discover PowerEdge RAID Controller(s) over sideband because of PCIe-VDM channel issues.
records.cause: iDRAC is unable to discover PowerEdge RAID Controller(s) over sideband because of PCIe-VDM channel issues.
records.recommended_action:
Restart iDRAC and check if the issue is resolved. To reset iDRAC by using a RACADM command, run
the following command at the Command Line Interface (CLI): racadm racreset. If the issue persists,
refer to the Troubleshooting" section in the iDRAC Users Guide.

messages: Unable to perform the prepare to remove operation for the NVMe device arg1 because the NVMe device state is either "sanitize in progress" or "sanitize failed".
records.explanation: The prepare to remove operation cannot be performed for the NVMe device identified in the message because the NVMe device state is either "sanitize in progress" or "sanitize failed".
records.cause: The prepare to remove operation cannot be performed for the NVMe device identified in the message because the NVMe device state is either "sanitize in progress" or "sanitize failed".
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following and retry the operation: 1) Make sure the NVMe device is in the Ready state
before starting the PrepareToRemove operation. 2) Enter the correct the ForceRemove parameter to
perform the PrepareToRemove operation irrespective of the NVMe device state. To view the drive
state, go to the respective Redfish Oem Drive URI.

messages: Detected two RAID controllers in integrated slots. This configuration is not currently supported and the second controller will not be powered on.
records.explanation: High Availability RAID is not supported by this firmware release. This event may occur during the upgrade process.
records.recommended_action: Remove one RAID controller.

messages: No RAID controllers have been detected. Access to shared storage will not be available.
records.explanation: No supported RAID controllers have been detected. Access to shared storage will not be available.
records.recommended_action: Ensure supported RAID controllers are installed.

messages: Unable to install the iDRAC firmware on the server because of a hardware dependency.
records.explanation: The iDRAC firmware cannot be installed on the server due to a hardware dependency.
records.recommended_action:
Ensure that the installed firmware version is compatible with the server firmware version. For
information about supported firmware versions, see the iDRAC Users Guide or Release Notes available
on the support site.

messages: Job creation failure.
records.explanation: Could not create a new job because of a network error or an unresponsive iDRAC.
records.cause: Could not create a new job because of a network error or an unresponsive iDRAC.
records.recommended_action: Retry the action. If this fails, reboot the iDRAC.

messages: iDRAC busy - Delete failed.
records.explanation: The iDRAC communication channel is open and being used by another process; this can be caused by an open session of Lifecycle Controller or Unified Server Configurator locally on the server.
records.cause: The iDRAC communication channel is open and being used by another process; this can be caused by an open session of Lifecycle Controller or Unified Server Configurator locally on the server.
records.recommended_action:
If Lifecycle Controller / Unified Server Configurator (USC) is in use, wait until it has exited and retry
the action. Otherwise retry after 30 seconds to check if network connectivity caused this error.

messages: Invalid firmware image
records.explanation: The firmware image provided by the user is not valid.
records.recommended_action: Provide a valid firmware image.

messages: A TFTP IP address has not been specified but is required.
records.explanation: The firmware update cannot proceed without the TFTP IP address.
records.recommended_action: Specify the TFTP IP address.

messages: Timeout waiting for firmware update process to complete.
records.explanation: Firmware Update time-out occurred.
records.recommended_action: Re-try the firmware update process.

messages: TFTP firmware update is currently disabled.
records.explanation: The cfgRhostsFwUpdateTftpEnable object must be set.
records.recommended_action: Set the cfgRhostsFwUpdateTftpEnable object in cfgRemoteHosts group using config subcommand.

messages: Unable to complete the operation because the catalog name entered has either unsupported firmware packages or same version installed on the server.
records.explanation: The operation cannot be completed because the catalog name entered has either unsupported firmware packages or same version installed on the server.
records.cause: The operation cannot be completed because the catalog name entered has either unsupported firmware packages or same version installed on the server.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure a valid catalog is used which has applicable and supported Windows Update Packages in
the repository.

messages: Unable to roll back the firmware version because one or more features that do not support the Rollback feature are currently enabled.
records.explanation: The firmware version cannot be rolled back because one or more features that do not support the Rollback feature are currently enabled.
records.cause: The firmware version cannot be rolled back because one or more features that do not support the Rollback feature are currently enabled.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the features that do not support the Rollback feature are disabled, and then retry the

continues to persist, update iDRAC firmware to the latest version, and retry the operation.If the issue

support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

records.explanation: A BIOS Update job failed due to iDRAC low memory. For more information, see the Job Queue.

messages: Unable to start or complete the firmware update operation because of internal issue identified in arg1.
records.explanation: The firmware update operation cannot be started or completed because of internal issue identified in the error code identified in the message. Share the SupportAssist log data and the debug logs option enabled with your service provider.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: a) Power off the server and disconnect the power cord. b) Wait for 10 seconds,
reconnect the power cord, power on the server, wait for iDRAC to be fully ready and device to be
available in the firmware inventory, and then retry the firmware update operation. c) If the issue
persists, update iDRAC firmware to the latest version, and then retry the operation. d) If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to perform the Power Supply Unit (PSU) firmware update operation because the PSU redundancy policy is set as No Redundant and one or more sleds is powered on.
records.explanation: The Power Supply Unit (PSU) firmware update operation cannot be completed because the PSU redundancy policy is set as No Redundant and one or more sleds is powered on.
records.cause: The Power Supply Unit (PSU) firmware update operation cannot be completed because the PSU redundancy policy is set as No Redundant and one or more sleds is powered on.
records.recommended_action:
Update the Power Supply Unit (PSU) firmware by doing one of the following: 1) Change the PSU
redundancy policy to A/B Grid Redundant by running the following RACADM command: racadm set
system.serverpwr.psredpolicy 0|1. 2) Power off all the sleds and retry the PSU firmware update
operation. 3) For more information, see the iDRAC RACADM CLI Guide.

messages: Unable to perform the Power Supply Unit (PSU) firmware update operation because the status of one PSU is defective.
records.explanation: The Power Supply Unit (PSU) firmware update operation cannot be completed because the status of one PSU is defective.
records.cause: The Power Supply Unit (PSU) firmware update operation cannot be completed because the status of one PSU is defective.
records.recommended_action:
Manually reseat the defective PSU and retry the PSU firmware update operation. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to update the GPU firmware version because the internal USB port is disabled.
records.explanation: The GPU firmware cannot be updated because the internal USB port is disabled.
records.cause: The GPU firmware cannot be updated because the internal USB port is disabled.
records.recommended_action:
Enable the USB port by doing one of the following: 1) On the BIOS page, set the "iDRAC Direct USB
Port" option to "On". 2) On the iDRAC GUI: Click Configuration >BIOS Settings >Integrated Devices.
2a) Set the iDRAC Direct USB Port to On 3) Run the following RACADM command at the RACADM
CLI: racadm set BIOS.IntegratedDevices.UsbManagedPort On 4) After enabling the USB port, to apply
modified value, create a configuration job and restart the system.

messages: The integrated USB port is currently disabled, which may affect certain GPU-related functionalities, such as GPU component firmware inventory and firmware updates.
records.explanation: The integrated USB port is currently disabled, which may affect certain GPU-related functionalities, such as GPU component firmware inventory and firmware updates.
records.recommended_action:
To enable the USB port, do the following. Else, no response action is required: 1) On the BIOS
page, set the "iDRAC Direct USB Port" option to "On". 2) On the iDRAC GUI: Click Configuration
>BIOS Settings >Integrated Devices. 2a) Set the iDRAC Direct USB Port to On 3) Run the following
RACADM command at the RACADM CLI: racadm set BIOS.IntegratedDevices.UsbManagedPort On 4)
After enabling the USB port, to apply the modified value, create a configuration job and restart the
system.

messages: Unable to update the Power Supply Unit (PSU) firmware because of unavailability of PSU redundancy.
records.explanation: The Power Supply Unit (PSU) firmware cannot be updated because the PSU redundancy is unavailable. This is because of a non-operational PSU or the power redundancy mode is not enabled.
records.cause: The Power Supply Unit (PSU) firmware cannot be updated because the PSU redundancy is unavailable. This is because of a non-operational PSU or the power redundancy mode is not enabled.
records.recommended_action:
Update the Power Supply Unit (PSU) firmware after making sure that the System Board PSU
Redundancy is already set to "Full Redundant" by running the following RACADM command: "racadm
getsensorinfo". If already in this mode, check to ensure that both the PSUs are operational.

messages: Unable to update the arg1 firmware to version arg2 because of: arg3.

updated in the target system inventory and retry the operation. Refer to the Drivers & Downloads

component if not present in the target system, complete the CSIOR operation, and then retry
the operation. 3) Enable the component if disabled and retry the operation. 4) Ensure the Collect
System Inventory on Reboot (CSIOR) feature is enabled. Restart the host device and allow inventory
collection to complete. For more information, see the iDRAC Users Guide available on the support site.
5) If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://
www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze
the collection and recommend a resolution.

the server. 2) Wait for 30 seconds. 3) Reconnect the power cords to the server. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

operation to complete, and then retry the operation. This operation can take a few minutes.

records.explanation: iDRAC is processing a previous reset to default command.
records.recommended_action: Retry after a few minutes.

messages: Error occurred while Resetting to defaults. The Reset status is not available.
records.explanation: iDRAC is not responding to the current Reset status query.
records.recommended_action: Retry after a few minutes.

messages: iDRAC communication failure.
records.explanation: iDRAC is busy and does not respond to iDRAC configurator IPMI requests.
records.recommended_action: Try AC power cycling the server or upgrade the iDRAC firmware.

messages: A firmware or software incompatibility detected between iDRAC in slot arg1 and CMC/MM.
records.explanation: FlexAddress is not implemented in one of the versions of firmware. Please update the firmware.
records.recommended_action: Check firmware versions of iDRAC and CMC/MM. Update to latest version.

messages: A firmware or software incompatibility detected between system BIOS in slot arg1 and CMC/MM.
records.explanation: FlexAddress is not implemented in one of the versions of firmware. Please update the firmware.
records.recommended_action: Check firmware versions of BIOS and CMC/MM. Update to latest version.

messages: A firmware or software incompatibility detected between CMC/MM 1 and CMC/MM 2.
records.explanation: FlexAddress is not implemented in one of the versions of firmware. Please update the firmware.
records.recommended_action: Check firmware versions. Update CMC/MM 1 and CMC/MM 2 firmware to match.

messages: arg1arg2 in Server-arg3 requires a version of Chassis Management Controller/Management Module (CMC/MM) firmware 5.0 or later for using the NParEP (ARI mode) functions.
records.explanation: The current CMC/MM firmware does not support the ARI Mode advanced features available in the network device on the server identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Update the CMC/MM firmware to the latest version and to enable access to the advanced features
available in the network device.

messages: Unable to recover the Secure Control Module (SCM) Host Processor Model (HPM) Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) version because of arg1.
records.explanation: The FPGA Version Sync feature cannot recover the FPGA because of an internal issue or unable to find a recovery file.
records.cause: The FPGA Version Sync feature cannot recover the FPGA because of an internal issue or unable to find a recovery file.
records.recommended_action: Update the FPGA Dell Update Packages (DUP) using the Open Server Manager UI.

messages: Unable to verify the Secure Control Module (SCM) Host Processor Model (HPM) Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) version because of arg1.
records.explanation: The FPGA version cannot be verified because of the reason identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Perform an AC Power Cycle operation by doing the following: 1) Disconnect the power cords from the
server. 2) Wait 30 seconds. 3) Reconnect the power cords to the server. If the issue persists, Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: System Controller (SC) has either stopped functioning or is updating a firmware version.
records.explanation: The System Controller (SC) has either stopped functioning or is updating a firmware version.
records.recommended_action: Make sure that the System Controller is functioning.

messages: Unable to update the System Controller (SC) firmware.
records.explanation: The System Controller (SC) firmware cannot be updated. For information about the causes, see SEL Event Data Byte 2.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the SC firmware update operation. If the issue persists, try updating by using a different
firmware update file.

messages: Unable to verify the BIOS image file because: arg1.
records.explanation: The BIOS image file cannot be verified because of the reasons identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Wait for the system to automatically retry the BIOS recovery process. If the issue persists, attempt a
systemcold boot operation. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using
iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual
Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to power on the server because an unidentified cable or device is disconnected. arg1 arg2arg3arg4, may not be fully seated.
records.explanation: The system cannot be powered on because either a critical cable is missing, or the device associated with the SL (slimline PCIe data) cable identified in the message is removed or missing a required SL cable, power cable, or signal cable. This may be a device seating issue or a connectivity issue with a cable required by the device or connectivity issue with a critical cable.
records.cause: The system cannot be powered on because either a critical cable is missing, or the device associated with the SL (slimline PCIe data) cable identified in the message is removed or missing a required SL cable, power cable, or signal cable. This may be a device seating issue or a connectivity issue with a cable required by the device or connectivity issue with a critical cable.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following:1) There is a cable or connection issue. Begin by identifying the issue:1a) Review
the Lifecycle Log for any Hardware Configuration (HWC) events that may be reported shortly after
this event. If the system can identify the cable or component causing this issue, it will report a
configuration error.1b) Reference the System Information Label on the chassis cover or the Cable
Routing section in the Installation and Service Manual (ISM). If the HWC message was located, look
for references to that connection, cable, or device.Else, if the message references an SL cable, use
the SL cable referenced in the message to locate the connector on the motherboard. This will be
used to trace the cable to the end device. Else, if the message references a critical cable, locate the
specified cable path and associated components.1c) If any maintenanceor service work was recently
completed and SWC5012 was not present before this activity, something is likely disconnected in that
area.2) Proceed withcorrection:2a) Disconnect the power cords.2b) Use the information gathered
above to locate the impacted cable or device.Else, if the message references an SL cable, locate the
SL cable connector on the motherboard and trace the cable to the end device. Else, if the message
references a critical cable, locate the specified cable path and associated components.2c)If the
message references an SL cable,ensure that the device is firmly seated and, if it has any power, signal,
and SL cables, ensure they are connected and firmly seated on both ends and there is no physical
damage.If the message references a critical cable, ensure that the critical cable is connected and
firmly seated on both ends and there is no physical damage.2d) Close the chassis cover and reconnect
the power cords.2e) If the issue persists, collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visithttps://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamicto use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: BIOS image Live Scan verification failed.
records.explanation: BIOS image verification failed.
records.recommended_action:
No response action is required. For specific issue-related information, see the Lifecycle Log data, and
then initiate necessary corrective action.

messages: BIOS live scan operation failed because: arg1.
records.explanation: The BIOS image file cannot be verified because of the reasons identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following based on failure reason: 1) Integrity check failed - Initiate a BIOS recovery
process using Dell supported BIOS image file. 2) Server is powered off or POST not complete - Power
ON the server and wait until POST completes and retry the operation. 3) Resource busy or Internal
error - Retry the operation at a later point.

messages: Unable to power on the host system because the cable is not connected on PSU/PUCK arg1.
records.explanation: The host system cannot be powered on because the cable is not connected on PSU/PUCK identified in the message.
records.cause: The host system cannot be powered on because the cable is not connected on PSU/PUCK identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure the upstream power cables are connected, and then retry the operation. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to authenticate the BIOS image file because: arg1.
records.explanation: The BIOS image file cannot be authenticated because of the reasons identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Wait for the system to boot. If the issue persists, attempt a system cold boot operation. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to verify the BIOS image file because: arg1.
records.explanation: The BIOS image file cannot be verified because of the reason identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Wait for the system to automatically retry the BIOS recovery process. If the BIOS Recovery failure
is observed the in lifecycle log data, attempt a direct update by running the following RACADM
command: racadm recover BIOS.Setup.1-1.Else, try running the following Redfish command: /
redfish/v1/UpdateService/upload HTTP/1.1. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection
(TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic
to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to verify the BIOS image file because of internal issues. An attempt to boot the host is continued. Error Code: arg1.
records.explanation: The BIOS image file cannot be verified because of the internal issues. However, An attempt to boot the host is continued.
records.recommended_action:
If the Auto Livescan feature is enabled, the next scheduled livescan will validate the BIOS image file.If
manual livescan is enabled, reinitiate the livescan. If the issue persists, perform an AC Power Cycle
operation.

messages: The selected profile was not applied to arg1.
records.explanation: The profile version must be compatible with the server generation and Lifecycle Controller firmware version.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that profile versions are compatible with target servers when attempting application of
profiles to servers.

messages: The Chassis Management Controller is unable to process data from the server in slot arg1.
records.explanation: The Chassis Management Controller (CMC) is unable to process inventory data from the server in the slot identified in the message. This can happen if: 1) There is a communications issue between the CMC and the iDRAC on the server identified in the message. 2) Incorrect firmware is installed on network cards. 3) Incorrect firmware is installed on the server iDRAC. 4) There is no free temporary storage in the CMC.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following and retry the operation: 1) Make sure the latest firmware is installed on the
network cards and iDRAC on the server identified in the message. 2) Reset the Chassis Management
Controller. 3) Reset the server iDRAC. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR)
report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use
the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: The network communication session between CMC and I/O Aggregator cannot be started on arg1.
records.explanation: The network communication session between CMC and I/O Aggregator (IOA) cannot be started because the IOA did not respond.
records.cause: The network communication session between CMC and I/O Aggregator (IOA) cannot be started because the IOA did not respond.
records.recommended_action: Power-cycle the IOA and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to configure the storage array in slot arg1, because there is no communication between Chassis Management Controller (CMC) and the storage device.
records.explanation: Unable to configure storage array. This could happen if CMC could not communicate with storage device.
records.cause: Unable to configure the storage array in slot arg1, because there is no communication between Chassis Management Controller (CMC) and the storage device.
records.recommended_action:
1) Reset iDRAC by using the graphical user interface (GUI): Click Chassis Overview > Troubleshooting
> Reset Components. In the Reset Server section, from the Reset drop-down menu, select iDRAC
Reset corresponding to the server iDRAC to be reset, and then click Apply Selection. Or, reset
iDRAC by running the following command at the command line interface (CLI): racadm racreset -m
server-n.2) Reset Chassis Management Controller (CMC) by using the GUI: Click Chassis Overview >
Troubleshooting > Reset Components, and then click Reset/Failover CMC. Or, reset CMC by running
the following command at the CLI: racadm racreset.For more information about the syntax and
parameters used, see the iDRAC 8/7 v2.30.30.30 RACADM CLI Guide and the Chassis Management
Controller Version 5.0 for Dell PowerEdge M1000e RACADM Command Line Reference Guide available
on the support site.

messages: Unable to create Profile because the SD card is in Write-protected mode.
records.explanation: The Profile cannot be created because the Extended Storage removable flash media SD card is not in the Read-Write mode.
records.cause: The Profile cannot be created because the Extended Storage removable flash media SD card is not in the Read-Write mode.
records.recommended_action:
Repair the removable flash media SD Card by selecting the Chassis Controller > Flash Media >
Configuration > Repair Active Controller Media in the CMC Web interface. Repairing is only allowed on
the SD card of the primary CMC. If the problem persists, replace the card. NOTE: All the data on the
removable flash media SD card is erased when the feature is disabled.

messages: The requested SecureBoot Certificate Import operation cannot be completed.
records.explanation: The SecureBoot Certificate Import operation cannot be completed because of one or more of the following reasons: corrupted input file (Certificate or UEFI Driver/op-ROM/boot loader file), invalid file, invalid file encoding format, input file (Certificate or UEFI Driver/op-ROM/boot loader file) is not found, the policy that is being updated already exists, insufficient space in certificate store and internal error.
records.cause: The SecureBoot Certificate Import operation cannot be completed because of one or more of the following reasons: corrupted input file (Certificate or UEFI Driver/op-ROM/boot loader file), invalid file, invalid file encoding format, input file (Certificate or UEFI Driver/op-ROM/boot loader file) is not found, the policy that is being updated already exists, insufficient space in certificate store and internal error.
records.recommended_action:
Enter valid parameters and retry the operation. If the issue persists, free some space in the certificate
store by deleting few certificates, restart iDRAC, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to complete the Secure Boot Certificate Import operation because the file size being imported is greater than the maximum file size allowed for importing.
records.explanation: The Secure Boot Certificate Import operation cannot be completed because the file size being imported is greater than the maximum file size allowed for importing.
records.cause: The Secure Boot Certificate Import operation cannot be completed because the file size being imported is greater than the maximum file size allowed for importing.
records.recommended_action:
Import the file by using the BIOS System Setup page by pressing F2 when the company logo is
displayed while booting the server. For information about the maximum file size allowed, see the
iDRAC Users Guide available on the support site.

messages: Unable to authenticate System Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) or CPLD either because of unsuccessful cryptographic authentication or integrity issue.
records.explanation: System FPGA or CPLD cannot be authenticated either because of unsuccessful cryptographic authentication or integrity issue.
records.cause: System FPGA or CPLD cannot be authenticated either because of unsuccessful cryptographic authentication or integrity issue.
records.recommended_action:
Update the System FPGA or CPLD version either by using UEFI or host Operating System, Lifecycle
Controller User Interface, or iDRAC by using the latest Update Package. The host server will be
unavailable until the update operation is complete.

messages: Unable to authenticate System Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) or CPLD either because of unsuccessful cryptographic authentication or integrity issue.
records.explanation: System FPGA or CPLD cannot be authenticated either because of unsuccessful cryptographic authentication or integrity issue.
records.cause: System FPGA or CPLD cannot be authenticated either because of unsuccessful cryptographic authentication or integrity issue.
records.recommended_action:
Recover System FPGA or CPLD by using RACADM command in either remote, local, or firmware
mode. To recover, run the following RACADM command at the Command Line Interface (CLI):
racadm recover CPLD.Embedded.1Alternatively, update the System FPGA or CPLD version either
by using UEFI or host Operating System, Lifecycle Controller User Interface, or iDRAC by using the
latest Update Package. The host server will be unavailable until the recovery or update operation is
complete.

messages: Unable to complete the System Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) or CPLD auto-recovery operation because of an internal error.
records.explanation: One or more System FPGAs or CPLDs could not be authenticated either because of unsuccessful cryptographic authentication or integrity issue. iDRAC was unable to automatically recover them because of an internal error.
records.recommended_action:
Recover System FPGA or CPLD by using RACADM command in either remote, local, or firmware
mode. To recover, run the following RACADM command at the Command Line Interface (CLI):
racadm recover CPLD.Embedded.1. Alternatively, update the System FPGA or CPLD version either
by using UEFI or host Operating System, Lifecycle Controller User Interface, or iDRAC by using the
latest Update Package. The host server will be unavailable until the recovery or update operation is
complete.

messages: Unable to recover System Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) or CPLD because of an internal error.
records.explanation: iDRAC was unable to complete a System FPGA or CPLD recovery operation requested because of an internal error.
records.recommended_action:
Update the System FPGA or CPLD version either by using the host Operating System, Lifecycle
Controller User Interface, or iDRAC by using the latest Update Package. The host server will be
unavailable until the update operation is complete and iDRAC will be reset several times.

messages: Unable to authenticate the System Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) or CPLD(s) because of an internal error.
records.explanation: The System FPGA(s) or CPLD(s) cannot be authenticated because of an internal error.
records.recommended_action:
Update System FPGA or CPLD and BIOS to the latest available versions, and then perform a cold-
reboot operation on the server. For information about updating the System FPGA or CPLD and BIOS
versions, see the Users Guide available on the support site.

messages: The LOM firmware cannot be authenticated either because of unsuccessful cryptographic authentication or integrity issue.
records.explanation: Unable to authenticate the LOM firmware either because of unsuccessful cryptographic authentication or integrity issue.
records.cause: Unable to authenticate the LOM firmware either because of unsuccessful cryptographic authentication or integrity issue.
records.recommended_action:
Wait for the server to attempt an auto-recovery operation. If the issue persists, update the LOM
firmware using the latest Update Package. For information about updating the LOM firmware, see the
iDRAC Users Guide available on the Dell support site.

messages: Unable to recover LOM firmware because of an internal issue.
records.explanation: iDRAC was unable to complete the LOM firmware recovery operation because of an internal issue.
records.recommended_action:
Update the LOM firmware to the latest Update Package. For information about updating the LOM
firmware, see the iDRAC Users Guide available on the Dell support site. If the issue persists, restart
iDRAC and retry the operation.

messages: The LOM firmware authentication operation is not started but skipped because a LOM firmware update or recovery job is either already scheduled or running.
records.explanation: The LOM firmware authentication operation is not started but skipped because a LOM firmware update or recovery job is either already scheduled or running.
records.cause: The LOM firmware authentication operation is not started but skipped because a LOM firmware update or recovery job is either already scheduled or running.
records.recommended_action: Wait for the recovery job to complete and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to authenticate CPLD either because of unsuccessful cryptographic authentication or integrity issue.
records.explanation: CPLD cannot be authenticated either because of unsuccessful cryptographic authentication or integrity issue.
records.cause: CPLD cannot be authenticated either because of unsuccessful cryptographic authentication or integrity issue.
records.recommended_action:
Update the CPLD version using the latest Update Package. The host server will be unavailable until
the update operation is complete.

messages: Unable to verify the BIOS image file because:arg1.
records.explanation: The BIOS image file cannot be verified because of the reasons identified in the message.
records.recommended_action: Contact your service provider to recover.

messages: Unable to authenticate the arg1 firmware either because of unsuccessful cryptographic authentication operation or integrity issue.
records.explanation: The firmware identified in the message cannot be authenticated either because of unsuccessful cryptographic authentication operation or integrity issue.
records.cause: The firmware identified in the message cannot be authenticated either because of unsuccessful cryptographic authentication operation or integrity issue.
records.recommended_action:
1) If the issue is related to LOM or BOSS card associated with iDRAC, then update the LOM or BOSS
card firmware using the latest Update Package. 2) If the Floating OCP Paddle (FLOP) card associated
with iDRAC has stopped functioning, then to authenticate the FPGA firmware, do the following: 2a)
Update the firmware to the latest available version, and then perform an AC Cycle operation on the
server. 2b) For information about updating the firmware, see the iDRAC Users Guide available on the
Dell support site. If the issue persists, restart iDRAC and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to recover the arg1 firmware because of an internal issue.
records.explanation: The firmware identified in the message cannot be recovered because of an internal issue.
records.recommended_action:
1) If the issue is related to LOM or BOSS card associated with iDRAC then update the component
firmware, and then perform the Cold Reboot operation on the servers. 2) For information about
updating the firmware, see the iDRAC Users Guide available on the Dell support site. If the issue
persists, restart iDRAC and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to start the arg1 firmware authentication operation because a similar firmware update or recovery job is either already scheduled or running.
records.explanation: A new job for authenticating the firmware cannot be started because a similar firmware update or recovery job is either already scheduled or running.
records.cause: A new job for authenticating the firmware cannot be started because a similar firmware update or recovery job is either already scheduled or running.
records.recommended_action: Wait for the current recovery job to complete and retry the operation.

messages: A mismatch between FPGA versions was detected. To ensure proper server operation, update the arg1 FPGA(s).
records.explanation: A version mismatch is detected between the Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Download and install the latest system and peripheral FPGA firmware available on the Dell support
site.

messages: The backplane firmware update did not complete successfully.
records.explanation: The expander or storage enclosure processor firmware update did not complete successfully.
records.recommended_action:
Check the Storage Enclosure Backplane type and the Firmware version and make sure they are
appropriately matched, and then retry the operation. For more information, see the platform Owners
Manual.

messages: Unable to set drive slot offset for backplane bay arg1.
records.explanation: Unable to set drive slot offset for backplane bay identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Check the iDRAC and Storage Enclosure Backplane firmware versions and make sure they are up to
date. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://
www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze
the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Invalid drive type detected in bay arg1, slot arg2.
records.explanation: An invalid drive type is detected in the bay and slot identified in the message. For example, a SATA drive is installed in a PCIe-only slot.
records.recommended_action:
Check the drive type and make sure the drive technology is compatible with the backplane technology
type.

messages: Unable to update the firmware version of arg1 arg2 because of the reason indicated in the status code arg3.
records.explanation: The firmware version of the sub-entity cannot be updated because of the reason indicated in the status code identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the firmware version and device type are compatible, and then retry the operation. If it
does not solve the issue, perform an AC Cycle operation, and then retry. If the issue persists, Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolutionand provide the status code indicated in the message.

messages: Unable to update the IOM infrastructure firmware of slot arg1. ErrorCode=0xarg2.
records.explanation: The IOM infrastructure firmware update operation is not successful.
records.recommended_action: Reacquire the Image file from the source folder, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the IOM firmware. Update Initiation was not successful. ErrorCode=0xarg1.
records.explanation: The IOM firmware update operation was not successful. Unable to initiate the Update process.
records.recommended_action: Retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the iDRAC firmware on the server in slot arg1. Transfer is not successful. ErrorCode=0xarg2.
records.explanation: iDRAC firmware update operation was not successful. The firmware Image file could not be transferred.
records.recommended_action: Make sure the iDRAC firmware Image file is available in the given path and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the iDRAC firmware on the server in slot arg1. The Image file is not accessible. ErrorCode=0xarg2.
records.explanation: Unable to update the iDRAC firmware. The firmware Image file is not accessible.
records.recommended_action: Make sure the iDRAC firmware Image file is available in the given path and retry the operation.

messages: The firmware update operation on the iDRAC on the server in slot arg1 is stopped.
records.explanation: The server was pulled out from the chassis during the iDRAC firmware update operation.
records.recommended_action:
Reinsert the server and retry the operation. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection
(TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic
to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: The firmware update operation of the iDRAC on the server in slot arg1 is stopped. The Image file is corrupted.
records.explanation: The iDRAC firmware update operation was stopped, because the Image file is corrupted.
records.cause: The iDRAC firmware update operation was stopped, because the Image file is corrupted.
records.recommended_action: Reacquire the Image file from the original source, and then retry the operation.

messages: The firmware update operation of the iDRAC on the server in slot arg1 is not successful.
records.explanation: The firmware update operation of the iDRAC identified in the message is not successful.
records.recommended_action: Reacquire the Image file from the original source, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the iDRAC on the server in arg1 firmware: ErrorCode=0xarg2.
records.explanation: The firmware update operation is not successful.
records.recommended_action: Reacquire the Image file from the original source, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the iDRAC on the server in slot arg1 firmware: ErrorCode=0xarg2.
records.explanation: The firmware update operation is not successful. This may be due to a problem encountered by the firmware, or because a server was removed during the firmware update operation.
records.cause: The firmware update operation is not successful. This may be due to a problem encountered by the firmware, or because a server was removed during the firmware update operation.
records.recommended_action: Reacquire the Image file from the source folder, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the iDRAC firmware on the server in slot arg1. The firmware update timeout limit is exceeded.
records.explanation: The firmware update operation is not successful. The update process was not completed within the firmware update timeout duration.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to update the iKVM firmware, because of a checksum error.
records.explanation: The process of iKVM firmware update is not successful due to a checksum error of the firmware image.
records.cause: The process of iKVM firmware update is not successful due to a checksum error of the firmware image.
records.recommended_action: Reacquire the Image file from the source folder, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the iKVM firmware, because the Image file was not transferred to the iKVM target.
records.explanation: The iKVM firmware update operation was not successful, because the firmware Image file could not be transferred to the target.
records.cause: The iKVM firmware update operation was not successful, because the firmware Image file could not be transferred to the target.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the iKVM firmware Image file is available at the specified location, and then retry the
operation.

messages: Unable to update the iKVM firmware.
records.explanation: The process for iKVM firmware update was not successful.
records.recommended_action: Reacquire the Image file from the source location, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the iKVM firmware. The firmware update timeout limit is exceeded.
records.explanation: The firmware update operation is not successful, because the Update process was not completed within the firmware update timeout duration.
records.cause: The firmware update operation is not successful, because the Update process was not completed within the firmware update timeout duration.
records.recommended_action: Retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the LKVM firmware, because an invalid parameter is entered. ErrorCode=0xarg1.
records.explanation: The LKVM firmware update operation is not successful, because an invalid parameter is entered.
records.cause: The LKVM firmware update operation is not successful, because an invalid parameter is entered.
records.recommended_action: Retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the LKVM firmware, because the target is not ready. ErrorCode=0xarg1.
records.explanation: The LKVM firmware update operation is not successful, because the target is not ready.
records.cause: The LKVM firmware update operation is not successful, because the target is not ready.
records.recommended_action:
Wait for the target to become ready. This may take a few minutes. After the target is ready, then
retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the iKVM firmware.
records.explanation: The iKVM firmware update operation is not successful.
records.recommended_action: Reacquire the Image file from the source location, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the LKVM firmware, because the Image file transfer is not successful. ErrorCode=0xarg1.
records.explanation: The LKVM firmware update operation was not successful, because the firmware Image file could not be transferred.
records.cause: The LKVM firmware update operation was not successful, because the firmware Image file could not be transferred.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the iKVM firmware image file is available at the specified location, and then retry the
operation.

messages: Unable to update the LKVM firmware, because the Image file could not be accessed. ErrorCode=0xarg1.

records.recommended_action:

operation.

messages: Unable to update the LKVM firmware, because the IP address provided is invalid. ErrorCode=0xarg1.

messages: Unable to update the iKVM firmware. Reason = 0xarg1.

records.recommended_action: Retry the Update operation. If the issue persists, reinsert the iKVM and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the PSU firmware, because the transfer of Image file is not successful. ErrorCode=0xarg1.

then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the Active CMC firmware. The Image file transfer process was not successful.
records.explanation: The firmware update operation for the CMC was not successful. The Image file could not be transferred.
records.recommended_action:

then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the Active CMC firmware. The Image file was not accessible.
records.explanation: The firmware update operation of CMC was not successful. The Image file was not accessible.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the CMC firmware image file is available at the location specified in the operation, and
then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the Standby CMC firmware because the Standby CMC could not be prepared for firmware update.

messages: Unable to update the Standby CMC firmware.
records.explanation: The firmware update operation of the Standby CMC was not successful.
records.recommended_action: Retry the update operation.

messages: Unable to update the Standby CMC firmware.
records.explanation: The firmware update operation of the Standby CMC was not successful.
records.recommended_action: Retry the update operation.

messages: Unable to update the Standby CMC firmware. The Image transfer process was not successful.
records.explanation: The firmware update operation of Standby CMC was not successful. The firmware image could not be transferred.
records.recommended_action:

then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the Standby CMC firmware. The Image was not accessible.
records.explanation: The firmware update operation of Standby CMC was not successful. The firmware image could not be accessed.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the CMC firmware image file is available at the location specified in the operation, and

messages: Unable to update the firmware of Standby CMC and Active CMC. The checksum process was not successful.
records.explanation: The firmware update process of Active CMC and Standby CMC was not successful, because of a firmware image checksum error.
records.cause: The firmware update process of Active CMC and Standby CMC was not successful, because of a firmware image checksum error.
records.recommended_action: Reacquire the Image file from the source location, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the firmware of Standby CMC and Active CMC.
records.explanation: The firmware update process of Active CMC and Standby CMC was not successful.
records.recommended_action: Reacquire the Image file from the source location, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the firmware of Active CMC. The checksum process was not successful.

messages: Unable to update the firmware of Active CMC/MM.
records.explanation: The firmware update process of Active CMC/MM was not successful.
records.recommended_action: Reacquire the Image file from the source location, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the Active CMC firmware. The Image file was not accessible.
