records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the CMC firmware Image file is available at the location specified in the operation, and
then retry the operation.

messages: Invalid firmware: The uploaded firmware image does not contain a verification signature.
records.explanation: Invalid firmware: The uploaded firmware image does not contain a verification signature.
records.recommended_action: Use a valid firmware image and retry the operation.

messages: The firmware downgrade operation is unsuccessful. A downgrade to the firmware version uploaded is not supported.
records.explanation: The firmware downgrade operation is unsuccessful. A downgrade to the firmware version uploaded is not supported.
records.recommended_action:
Refer to the platform Owners Manual for more information or If the issue persists, Collect a
SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: The firmware update process of Active CMC and Standby CMC was not successful because of a unrecognized image error.
records.explanation: The firmware update process of Active CMC and Standby CMC was not successful because of a unrecognized image error.
records.cause: The firmware update process of Active CMC and Standby CMC was not successful because of a unrecognized image error.
records.recommended_action: Obtain a valid firmware image from your service provider and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to downgrade the firmware version because the current hardware configuration does not support rollback to the earlier firmware version.
records.explanation: The firmware version selected for rollback does not support the current chassis hardware configuration.
records.cause: Unable to downgrade the firmware version because the current hardware configuration does not support rollback to the earlier firmware version.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that firmware version selected for rollback is supported for the current hardware
configuration, such as I/O modules, PSU modules, and servers. For example, a newer generation PSU
may not work with an earlier iDRAC or CMC firmware. For more information, see the platform Owners
Manual or CMC or iDRAC Release Notes for details.

messages: The firmware image file uploaded to Chassis Management Controller (CMC) does not match the current hardware.
records.explanation: The firmware image file uploaded to Chassis Management Controller (CMC) does not match the current hardware.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the compatible firmware image file is uploaded and retry the operation. For information
about the compatible hardware to be used with CMC version, see the Chassis Management Controller
Users Guide available at the support site.

messages: Unable to update the I/O Aggregator (IOA) firmware because of an issue in the network communication session between CMC and IOA in slot arg1.
records.explanation: The IOA firmware cannot be updated because of an issue in the network communication session between CMC and IOA.
records.cause: The IOA firmware cannot be updated because of an issue in the network communication session between CMC and IOA.
records.recommended_action: Power-cycle the IOA and if the firmware version is unchanged, retry the firmware update operation.

messages: Unable to update the Chassis Management Controller (CMC) firmware version because of an internal error.
records.explanation: The CMC firmware cannot be updated because of an internal error.
records.recommended_action: Perform Reset operation on Chassis Management Controller (CMC) and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update the firmware of controller in slot arg1 because the firmware image file is corrupted.
records.explanation: The firmware of controller in the slot identified in the message cannot be updated because the firmware image file is corrupted. For example, the task to verify Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) or signature is unsuccessful.
records.cause: The firmware of controller in the slot identified in the message cannot be updated because the firmware image file is corrupted. For example, the task to verify Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) or signature is unsuccessful.
records.recommended_action:
Download the firmware image file again and retry the operation. For more information, see the iDRAC
Users Guide available on the support site.

messages: The controller in slot arg1 is unable to update the firmware version because of a Flash Programming error.
records.explanation: The controller in slot identified in the message is unable to update the firmware version because of a Flash Programming error.
records.cause: The controller in slot identified in the message is unable to update the firmware version because of a Flash Programming error.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation. If the issues persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using
iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual
Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to update the firmware of controller in slot arg1 because of pinned cached data.
records.explanation: The firmware of controller in the slot identified in the message cannot be updated because of pinned cached data.
records.cause: The firmware of controller in the slot identified in the message cannot be updated because of pinned cached data.
records.recommended_action:
Resolve the pinned cache and retry the operation. For more information, see the Controller Users
Guide available on the support site.

messages: The firmware of the arg1 is either pending activation or initiating an offline activation.
records.explanation: The firmware of the controller identified in the message is either pending activation or initiating an offline activation.
records.recommended_action: Restart the server to complete any pending firmware activation.

messages: The Controller in slot arg1 has converted the firmware activation operation to an offline activation.
records.explanation: The Controller in slot identified in the message has converted the firmware activation operation to an offline activation.
records.recommended_action:
Reset the server and resolve the pinned cache issue to complete the firmware activation process.
To reset the server, on the iDRAC GUI, click Configuration > Power Management > Power Control
> Power Cycle System (cold boot). Else, run the RACADM command at the Command Line Interface
(CLI): racadm serveraction powercycle. For more information, see the Controller Users Guide available
on the support site.

messages: The Controller in slot arg1 is unable to complete the Firmware Online Activation operation because one of the firmware components require an offline activation.
records.explanation: The Controller in slot identified in the message is unable to complete the Firmware Online Activation operation because one of the firmware components require an offline activation.
records.cause: The Controller in slot identified in the message is unable to complete the Firmware Online Activation operation because one of the firmware components require an offline activation.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation by using an offline activation method. For more information, see the Controller
Users Guide available on the support site.

messages: Unable to activate the firmware because the controller in slot arg1requires a server power-cycle to be completed.
records.explanation: The firmware cannot be activated because the controller in slot identified in the message requires a server power-cycle to be completed.
records.cause: The firmware cannot be activated because the controller in slot identified in the message requires a server power-cycle to be completed.
records.recommended_action: Reseat the power cable of the server to perform an AC power-cycle operation.

messages: Unable to set the value for arg1
records.explanation: The operation did not complete successfully because of incorrect parameters or internal firmware issues.
records.cause: The operation did not complete successfully because of incorrect parameters or internal firmware issues.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation. If the issue persists, do one of the following: 1) verify the value being set is
correct, 2) reset the iDRAC.

messages: Resource allocation failure.
records.explanation: The operation could not complete because of an internal resource allocation issue with the firmware.
records.recommended_action: Reset the iDRAC and retry the operation.

messages: The Server Configuration Profile for import configuration is not compliant with schema nesting checks.
records.explanation: The Server Configuration Profile for the import configuration operation is not compliant with schema nesting checks. Only RAID controllers can have nested Component nodes up to a maximum nesting depth of three.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the Server Configuration Profile is compliant with the system configuration schema
published on delltechcenter.com/lc in the LC profile Schema Guide. Only RAID controllers can have
nested Component nodes.

messages: Input file for import configuration operation cannot be found or opened.
records.explanation: An internal error occurred opening the input configuration XML file. An iDRAC reset is required.
records.recommended_action: Reset iDRAC and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to complete the diagnostics operation because the required Dell Diagnostics firmware package is not installed.
records.explanation: The required Dell Diagnostics firmware package is not installed or cannot be found in the iDRAC internal storage.
records.cause: Unable to complete the diagnostics operation because the required Dell Diagnostics firmware package is not installed.
records.recommended_action:
Install the Dell 64bit uEFI Diagnostics firmware package, and then retry the operation. The Dell
Diagnostics can be installed using the Dell 64bit uEFI Diagnostics Dell Update Package (DUP).

messages: The power cord sensor is non-functional.
records.explanation: The power cord sensor becomes non-functional because of one of the following reasons: 1) The power cable may not be connected properly or disconnected. 2) The power cord sensor in the power supply unit has failed. However, the power supply unit may still function. 3) There is an input power failure.
records.cause: The power cord sensor becomes non-functional because of one of the following reasons: 1) The power cable may not be connected properly or disconnected. 2) The power cord sensor in the power supply unit has failed. However, the power supply unit may still function. 3) There is an input power failure.
records.recommended_action:
Do of the following to resolve the issue: 1) Reconnect the power cord to the power supply unit. 2)
Replace the power supply unit that has the failed power cord sensor, with a new power supply unit. 3)
Make sure that the input power supply is restored.

messages: Unable to determine the status of the power cord.
records.explanation: The status of the power cord cannot be determined because of one of the following reasons: 1) The power cable may not be connected properly or disconnected. 2) The power cord sensor in the power supply unit has failed. However, the power supply unit may still function. 3) There is an input power failure.
records.cause: The status of the power cord cannot be determined because of one of the following reasons: 1) The power cable may not be connected properly or disconnected. 2) The power cord sensor in the power supply unit has failed. However, the power supply unit may still function. 3) There is an input power failure.
records.recommended_action:
Do of the following to resolve the issue: 1) Reconnect the power cord to the power supply unit. 2)
Replace the power supply unit that has the failed power cord sensor, with a new power supply unit. 3)
Make sure that the input power supply is restored.

messages: The input power supply is not available.
records.explanation: The input power supply is not available because of one of the following reasons: 1) The power cable may not be connected properly or disconnected. 2) There is an input power failure.
records.cause: The input power supply is not available because of one of the following reasons: 1) The power cable may not be connected properly or disconnected. 2) There is an input power failure.
records.recommended_action:
Do of the following to resolve the issue: 1) Reconnect the power cord to the power supply unit. 2)
Make sure that the input power supply is restored.

messages: Unable to expose the OS Collector to the server OS.
records.explanation: The OS collector cannot be exposed to the host server because of communication issues between the iDRAC and server OS.
records.cause: The OS collector cannot be exposed to the host server because of communication issues between the iDRAC and server OS.
records.recommended_action: Do the following: 1) Retry the operation. 2) If the issue persists, restart the iDRAC and server OS.

messages: Unable to retrieve the TTY Log because another operation is in progress on the RAID controller.
records.explanation: The TTY Log cannot be retrieved because another operation is in progress on the RAID controller.
records.cause: The TTY Log cannot be retrieved because another operation is in progress on the RAID controller.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) View the job queue and make sure all jobs are in a completed state. 2) Retry the
operation.

messages: There was an issue retrieving Hardware data.
records.explanation: There was an issue retrieving Hardware data from the iDRAC internal storage. This may be because Collect System Inventory on Restart (CSIOR) feature is disabled and has never executed or the iDRAC Remote Services API status may not be in the Ready state.
records.cause: There was an issue retrieving Hardware data from the iDRAC internal storage. This may be because Collect System Inventory on Restart (CSIOR) feature is disabled and has never executed or the iDRAC Remote Services API status may not be in the Ready state.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure the Collect System Inventory on Restart (CSIOR) is enabled and has run at least
once before retrying this operation. For remote web services API access, make sure the
GetRemoteServicesAPIStatus method returns Ready status before trying this operation. If the issue
persists, reset iDRAC and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to export TTY log data because the storage controller present in the server does not support the feature.
records.explanation: Unable to export TTY log data because the storage controller present in the server does not support the feature.
records.cause: Unable to export TTY log data because the storage controller present in the server does not support the feature.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that at least one storage controller is present in the server that supports the TTY log
feature, and then retry the operation.

messages: There was an issue encountered when attempted to export TTY Log data for the storage controller arg1.
records.explanation: The TTY log data of the storage controller identified in the message cannot be exported because an issue was encountered while communicating with the controller.
records.cause: The TTY log data of the storage controller identified in the message cannot be exported because an issue was encountered while communicating with the controller.
records.recommended_action:
While exporting the TTY log, make sure that the server is not in BIOS POST, and then retry
the operation. Use GetRemoteServicesAPIStatus() invoke method and check for output parameter
RTStatus and ensure it shows 0 (ready status) and then retry the operation. If the issue persists,
reset iDRAC, and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to communicate with internal iDRAC memory.
records.explanation: An internal iDRAC memory component is unresponsive.
records.recommended_action:
The iDRAC requires an AC power cycle. Do the following: 1) Determine a time that the AC power can
be removed and then reapplied to the server. 2) Save data and perform an AC power cycle.

messages: Unable to complete the disk erase operation on the drive arg1.
records.explanation: The disk erase operation cannot be completed on the drive identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Retry the System Erase operation. To retry the System Erase operation by using
the Lifecycle Controller utility, restart the server. When the company logo is displayed, press F10.
Select Hardware Configuration > Retire or Repurpose System, Select the appropriate options under
Storage & Physical Disks, and then retry the operation. 2) If the issue persists, erase the drive
manually.

messages: Unable to perform the drive erase operation because compatible drives are not found.
records.explanation: The drive erase operation cannot be performed because compatible drives are not found.
records.cause: The drive erase operation cannot be performed because compatible drives are not found.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the drive supports the erase operation by running the RACADM command at the
Command Line Interface (CLI): racadm storage get pdisks -o. The "SystemEraseCapability" field must
indicate "SecureErasePD" or "OverwritePD".

messages: Unable to perform the drive erase operation for arg1 because the drive is part of a configuration that has both internal and external drives.
records.explanation: The drive erase operation cannot be performed on the drive identified in the message because the drive is part of a configuration that has both internal and external drives.
records.cause: The drive erase operation cannot be performed on the drive identified in the message because the drive is part of a configuration that has both internal and external drives.
records.recommended_action:
Delete the mixed configuration that the drive is part of by running the RACADM command at the
command line prompt: "racadm storage deletevd:". Then perform the disk erase operation for the
drive.

messages: arg1 Refer to error message ID: arg2.
records.explanation: An event is logged in the IPMI System Event Log (SEL) for a sensor not specifically monitored by Open Manage Server Administrator (OMSA). For more information about the error message ID identified in the message, see the Event and Error Message Reference Guide available on the support site.
records.recommended_action:
For more information about the error message ID identified in the message, see the Event and Error
Message Reference Guide for Servers available on the support site.

messages: arg1 Refer to error message ID: arg2.
records.explanation: A critical event is logged in the IPMI System Event Log (SEL) for a sensor not specifically monitored by Open Manage Server Administrator (OMSA). For more information about the error message ID identified in the message, see the Event and Error Message Reference Guide available on the support site.
records.recommended_action:
For more information about the error message ID identified in the message, see the Event and Error
Message Reference Guide for Servers available on the support site.

messages: Unable to update the firmware version because of one or more missing firmware update prerequisites.
records.explanation: The firmware version cannot be updated because of one or more missing firmware update prerequisites.
records.cause: The firmware version cannot be updated because of one or more missing firmware update prerequisites.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the prerequisite firmwares are installed, and then retry updating the firmware. For
information about prerequisite firmware, see the iDRAC Users Guide available on the support site.

messages: Unable to apply the firmware file arg1 because one or more missing firmware update prerequisites.
records.explanation: The file identified in the message cannot be applied because of one or more missing firmware update prerequisites.
records.cause: The file identified in the message cannot be applied because of one or more missing firmware update prerequisites.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the prerequisite firmware updates are installed, and then retry updating the firmware.
For information about prerequisite firmware, see the iDRAC Users Guide available on the support site.

messages: Unable to apply the firmware file arg1 because the firmware update prerequisite arg2 is not installed.
records.explanation: The file identified in the message cannot be applied because the firmware update prerequisite identified in the message is not installed.
records.cause: The file identified in the message cannot be applied because the firmware update prerequisite identified in the message is not installed.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the firmware prerequisite identified in the message is installed, and then retry updating
the firmware. For information about prerequisite firmware, see the iDRAC Users Guide available on the
support site.

messages: Unable to perform system erase of NVDIMM because there are no Non Volatile memory devices in the system.
records.explanation: NVDIMM erase operation was unsuccessful. This may be because of non volatile memory devices not present in the system.
records.cause: NVDIMM erase operation was unsuccessful. This may be because of non volatile memory devices not present in the system.
records.recommended_action:
Ensure NVDIMM(s) are present and then retry the System Erase operation with only NVDIMM option
selected.

messages: Unable to upload the firmware image because the file extension is not supported.
records.explanation: The operation cannot be completed because the uploaded firmware image file extension is not supported.
records.cause: The operation cannot be completed because the uploaded firmware image file extension is not supported.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure to use a valid firmware image and retry the operation. For information about the supported
file extension types, see the Redfish Users Guide available on the support site.

messages: Unable to retrieve the BIOS configuration data either because the system inventory is not collected, Lifecycle Controller Wipe operation is performed, or because of a system error.
records.explanation: The BIOS configuration data cannot be retrieved either because the system inventory is not collected, Lifecycle Controller Wipe operation is performed, or because of a system error.
records.cause: The BIOS configuration data cannot be retrieved either because the system inventory is not collected, Lifecycle Controller Wipe operation is performed, or because of a system error.
records.recommended_action:
Enable the Lifecycle Controller CSIOR (Collect System Inventory on Restart) feature, collect the
system inventory, and then retry the operation. To enable CSIOR and Lifecycle Controller respectively
perform the PATCH operation for these attributes on the Redfish OemAttributes URL.

messages: Unable to reset the Secure Boot keys because the installed BIOS version does not support the operation.
records.explanation: The Secure Boot keys cannot be reset because the installed BIOS version does not support the operation.
records.cause: The Secure Boot keys cannot be reset because the installed BIOS version does not support the operation.
records.recommended_action:
Update the BIOS to the latest version and retry the operation. For information about updating BIOS,
see the iDRAC Users Guide available on the support site.

messages: Unable to complete the operation because the Secure Boot policy is set to Standard.
records.explanation: The operation cannot be completed because the Secure Boot policy is set to Standard.
records.cause: The operation cannot be completed because the Secure Boot policy is set to Standard.
records.recommended_action:
Reset the Secure Boot policy to Custom by performing the PATCH operation for the
SecureBootPolicy attribute on the Redfish Bios URL.

messages: Unable to reset data for one or more DPUs.
records.explanation: The DPU data cannot be reset.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following and retry the operation; 1) Review the Lifecycle Controller (lifecycle?) log for related
update configuration or collection job errors, 2) Reset the DPU and retry the System Erase operation,
3) If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://
www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze
the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to power on the server because one or more iDRAC jobs are in pending state.
records.explanation: The server cannot be powered on because one or more iDRAC jobs are in pending state.
records.cause: The server cannot be powered on because one or more iDRAC jobs are in pending state.
records.recommended_action: Either wait for the iDRAC jobs to get completed or delete the jobs and then restart iDRAC.

messages: The memory module temperature has exceeded the warning threshold value.
records.explanation: The memory module temperature has exceeded the warning threshold value.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Verify if the system inlet temperature is within the operational range. 2) If the
fans are not rotating at maximum speed, apply the Fan Max Offset setting in iDRAC. 3) If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to update the firmware of arg1 because of a timeout issue while waiting for the device to update its backup firmware copy.
records.explanation: The firmware identified in the message cannot be updated because of a timeout issue while waiting for the device to update its backup firmware copy.
records.cause: The firmware identified in the message cannot be updated because of a timeout issue while waiting for the device to update its backup firmware copy.
records.recommended_action:
Perform an AC Power Cycle operation and retry the firmware update operation. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: The firmware version of arg1 Microcontroller Unit (MCU) is updated.
records.explanation: The firmware version of Microcontroller Unit (MCU) identified in the message is updated.
records.recommended_action:
Power cycle the system to make the updated version of Microcontroller Unit (MCU) firmware
effective.

messages: Unable to import the configuration properties of chassis because the input XML file for importing chassis configuration is not compliant with the schema nesting check parameters.
records.explanation: The configuration properties of chassis cannot be imported because the input XML file for importing chassis configuration is not compliant with the schema nesting check parameters. Only RAID controllers can have nested Component nodes.
records.cause: The configuration properties of chassis cannot be imported because the input XML file for importing chassis configuration is not compliant with the schema nesting check parameters. Only RAID controllers can have nested Component nodes.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the XML file schema used for chassis configuration is compliant with the schema
defined in the Lifecycle Controller XML Schema Guide on the Tech Center support site.

messages: The server is currently ignoring the fan speed limit by enabling the Sound Cap thermal profile because of ambient temperature.
records.explanation: The server is currently ignoring the fan speed limit by enabling the Sound Cap thermal profile because of the ambient temperature.
records.cause: The server is currently ignoring the fan speed limit by enabling the Sound Cap thermal profile because of the ambient temperature.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the server is operating within the recommended ambient temperature. After the
ambient temperature reduces to the recommended value, the server will revert to the fan speed
corresponding to the speed set by the Sound Cap thermal profile.

messages: The server is currently ignoring the fan speed limit that is set by enabling the Sound Cap thermal profile because of thermal cooling constraints.
records.explanation: The server is currently ignoring the fan speed limit that is set by enabling the Sound Cap thermal profile because of thermal cooling constraints. The server is expected to reinstate the Sound Cap thermal profile based fan speed limit if the server power consumption and/or power management capabilities allows meeting system thermal requirement. PCIe adapters and storage drives are some sub-systems that do not have granular power controls and may limit overall server power reduction to meet server cooling requirements at the limited fan speed.
records.cause: The server is currently ignoring the fan speed limit that is set by enabling the Sound Cap thermal profile because of thermal cooling constraints. The server is expected to reinstate the Sound Cap thermal profile based fan speed limit if the server power consumption and/or power management capabilities allows meeting system thermal requirement. PCIe adapters and storage drives are some sub-systems that do not have granular power controls and may limit overall server power reduction to meet server cooling requirements at the limited fan speed.
records.recommended_action:
No response action is required. However, if the situation persists, the system configuration and/or
the operating environment is not favorable for this thermal profile. Consider disabling the Sound Cap
thermal profile.

messages: Unable to read system inlet ambient temperature because the sensor is not functioning. An approximation of the inlet ambient temperature is used for fan control.
records.explanation: The system inlet ambient temperature cannot be read because the sensor is not functioning. An approximation of the inlet ambient temperature is used for fan control. Fan speeds may increase as a result.
records.cause: The system inlet ambient temperature cannot be read because the sensor is not functioning. An approximation of the inlet ambient temperature is used for fan control. Fan speeds may increase as a result.
records.recommended_action:

records.recommended_action:

3) Select iDRAC Settings then Lifecycle Controller. 4) Change Lifecycle Controller back to Enabled.
If subsequent failures occur, press and hold the system ID button down for 15 seconds to reset the
iDRAC. For more information on how to reset iDRAC, see iDRAC Users Guide.

messages: Unable to initialize iDRAC because of some critical issues.
records.explanation: iDRAC could not be initialized because of some critical issues. Continuing to boot may result in unexpected power loss because of unknown power inventory and unavailability of features such as remote out of band access, active power management, thermal management, inventory collection, LCD, or system error reporting.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Remove input power from the system, wait for 30 seconds, and re-apply
input power. Turn on the system. 2) Update the iDRAC firmware. 3) Continue to boot. Note: This may
result in unexpected power loss because of unknown power inventory and unavailability of features
such as remote out of band access, active power management, thermal management, inventory
collection, LCD, or system error reporting.

messages: PCIe downtrain is detected on arg1. Expected link width: arg2 Actual link width: arg3.
records.explanation: The PCIe device identified in the message was not trained at the expected link width.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Remove input power from the system, wait for 30 seconds, and re-
apply input power. Turn on the system. 2) Update the firmware on the PCIe device. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to initialize the TPM chip because the TPM chip is not functioning.
records.explanation: The TPM chip cannot be initialized because the TPM chip is not functioning.
records.recommended_action:
Remove input power from the system, wait for 30 seconds, and re-apply input power. Turn on the
system.

messages: Default system BIOS settings are in use because arg1.
records.explanation: The hardware setting identified in the message clears the BIOS configuration. After clearing the BIOS configuration, revert the hardware setting to the previous state so that the system can function normally and any non-default BIOS system setting changes can be persistently saved. For more information, see the System board connectors and DIP Switches or System board jumpers and connectors section in the Installation and Service Manual of the respective server model available on the support site.
records.recommended_action:
To change the system BIOS settings and persistently save the settings, revert the hardware setting
identified in the message to the previous state and then go to the System Setup > System BIOS page
to configure the system settings.

messages: A CMOS battery loss is detected resulting in an invalid BIOS configuration.
records.explanation: A CMOS battery loss is detected resulting in an invalid BIOS configuration.
records.recommended_action: Go to the System Setup to configure system settings, system time and date.

messages: Unable to initialize the iDRAC Shared Memory Architecture (SMA) interface.
records.explanation: The iDRAC Shared Memory Architecture (SMA) interface cannot be initialized. The BIOS will use the Keyboard Controller Style (KCS) interface.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Remove input power from the system, wait for 30 seconds, and re-apply
input power. Turn on the system. 2) Update the iDRAC firmware on the system.

messages: Unable to communicate with iDRAC because of missing interrupts on the Shared Memory Architecture (SMA) interface.
records.explanation: Unable to communicate with iDRAC because an expected interrupt(s) from the iDRAC SMA (Shared Memory Architecture) interface did not happen. messages: Unable to enable the TXT feature because the Virtualization Technology (VT) feature is not enabled on the processor.

records.recommended_action:
From System Setup, enable VT, and then enable TXT. If the issue persists, update the system BIOS
firmware.

messages: Unable to enable the TXT feature because Trusted Platform Module (TPM) configuration is invalid.
records.explanation: Unable to enable the TXT feature because Trusted Platform Module (TPM) configuration is invalid.
records.cause: Unable to enable the TXT feature because Trusted Platform Module (TPM) configuration is invalid.

Go to System Setup > System Security page, select the "On with pre-boot measurement" option for
TPM Security, and click the "Activate" option under TPM command. Restart the system, go to System
Setup > System Security page, and then enable TXT.

messages: Unable to enable the TXT feature because the processor does not support TXT.

records.cause: Unable to enable the TXT feature because the processor does not support TXT.
records.recommended_action: Install a TXT-capable processor and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to enable the TXT feature because a TPM chip is not present.

SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: An issue is observed in the previous invocation of TXT SINIT Authenticated Code Module (ACM) because the TXT information stored in the TPM chip may be corrupted.

page, click the "Clear" option under TPM command. Restart the system. For TPM 1.2, go to System
Setup > System Security page, click the "Activate" option under TPM command, and then enable TXT.

messages: The Collect System Inventory on Restart (CSIOR) operation is not performed during this restart because Lifecycle Controller is not functioning.

messages: Unable to enable the Non-maskable Interrupt (NMI) button because either the NMI button is stuck or iDRAC firmware is not updated.

records.recommended_action: Correct the NMI button if stuck or update iDRAC firmware on the system.

messages: One or more uncorrectable PCIe device issues have been detected during the Power-On-Self-Test (POST) operation.

records.recommended_action:

the device firmware. 3) Restart the server. 4) If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection
(TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic
to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: An uncorrectable Memory Error has occurred because a Dual Inline Memory Module (DIMM) is not functioning.

records.cause: Uncorrectable Memory Error has occurred because a Dual Inline Memory Module (DIMM) is not functioning.
records.recommended_action: Check the System Event Log (SEL) to identify the non-functioning DIMM, and then replace it.

messages: The Power Supply Units (PSUs) in the system do not match.
records.explanation: The Power Supply Units (PSUs) in the system do not match.
records.recommended_action:
Check the PSU types and make sure they are appropriately matched, and then retry the operation. For
more information, see the platform Owners Manual.

messages: Power required by the system exceeds the power supplied by the Power Supply Units (PSUs).
records.explanation: Power required by the system exceeds the power supplied by the PSUs. Continuing to restart the system may automatically turn off the system without any notification.

messages: A PCIe link training failure is observed in arg1 and the link is disabled. The system has halted.
records.explanation: A PCIe Link failure is observed in the device identified in the message and device link is disabled. The system will be halted.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Turn off the input power to the system and turn on again. 2) Update
the PCIe device firmware. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using
iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual
Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: A PCIe link training failure is observed in arg1 and device link is disabled.
records.explanation: A PCIe link failure is observed in the PCIe device identified in the message and device link is disabled.
records.recommended_action:
1) Update the iDRAC, BIOS, and PCIe device firmware to the latest available version. 2) Drain the
Flea power by doing the following: a) Power off the server. b) Remove the power cable. c) Press
and hold the power button for 30 seconds. d) Power on the server. 3) Power off the server, reinstall
each PCIe card, and then power on. 4) If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR)
report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use
the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: A CMOS checksum error has occurred. CMOS is reinitialized.

messages: One or more correctable PCIe device issues have been detected during the Power-On-Self-Test (POST) operation.

Do the following: 1) Check the System Event Log (SEL) data to identify the PCIe device. 2) Update

messages: One or more UEFI network interfaces is not available. The corresponding UEFI network devices are disabled.
records.explanation: One or more UEFI network interfaces is not available. The corresponding UEFI network devices are disabled.
records.recommended_action:
Connect the missing network interface card to the system and enable the UEFI network interface in
System Setup.

messages: Unable to load the firmware from arg1 because of the Secure Boot policy.
records.explanation: When the Secure Boot feature is enabled, the system BIOS authenticates each UEFI driver against the Secure Boot policy. If a UEFI driver does not meet the policy criteria, the system BIOS does not load or execute the UEFI driver and displays this message at the end of POST. The Secure Boot policy consists of authorized and unauthorized X.509 certificates; signed drivers must chain to an authorized certificate. The policy may also authorize hash values of individual UEFI driver images. Users can configure the Secure Boot feature and the Secure Boot policy in F2 System Setup > System BIOS > Security Settings page.
records.cause: Unable to load the firmware from arg1 because of the Secure Boot policy.
records.recommended_action:
If the Secure Boot feature is not desired, disable it in System Setup > System BIOS > Security
Settings page. Otherwise, do the following: 1) Make sure the firmware on the failing device is up-to-
date. 2) If subsequent failures occur, review the Secure Boot Policy Summary in System Setup >
System BIOS > Security Settings page. The device firmware must be authorized by a public key or
hash value in the Authorized Signature Database. The public key or hash value must not be present in
the Forbidden Signature Database.

messages: The Secure Boot policy has been modified since the last time the system was started.
records.explanation: The system BIOS logs this message after detecting a change in Secure Boot policy settings. Such a change may result from user configuration or a system BIOS update. Changes to the following settings trigger this message: 1) Secure Boot (Enable/Disable) 2) Secure Boot Policy (Standard/ Custom) 3) Platform Key 4) Key Exchange Keys 5) Authorized Signature Database (db) 6) Forbidden Signature Database (dbx).
records.recommended_action:
Review the Secure Boot policy settings in System Setup > System BIOS > Security Settings. If the
BIOS was recently updated, check whether the BIOS release notes mention changes to the Secure
Boot policy. If policy changes were expected, no action is necessary. Otherwise, modify the Secure
Boot policy settings as needed.

messages: One or more Corrected Machine Check(CMC) errors have occurred.
records.explanation: A Corrected Machine Check error(s) has occurred.
records.recommended_action:

the issue identified in the SEL that caused the CMC.

messages: One or more uncorrectable PCIe device issues have been detected during the last boot operation.

support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and

messages: Unsupported Small Outline Dual In-line Memory Module (SODIMM) memory is installed on RDIMM memory slot: arg1.

messages: Unable to boot a boot option because the watchdog timer has expired. System will reset.
records.explanation: The watchdog timer is armed before the BIOS boot manager invokes an UEFI boot option. The watchdog is set to a period of 5 minutes. The Operating System boot loader from the boot option is required to disable the watchdog timer after it is successfully loaded, otherwise the system will reset if the timer expires.
records.cause: Unable to boot a boot option because the watchdog timer has expired. System will reset.
records.recommended_action: Check the boot option image and boot loader. Update them to the latest version if possible.

messages: Unable to allocate legacy I/O resources for one of more PCIe devices because the legacy I/O space limit was reached.
records.explanation: Unable to allocate legacy I/O resources for one of more PCIe devices because the legacy I/O space limit was reached. The legacy I/O space limit is 64K.
records.cause: Unable to allocate legacy I/O resources for one of more PCIe devices because the legacy I/O space limit was reached. The legacy I/O space limit is 64K.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following and retry the operation: 1) Remove unused PCIe cards to free up legacy I/O
space. 2) Go to System Setup and disable unused PCIe cards to free up legacy I/O space.

messages: An issue is observed on the Hard-drive/SSD backplane.

(TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic
to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

records.recommended_action:

server. For more information, see the System board connectors and DIP Switches or System board
jumpers and connectors section in the Installation and Service Manual of the respective server model
available on the support site.

messages: Unable to import Secure Boot policy data because the format of the data is incompatible with the Secure Boot databases.
records.explanation: The BIOS cannot accept the Secure Boot policy data from the management console because the format of the data is incompatible with the BIOS Secure Boot databases. Secure Boot policy data consists of a Platform Key (PK), Key Exchange Key (KEK) database, Authorized Signature Database (db), and Forbidden Signature Database (dbx). The contents of PK and KEK must follow the Distinguished Encoding Rules (DER) X.509 certificate format. Each entry in db and dbx must follow the DER X.509 certificate format or consist of a hash value generated by a Secure Hash Algorithm (SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512).
records.cause: The BIOS cannot accept the Secure Boot policy data from the management console because the format of the data is incompatible with the BIOS Secure Boot databases. Secure Boot policy data consists of a Platform Key (PK), Key Exchange Key (KEK) database, Authorized Signature Database (db), and Forbidden Signature Database (dbx). The contents of PK and KEK must follow the Distinguished Encoding Rules (DER) X.509 certificate format. Each entry in db and dbx must follow the DER X.509 certificate format or consist of a hash value generated by a Secure Hash Algorithm (SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512).
records.recommended_action:
Make sure certificates follow the Distinguished Encoding Rules (DER) X.509 certificate format. Hash
values in the Secure Boot policy must be 32 bytes, 48 bytes, or 64 bytes in size. Also make sure
the data for the Platform Key (PK) and Key Exchange Key (KEK) database contain only certificates,
not hash values. If the import operation includes multiple policy objects (certificates or hash values),
determine the failing object by retrying the operation with one object at a time.

messages: The QuickPath Interconnect (QPI) link arg1 of the processor arg2 has a downgraded clock speed or dropped clock because of an initialization error.
records.explanation: The QuickPath Interconnect (QPI) link of the processor identified in the message has a downgraded clock speed or dropped clock because of an initialization error.
records.cause: The QuickPath Interconnect (QPI) link of the processor identified in the message has a downgraded clock speed or dropped clock because of an initialization error.
records.recommended_action:
Reseat all processors in the system, make sure all processors are of the same type/capacity/model,
check for damage, and then retry the operation. For more information, see the Troubleshooting
section in the platform Owners Manual. If the issues persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR)
report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use
the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to enable the Memory Multi-rank Sparing feature because the current DIMM population or hardware configuration does not support the feature.
records.explanation: The Memory Multi-rank Sparing feature cannot be enabled because the current DIMM population or hardware configuration does not support the feature.
records.cause: The Memory Multi-rank Sparing feature cannot be enabled because the current DIMM population or hardware configuration does not support the feature.
records.recommended_action:
Check the DIMM population and hardware configuration to make sure Memory Multi-rank Sparing
feature can be supported. For more information, see the platform Owners Manual.

messages: Unable to initialize DDR memory because no Dual Inline Memory Modules (DIMMs) are installed.
records.explanation: DDR memory initialization cannot be completed because no Dual Inline Memory Modules (DIMMs) are installed. Only processor embedded memory is available.
records.cause: DDR memory initialization cannot be completed because no Dual Inline Memory Modules (DIMMs) are installed. Only processor embedded memory is available.
records.recommended_action:
Populate Dual Inline Memory Modules (DIMMs) in a supported memory configuration. For more
information, see the platform Owners Manual available on the support site.

messages: Unable to configure the requested Processor Embedded Memory mode because no on-package memory was detected.
records.explanation: The Processor Embedded Memory mode cannot be enabled because no on-package memory was detected.
records.cause: The Processor Embedded Memory mode cannot be enabled because no on-package memory was detected.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the processor to make sure that the Processor Embedded Memory mode is supported, and
then retry the operation. For more information, see the platform Owners Manual.

messages: Unable to initialize the Dual Inline Memory Module (DIMM) in memory slot arg1 because of a mismatch in the size of the DIMM installed in the server.
records.explanation: DDR memory initialization of the Dual Inline Memory Module (DIMM) in the specified memory slot cannot be completed because of a mismatch in the size of the DIMM installed in the server.
records.cause: DDR memory initialization of the Dual Inline Memory Module (DIMM) in the specified memory slot cannot be completed because of a mismatch in the size of the DIMM installed in the server.
records.recommended_action:
Remove the mismatched Dual Inline Memory Module (DIMM) module and replace it with a DIMM
of the same size as other DIMMs installed on the Integrated Memory Controller (iMC). For more
information, see the platform Owners Manual available on the support site.

messages: Unable to initialize all Dual Inline Memory Modules (DIMMs) in the system because DIMMs are installed in an unsupported, asymmetric configuration between the Integrated Memory Controllers (iMCs).
records.explanation: DDR memory initialization of the Dual In-line Memory Modules (DIMMs) installed in the system cannot be completed because the DIMMs are installed in an unsupported, asymmetrical configuration between the Integrated Memory Controllers (iMCs).
records.cause: DDR memory initialization of the Dual In-line Memory Modules (DIMMs) installed in the system cannot be completed because the DIMMs are installed in an unsupported, asymmetrical configuration between the Integrated Memory Controllers (iMCs).
records.recommended_action:
Remove the Dual Inline Memory Modules (DIMMs) and install in a supported, symmetric configuration
between the Integrated Memory Controllers (iMCs). For more information, see the platform Owners
Manual available on the support site.

messages: Unable to initialize the Dual Inline Memory Module (DIMM) in memory slot arg1 because of a mismatch in the number of ranks.
records.explanation: DDR memory initialization of the Dual Inline Memory Module (DIMM) in the specified memory slot cannot be completed because of a mismatch in the number of ranks between the DIMMs installed in the server.
records.cause: DDR memory initialization of the Dual Inline Memory Module (DIMM) in the specified memory slot cannot be completed because of a mismatch in the number of ranks between the DIMMs installed in the server.
records.recommended_action:
Remove the mismatched Dual Inline Memory Module (DIMM) and replace it with a DIMM with the
same rank count as the other installed DIMMs in the Integrated Memory Controllers (iMCs). For more
information, see the platform Owners Manual available on the support site.

messages: An issue has occurred during processor Built-In Self-Test (BIST). Tiles Affected: arg1 on Socket arg2.
records.explanation: An issue has occurred in processor Built-In-Self-Test (BIST). The affected tile and socket are identified by the message.
records.recommended_action:
Remove input power from the system, wait for 30 seconds, and re-apply input power. Turn on
the system. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit
https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to
analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to complete the BIOS Recovery process because of unknown issues.
records.explanation: The BIOS Recovery process cannot be completed because of unknown issues. A BIOS recovery process is automatically started.
records.recommended_action: Wait for the system to automatically retry the BIOS Recovery process.

messages: The BIOS Recovery process failed consecutively for three times because of unknown issues.
records.explanation: The BIOS Recovery process failed consecutively three times because of unknown issues.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Disconnect the input power supply to the server. 2) Restart the server.
If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://
www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze
the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: arg1 on NVDIMM located at arg2. The identified NVDIMM module will be set to read only mode.
records.explanation: The NVDIMM module in slot identified in the message has issue because of the reasons described in the message. The NVDIMM module identified will be set to read-only mode.
records.recommended_action:
Remove input power to the system, reseat the NVDIMM module and restart the system. If the issue
persists, replace the faulty memory module identified in the message.

messages: arg1 on NVDIMM located at arg2. The identified NVDIMM module will be set to fully functional mode.
records.explanation: The NVDIMM module in slot identified in the message has issue because of the reasons described in the message. The NVDIMM module identified will be set to fully-functional mode.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the NVDIMM module. For information about replacing, see the Owners Manual on the support
site.

messages: Unable to complete the NVDIMM Save operation because arg1. All NVDIMM modules will be set to write-protected mode.
records.explanation: The Save operation cannot be completed because of an issue identified in the message. All NVDIMM modules will be set to write-protected mode.
records.recommended_action: Install NVDIMM battery and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to update BIOS firmware in the previous boot. (Reason: arg1).
records.explanation: The BIOS firmware could not be updated during the previous reboot operation because of the reason identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to update BIOS firmware because the new BIOS image file used is corrupted.
records.explanation: The BIOS firmware cannot be updated because the BIOS image file used is corrupted.
records.cause: The BIOS firmware cannot be updated because the BIOS image file used is corrupted.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the BIOS firmware is downloaded from the correct support site. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.
