messages: Unable to process an iDRAC request to configure Secure Boot keys because of a communication error between BIOS and iDRAC.
records.explanation: An iDRAC request to configure Secure Boot keys cannot be processed because of a communication error between BIOS and iDRAC.
records.cause: An iDRAC request to configure Secure Boot keys cannot be processed because of a communication error between BIOS and iDRAC.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Remove input power from the system, wait for 30 seconds, and then
reconnect the input power. Turn on the server and retry the operation. 2) Make sure the iDRAC
firmware and BIOS firmware on the system is up to date and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to allocate the Memory Mapped Input Output (MMIO) resources for one or more PCIe cards either because of insufficient MMIO memory space or because arg1.
records.explanation: The Memory Mapped Input Output (MMIO) resources cannot be allocated for one or more PCIe cards either because of insufficient MMIO memory space or because of the hardware setting identified in the message. For more information, see the System board connectors and DIP Switches or System board jumpers and connectors section in the Installation and Service Manual of the respective server model available on the support site.
records.cause: The Memory Mapped Input Output (MMIO) resources cannot be allocated for one or more PCIe cards either because of insufficient MMIO memory space or because of the hardware setting identified in the message. For more information, see the System board connectors and DIP Switches or System board jumpers and connectors section in the Installation and Service Manual of the respective server model available on the support site.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following and retry the operation after each step: 1) Revert the hardware setting identified
in the message to the previous state. 2) Remove the unused PCIe cards to provide more Memory
Mapped Input Output (MMIO) memory space. 3) See the System board connectors and DIP
Switches or System board jumpers and connectors section in the Installation and Service Manual
of the respective server model available on the support site. If the issue persists, Collect a
SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: The PWD_EN jumper is not installed. The BIOS Initial Boot Block code has detected an unauthenticated Pre-EFI (PEI) module.
records.explanation: The PWD_EN jumper is not installed. The BIOS Initial Boot Block code has detected an unauthenticated Pre-EFI (PEI) module.
records.recommended_action:
No response action is required, if the issue is observed in the development phase. However, in
production environment, recover the BIOS by doing the following: 1) Turn off the server and
disconnect the input power. 2) Install the PWD_EN jumper on the motherboard. 3) Reconnect to
the power source and restart the server.

messages: The system is booting from the recovery BIOS image. The recovery BIOS did not receive a request from iDRAC to update the primary BIOS, and therefore system stopped responding.
records.explanation: The system is booting from the recovery BIOS image file. The recovery BIOS did not receive a request from iDRAC to update the primary BIOS, and therefore the system stopped responding.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following and retry the operation: 1) Turn off the server and disconnect the input
power. 2) Wait for 30 seconds and reconnect to the power source and retry the operation. 3) Make
sure that the iDRAC firmware version on the system is up to date and retry the operation.

messages: The iDRAC firmware is corrupted and unrecoverable.
records.explanation: The iDRAC Boot Block code detected that the iDRAC firmware version is corrupted and is unrecoverable.
records.recommended_action:
1) Turn off the server. 2) Disconnect the input power, wait for 30 seconds, and then reconnect to the
power source. 3) Turn on the server. 4) If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR)
report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use
the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: The iDRAC firmware is corrupted and unrecoverable.
records.explanation: The iDRAC U-Boot code detected that the iDRAC firmware version is corrupted and is unrecoverable.
records.recommended_action:
1) Turn off the server. 2) Disconnect the input power supply, wait for 30 seconds, and then reconnect
the power. 3) Turn on the server. 4) If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR)
report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use
the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: The iDRAC firmware is in unrecoverable state and will not be able to successfully complete boot process.
records.explanation: The iDRAC firmware is in unrecoverable state and will not be able to successfully complete boot process.
records.recommended_action:
1) Turn off the server. 2) Disconnect the input power supply, wait for 30 seconds, and then reconnect
the power. 3) Turn on the server. 4) If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR)
report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use
the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: iDRAC is running in an unprotected mode. Do not allow unauthorized access to iDRAC while in this mode.
records.explanation: The iDRAC is running in an unprotected debug mode or running non-production firmware. Do not allow unauthorized access to iDRAC while in this mode.
records.recommended_action: Update the iDRAC firmware or call your service provider.

messages: The UPI topology of the server is degraded.
records.explanation: The UPI topology of the server is degraded.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that all processors or cables in the server support optimal operation. For more information
about related specifications, see the platform Owners Manual.

messages: One or more memory errors have occurred during the Double Data Rate (DDR) memory channel initialization on the memory slot arg1.
records.explanation: One or more memory errors have occurred during the Double Data Rate (DDR) memory channel initialization on the memory slot identified in the message. This can be because of invalid DIMM Serial Presence Detect (SPD) contents.
records.cause: One or more memory errors have occurred during the Double Data Rate (DDR) memory channel initialization on the memory slot identified in the message. This can be because of invalid DIMM Serial Presence Detect (SPD) contents.
records.recommended_action:
Disconnect the input power to the system, reseat the DIMM, reconnect the power, and then restart. If
the issue persists, replace the faulty DIMM installed in the slot identified in the message.

messages: Unable to update the firmware of NVDIMM located in the memory slot arg1.
records.explanation: The firmware of NVDIMM located in the memory slot identified in the message was not updated. The update was attempted on firmware slot 1. Because firmware slot 1 was not updated, the NVDIMM is now using the firmware version on firmware slot 0.
records.recommended_action:
Disconnect the input power to the system, wait for 30 seconds, and reconnect the power, Turn on the
server and retry the operation. If the issue persists, replace the NVDIMM. For more information, see
the product Owners Manual on the support site.

messages: The Dual Inline Memory Module (DIMM) in the memory slot arg1 is disabled because of initialization errors.
records.explanation: The Dual Inline Memory Module (DIMM) in the memory slot identified in the message is disabled because of initialization errors.
records.cause: The Dual Inline Memory Module (DIMM) in the memory slot identified in the message is disabled because of initialization errors.
records.recommended_action:
Check the System Event Log (SEL) or the Lifecycle Controller (LC) Log and re-insert the Dual Inline
Memory Module (DIMM) identified in the message into the same slot.

messages: NVDIMM running from Backup Firmware Image at arg1 .
records.explanation: The NVDIMM located at slot identified in the message is running from firmware slot 0 because firmware slot 1 is faulty.
records.cause: The NVDIMM located at slot identified in the message is running from firmware slot 0 because firmware slot 1 is faulty.
records.recommended_action:
Update the NVDIMM to the latest firmware. If the issue persists, replace the faulty memory module
identified in the message.

messages: arg1 on NVDIMM located at arg2.
records.explanation: The NVDIMM located at slot identified in the message has specific issue identified in the message that sets the NVDIMM to Read-Only mode.
records.recommended_action: This NVDIMM module will be set to read only mode. Replace the NVDIMM module.

messages: The CPU in the arg1 socket is not properly fused.
records.explanation: The CPU is not fused to enable Platform Secure Boot.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Fuse the CPU to enable the Platform Secure Boot feature. 2) Replace the
CPU.

messages: Unable to boot the system because either the backplane signal cable is not installed properly or is damaged.
records.explanation: System boot cannot be completed because either the backplane signal cable is not installed properly or is damaged. When the backplane power cable is installed but the backplane signal cable is not not installed, the voltage level of the backplane becomes less than the expected 5V, potentially leading to data loss and other issues.
records.cause: System boot cannot be completed because either the backplane signal cable is not installed properly or is damaged. When the backplane power cable is installed but the backplane signal cable is not not installed, the voltage level of the backplane becomes less than the expected 5V, potentially leading to data loss and other issues.
records.recommended_action:
Turn off the server and reinstall or replace the backplane signal cable. For more information about the
cable connections, see the Owners Manual of the system available on the support site.

messages: Unable to complete the erase operation on the non-volatile DIMM with serial number arg1 in slot arg2.
records.explanation: The erase operation could not be completed for the DIMM identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to initialize the memory because one or more errors have occurred during the NVDIMM initialization in the slot arg1.
records.explanation: The memory cannot be initialized because one or more errors have occurred during the NVDIMM initialization in the slot identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Manually remove and reinstall the NVDIMM. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection
(TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic
to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to initialize the NVDIMMs because different types of NVDIMM SKUs or controller revisions are installed.
records.explanation: The NVDIMMs cannot be initialized because different types of NVDIMM SKUs or controller revisions (Stepping) are installed.
records.cause: The NVDIMMs cannot be initialized because different types of NVDIMM SKUs or controller revisions (Stepping) are installed.
records.recommended_action:
Turn off the server and replace the NVDIMMs to make sure all NVDIMM SKUs or controller revisions
are same. For more information about the NVDIMMs SKUs or controller revision, see the product
Installation and Service Manual available on the support site.

messages: The NVDIMM in the memory slot arg1 is replaced or removed from a previously configured Persistent Memory (PM) region.
records.explanation: The NVDIMM in the memory slot identified in the message is replaced or removed from a previously configured Persistent Memory (PM) region.
records.recommended_action:
Create a new Persistent Memory (PM) region. For more information about creating a PM region, see
the platform Installation and Service Manual available on the support site.

messages: The NVDIMMs on socket arg1 are installed in an unsupported (configuration) manner. Major Error code arg2 Minor Error code arg3. Data in the Persistent Memory (PM) region may not be accessible.
records.explanation: The NVDIMMs on socket identified in the message are not installed at supported configuration with major/minor MRC code to indicate invalid population. Data in the Persistent Memory (PM) region may not be accessible.
records.recommended_action:
For more information about creating a PM region, see the platform Installation and Service Manual
available on the support site.

messages: The Persistent Memory (PM) configuration information of the NVDIMM in the memory slot arg1 is corrupted because the checksum or the header type is not valid.
records.explanation: The Persistent Memory (PM) configuration information of the NVDIMM in the memory slot identified in the message is corrupted because the checksum or the header type is not valid. The corrupted configuration information has been reset to default.
records.cause: The Persistent Memory (PM) configuration information of the NVDIMM in the memory slot identified in the message is corrupted because the checksum or the header type is not valid. The corrupted configuration information has been reset to default.
records.recommended_action:
Remove and reinstall the NVDIMMs or create a new Persistent Memory (PM) configuration.
If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://
www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze
the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: The ratio of DDR memory capacity and NVDIMM capacity on the socket arg1 is not optimal to deliver the best performance.
records.explanation: The ratio of DDR memory capacity and NVDIMM capacity on the socket identified in the message is not optimal to deliver the best performance.
records.recommended_action:
It is recommended that you reconfigure the ratio of DDR memory capacity to NVDIMM capacity to
a value between 1:4 and 1:16. For more information about reconfiguring the DDR memory, see the
platform Installation and Service Manual, available on the support site.

messages: All the NVDIMMs are disabled because the value of memory capacity of all the installed NVDIMMs has exceeded the maximum value supported by the processor.
records.explanation: All the NVDIMMs are disabled because the value of memory capacity of all the installed NVDIMMs has exceeded the maximum value supported by the processor.
records.cause: All the NVDIMMs are disabled because the value of memory capacity of all the installed NVDIMMs has exceeded the maximum value supported by the processor.
records.recommended_action:
Reconfigure the processor to support the value of memory capacity of all the installed NVDIMMs. For
more information about reconfiguring the processor, see the platform Installation and Service Manual
available on the support site.

messages: The data in the Persistent Memory DIMM located in memory slot arg1 is not accessible because the DIMM is locked and the passphrase is incorrect.
records.explanation: The data in the Persistent Memory DIMM located in the memory slot identified in the message is not accessible because the DIMM is locked and the passphrase is incorrect. Update the Persistent Memory Passphrase to the correct passphrase, or perform a Secure Erase on the DIMM. Secure erase will erase all persistent data.
records.cause: The data in the Persistent Memory DIMM located in the memory slot identified in the message is not accessible because the DIMM is locked and the passphrase is incorrect. Update the Persistent Memory Passphrase to the correct passphrase, or perform a Secure Erase on the DIMM. Secure erase will erase all persistent data.
records.recommended_action:
Update the Persistent Memory Passphrase to the correct passphrase or perform a Secure Erase
operation on the Dual in-line Memory Module (DIMM). Secure erase will erase all persistent data.

messages: Unable to complete the Cryptographic Erase operation on the Intel Persistent Memory DIMM with serial number arg1 in slot arg2.
records.explanation: The Cryptographic Erase operation could not be completed for the Intel Persistent Memory DIMM identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to complete the Factory Default operation on the Intel Persistent Memory DIMMs.
records.explanation: Unable to complete the Factory Default operation on the Intel Persistent Memory DIMMs.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: The ratio of DDR memory capacity and NVDIMM capacity on the socket arg1 is not optimal to deliver the best performance.
records.explanation: The ratio of DDR memory capacity and NVDIMM capacity on the socket identified in the message is not optimal to deliver the best performance.
records.recommended_action:
It is recommended that you reconfigure the ratio of DDR memory capacity to NVDIMM capacity to
a value between 1:2 and 1:16. For more information about reconfiguring the DDR4 memory, see the
platform Installation and Service Manual, available on the support site.

messages: Unable to detect the power loss in chassis because the communication between the server module and Chassis Management Module (CMM) is unavailable.
records.explanation: The power loss in chassis cannot be detected because the communication between the server module and Chassis Management Module (CMM) is unavailable. The Persistent Memory feature cannot save data if an input power loss occurs.
records.cause: The power loss in chassis cannot be detected because the communication between the server module and Chassis Management Module (CMM) is unavailable. The Persistent Memory feature cannot save data if an input power loss occurs.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that there are two working Chassis Management Modules (CMMs) available. If only one
CMM is present, perform a firmware update operation on it only when the server modules that have
the Persistent Memory feature are turned off.

messages: An uncorrectable Memory Error has occurred because a Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) is not functioning.
records.explanation: Uncorrectable Memory Error has occurred because a Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) is not functioning.
records.cause: Uncorrectable Memory Error has occurred because a Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) is not functioning.
records.recommended_action:
Check the System Event Log (SEL) to identify the non-functioning NVDIMM. Remove and reinstall
the Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device. If the issue persists, Collect a
SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: The Complex Programmable Logic Device (CPLD) cannot arm for the Asynchronous DRAM Refresh (ADR) signal. It might be due to Intel Persistent Memory DIMMs failed to initialize.
records.explanation: The Complex Programmable Logic Device (CPLD) cannot arm for the Asynchronous DRAM Refresh (ADR) signal. It might be due to Intel Persistent Memory DIMMs failed to initialize.
records.cause: The Complex Programmable Logic Device (CPLD) cannot arm for the Asynchronous DRAM Refresh (ADR) signal. It might be due to Intel Persistent Memory DIMMs failed to initialize.
records.recommended_action:
Reboot the system. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: The NVDIMM installed in slot arg1 is in critical condition.
records.explanation: This is a critical issue identified during the NVDIMM initialization. The NVDIMM installed in slot identified in the message needs immediate replacement.
records.recommended_action:
Turn off the server and replace the NVDIMM immediately. For more information about the NVDIMM
Health Status, see the product Installation and Service Manual available on the support site.

messages: The Non-Volatile Dual In-Line Memory Module (NVDIMM) in the memory slot arg1 has encountered a transient fatal failure during the previous boot.
records.explanation: The Non-Volatile Dual In-Line Memory Module (NVDIMM) in the memory slot identified in the message has encountered a transient fatal error during the previous boot.
records.recommended_action:
Remove and reinstall the Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module (NVDIMM) device. If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution. For more information about installation and removal, see the Installation and
Service Manual of the server available on the support site.

messages: The Non-Volatile Dual In-Line Memory Module (NVDIMM) in the memory slot arg1 has encountered a thermal shutdown event during the previous boot.
records.explanation: The Non-Volatile Dual In-Line Memory Module (NVDIMM) in the memory slot identified in the message has encountered a thermal shutdown event during the previous boot.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Turn off the server. 2) Disconnect the input power, wait for 30 seconds,
and then reconnect to the power source. 3) Turn on the server. 4) If the issue persists, Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: Unable to recognize chassis type because the Chassis Manager firmware is not up-to-date.
records.explanation: The chassis type identification cannot be completed because the Chassis Manager firmware is not up-to-date.
records.cause: The chassis type identification cannot be completed because the Chassis Manager firmware is not up-to-date.
records.recommended_action: Update the Chassis Manager version to 2.x and later version, and then retry the operation.

messages: Unsupported processors are installed. The processor Thermal Design Power (TDP) is higher than the system power limitation (threshold) value.
records.explanation: Unsupported processors are installed. The processor Thermal Design Power (TDP) is higher than the system power limitation (threshold) value.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the processor(s) by using the supported processors. If the issue persists, Collect a
SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: One or more drives are either in failed or degraded state.
records.explanation: One or more drives are either in failed or degraded state.
records.recommended_action:
To view more information about the issue, go to the System Setup page on the BIOS HII, and then
click the S150 Configuration Utility link. For more information, see the Dell PowerEdge RAID Controller
(PERC) S150 Users Guide available on the support site.

messages: The server detected that a CMOS battery functionality is impacted. This is an expected behavior on the first boot after CPU or arg1 replacement.
records.explanation: The server detected that a CMOS battery functionality is impacted. This is an expected behavior during the first boot operation after the replacement of either of the components identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
To configure the system settings, go to the System Setup > System BIOS page. To configure the
system time and date, go to the System Setup > System BIOS > Miscellaneous Settings page.

messages: A CMOS checksum issue is detected. CMOS is reinitialized. This is an expected behavior during the first boot operation after CPU or arg1 replacement.
records.explanation: A CMOS checksum issue is detected. CMOS is reinitialized. This is an expected behavior during the first boot operation after replacement of either of the components identified in the message.
records.recommended_action: To configure the necessary settings, go to the System Setup > System BIOS page.

messages: The slot in the riser arg1 has partially incompatible routing with the PowerEdge model arg2.
records.explanation: The slot in the riser identified in the message has partially incompatible routing with the model identified in the message.
records.recommended_action: Manually replace the riser with a riser that is compatible with this PowerEdge server.

messages: The slot in the riser arg1 has incompatible routing with the PowerEdge server model arg2. The slot will be disabled.
records.explanation: The slot in the riser identified in the message has incompatible routing with the PowerEdge server model name identified in the message.
records.recommended_action: Manually replace the riser with a riser that is compatible with this PowerEdge server.

messages: Unable to authenticate the digital signature of the CPLD firmware because the current CPLD firmware version does not support the authentication process.
records.explanation: Unable to authenticate the digital signature of the CPLD firmware because the current CPLD firmware version does not support the authentication process.
records.cause: Unable to authenticate the digital signature of the CPLD firmware because the current CPLD firmware version does not support the authentication process.
records.recommended_action:
Download the latest CPLD version from the support version, update the CPLD version, and then retry
the operation. For information about updating a CPLD firmware, see the CPLD Release Notes available
on the Drivers and Downloads page of the support site.

messages: Unable to validate the HTTPS certificate management task number arg1 generated by iDRAC because either the certificate is not of HTTPS type, an incorrect device number is entered, the operation is invalid, or the iDRAC or BIOS version is not up-to-date.
records.explanation: The HTTPS certificate management task number identified in the message cannot be validated by iDRAC because either the certificate is not of HTTPS type, an incorrect device number is entered, the operation in invalid, or the iDRAC or BIOS version is not up-to-date.
records.cause: The HTTPS certificate management task number identified in the message cannot be validated by iDRAC because either the certificate is not of HTTPS type, an incorrect device number is entered, the operation in invalid, or the iDRAC or BIOS version is not up-to-date.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure of the following and retry the operation: 1) The certificate is of HTTPS type. 2) Correct
device is associated with the certificate. 3) Correct operation is specified for this task. 4) The BIOS
and iDRAC version on the system are up-to-date.

messages: Unable to sync the HTTPS certificate arg1 of the HTTP device arg2 to iDRAC because either the iDRAC or BIOS version on the system is not up-to-date.
records.explanation: The HTTPS certificate number of the HTTP device identified in the message cannot be synced with iDRAC because either the iDRAC or BIOS version on the system is not up-to-date.
records.cause: The HTTPS certificate number of the HTTP device identified in the message cannot be synced with iDRAC because either the iDRAC or BIOS version on the system is not up-to-date.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the BIOS and iDRAC version on the system are up-to-date, and then retry the
operation.

messages: There is not even one Double Data Rate (DDR) type DIMM installed in CPU socket arg1.
records.explanation: There is not even one Double Data Rate (DDR) type DIMM installed in the CPU socket identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that there is at least one Double Data Rate (DDR) type DIMM installed in the CPU socket.
For more information about DIMM population, see the respective Installation and Service Manual.

messages: Unable to use the system memory because the DIMMs are populated in an unsupported (configuration) manner.
records.explanation: The system memory cannot be used because the DIMMs are populated in an unsupported (configuration) manner. The Memory initialization Reference Code (MRC) feature verifies the DIMM population in the slots, and then maps out the memory that does not meet the Power-on-Requirement (PoR) requirements.
records.cause: The system memory cannot be used because the DIMMs are populated in an unsupported (configuration) manner. The Memory initialization Reference Code (MRC) feature verifies the DIMM population in the slots, and then maps out the memory that does not meet the Power-on-Requirement (PoR) requirements.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the DIMMs are populated as recommended, and then retry the operation. For
information about correct population of DIMMs, see the server-specific installation and Service
Manual available on the support site.

messages: Unable to configure the system memory interleaving across sockets because the current memory population do not fulfill the Uniform Memory Access Architecture (UMA) requirements.
records.explanation: The system memory interleaving across sockets cannot be configured because the current memory population do not fulfill the Uniform Memory Access Architecture (UMA) requirements.
records.cause: The system memory interleaving across sockets cannot be configured because the current memory population do not fulfill the Uniform Memory Access Architecture (UMA) requirements.
records.recommended_action:
Check the Dual Inline Memory Module (DIMM) population to make sure that Node Interleave can be
enabled. For more information, see the platform Installation and Service Manual.

messages: The NVDIMMs on socket arg1 are installed in an unsupported (configuration) manner.
records.explanation: The NVDIMMs on socket identified in the message are installed in an unsupported (configuration) manner. The Memory initialization Reference Code (MRC) feature verifies the DIMM population that does not meet the POR(Plan Of Record) requirements.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the DIMMs are populated as recommended, and then retry the operation. For
information about correct population of DIMMs, see the server-specific installation and Service
Manual available on the support site.

messages: Unable to recognize the Chassis type because the Chassis Manager firmware may not be up-to-date, and it must be at version arg1 or later.
records.explanation: The Chassis type cannot be recognized because the Chassis Manager firmware may not be up-to- date, and it must be at version 3.x or later as identified in the message.
records.cause: The Chassis type cannot be recognized because the Chassis Manager firmware may not be up-to- date, and it must be at version 3.x or later as identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
1) Visit Dell Technologies support site. 2. Search for the chassis model name (for example, C6400).
3. Click DRIVERS & DOWNLOADS. 4. From the Category drop-down menu, select Chassis System
Management. 5. From the list of firmware displayed, select the check box corresponding to the latest
version, and then click Download.

messages: The value of memory capacity of all the installed DIMMs has exceeded the maximum value supported by the processor, all NVDIMMs capacity are capped under the maximum value.
records.explanation: The value of memory capacity of all the installed DIMMs has exceeded the maximum value supported by the processor, all NVDIMMs capacity are capped under the maximum value.
records.recommended_action:
Reconfigure the processor to support the value of memory capacity of all the installed NVDIMMs. For
more information about reconfiguring the processor, see the platform Installation and Service Manual
available on the support site.

messages: CPU Test Mode is enabled. Platform Secure Boot security is bypassed.
records.explanation: CPU Test Mode is enabled in System Setup. To enable security and prevent the warning message, disable CPU Test Mode.
records.recommended_action:
To enable security, go to System Setup > Processor Settings > CPU Test Mode, and disable CPU Test
Mode.

messages: An unsecure CPU with Platform Secure Boot disabled was detected.
records.explanation: A CPU with Platform Secure Boot disabled is installed. Install a secure CPU in order to boot the system. To allow an unsecure CPU to possibly boot the system, go to System Setup > Processor Settings > CPU Test Mode, enable CPU Test Mode, then re-install the unsecure CPU.
records.recommended_action:
To boot an unsecure CPU: install a secured CPU, go to System Setup > Processor Settings > CPU
Test Mode, enable CPU Test Mode, and then re-install the unsecure CPU.

messages: A arg1 issues occurred during the last shutdown operation on NVDIMM located in slot arg2.
records.explanation: The NVDIMM module in the slot identified in the message has issue because of the reasons identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
During subsequent restart operations, if the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR)
report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use
the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to update arg1 firmware in during the previous boot operation. (Reason: arg2 ).
records.explanation: The component firmware could not be updated during the previous reboot operation because of the reason identified in the message.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the operation. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC.
Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant
to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: System BIOS is unable to fulfill the DIMM map-out request because the request renders the system with no usable memory.
records.explanation: System BIOS is unable to fulfill the DIMM map-out request because the request renders the system with no usable memory. The server cannot function correctly without any usable system memory.
records.cause: System BIOS is unable to fulfill the DIMM map-out request because the request renders the system with no usable memory. The server cannot function correctly without any usable system memory.
records.recommended_action:
Verify the DIMM map-out configuration in system BIOS setup and make sure that at least one DIMM
is physically present in the server and enabled. For information about DIMM installation, see the
respective Installation and Service Manual of the server.

messages: Unable to fully enumerate the Data Processing Unit (DPU) arg1 installed on the server because this DPU was not ready within the specified timeout period.
records.explanation: The Data Processing Unit (DPU) identified in the message installed on the server cannot be fully enumerated because this DPU is not ready within the specified timeout period. If the Operating System (OS) of Data Processing Unit is not booted before the system BIOS PCIe enumeration, the system BIOS will not initialize the additional PCIe functions that would be enabled by the OS of Data Processing Unit.
records.cause: The Data Processing Unit (DPU) identified in the message installed on the server cannot be fully enumerated because this DPU is not ready within the specified timeout period. If the Operating System (OS) of Data Processing Unit is not booted before the system BIOS PCIe enumeration, the system BIOS will not initialize the additional PCIe functions that would be enabled by the OS of Data Processing Unit.
records.recommended_action:
Update the Operating System and firmware of the Data Processing Unit (DPU), and then restart
the server. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit
https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to
analyze the collection and recommend a resolution. For information about updating DPU operating
system, see the User Documentation supplied with the DPU or available on the support site.

messages: When TLS is enabled, insecure HTTP boot without TLS is not allowed.
records.explanation: System BIOS is unable to boot via HTTP protocol (HTTP without TLS) because TLS mode is currently enabled.
records.cause: System BIOS is unable to boot via HTTP protocol (HTTP without TLS) because TLS mode is currently enabled.
records.recommended_action:
It is recommended to use HTTP boot over TLS for better security. To enable HTTP over TLS, 1) Set
TLS Authentication Mode from None to desired mode in Network Settings > HTTP Device Settings
> TLS Authentication Configuration 2) Import appropriate certificate in Root Certificate Configuration
under same page. 3) HTTP boot URI should starts with https:// and configure necessary network
environment. Alternatively, change TLS Authentication Mode to None to disable TLS. However, please
note that HTTP without TLS is not secure.

messages: Unable to perform the NVMe over Fabrics (NVMe-oF) boot operation on the subsystem arg1 because the NVMe-oF host IP address is invalid.
records.explanation: The server BIOS cannot perform the NVMe over Fabrics (NVMe-oF) boot operation on the subsystem identified in the message because the NVMe-oF host IP address is invalid.
records.cause: The server BIOS cannot perform the NVMe over Fabrics (NVMe-oF) boot operation on the subsystem identified in the message because the NVMe-oF host IP address is invalid.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the host IP address is valid and retry the operation. Click System Setup > Network
Settings > NVME-oF Device Settings, and then edit the host IP address, if necessary.

messages: Unable to perform the NVMe over Fabrics (NVMe-oF) boot operation on the subsystem arg1 because the NVMe-oF host subnet mask is invalid.
records.explanation: The server BIOS cannot perform the NVMe over Fabrics (NVMe-oF) boot operation on the subsystem identified in the message because the NVMe-oF host subnet mask is invalid.
records.cause: The server BIOS cannot perform the NVMe over Fabrics (NVMe-oF) boot operation on the subsystem identified in the message because the NVMe-oF host subnet mask is invalid.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the host subnet mask is valid and retry the operation. Click System Setup > Network
Settings > NVME-oF Device Settings, and then edit the host subnet mask, if necessary.

messages: Unable to perform the NVMe over Fabrics (NVMe-oF) boot operation on the subsystem arg1 because the NVMe-oF host gateway is invalid.
records.explanation: The server BIOS cannot perform the NVMe over Fabrics (NVMe-oF) boot operation on the subsystem identified in the message because the NVMe-oF host gateway is invalid.
records.cause: The server BIOS cannot perform the NVMe over Fabrics (NVMe-oF) boot operation on the subsystem identified in the message because the NVMe-oF host gateway is invalid.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the host gateway is valid and retry the operation. Click System Setup > Network
Settings > NVME-oF Device Settings, and then edit the host gateway, if necessary.

messages: Unable to perform the NVMe over Fabrics (NVMe-oF) boot operation on the subsystem arg1 because the NVMe-oF subsystem address is invalid.
records.explanation: The server BIOS cannot perform the NVMe over Fabrics (NVMe-oF) boot operation on the subsystem identified in the message because the NVMe-oF subsystem address is invalid.
records.cause: The server BIOS cannot perform the NVMe over Fabrics (NVMe-oF) boot operation on the subsystem identified in the message because the NVMe-oF subsystem address is invalid.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the subsystem address is valid and retry the operation. Click System Setup > Network
Settings > NVME-oF Device Settings, and then edit the subsystem address, if necessary.

messages: The ratio of DDR memory capacity and NVDIMM capacity on the socket arg1 is not optimal to deliver the best performance.
records.explanation: The ratio of DDR memory capacity and NVDIMM capacity on the socket identified in the message is not optimal to deliver the best performance.
records.recommended_action:
It is recommended that you reconfigure the ratio of DDR memory capacity to NVDIMM capacity to
a value between 1:2 and 1:8. For more information about reconfiguring the DDR memory, see the
platform Installation and Service Manual, available on the support site.

messages: One or more memory initialization errors have occurred on High Bandwidth Memory within CPU in socket arg1. All High Bandwidth Memory Stacks are disabled.
records.explanation: High Bandwidth Memory within CPU occurs memory initialization error, all HBM stacks are disabled.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Remove input power to the system, 2) Reseat all processors and 3) Restart
the system. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit
https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to
analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to allocate Memory Mapped Input Output (MMIO) resources for one or more PCIe devices because of insufficient MMIO memory.
records.explanation: The Memory Mapped Input Output (MMIO) resources cannot be allocated for one or more PCIe devices because of insufficient MMIO memory.
records.cause: The Memory Mapped Input Output (MMIO) resources cannot be allocated for one or more PCIe devices because of insufficient MMIO memory.
records.recommended_action: Remove unused PCIe card(s) to free up MMIO space.

messages: The server BIOS has initiated the cold-reboot operation for a maximum of three times to recover arg1 from the arg2 state.
records.explanation: BIOS has initiated the cold reboot for a maximum of three times to recover the Data Processing Unit (DPU) from its current boot status identified in the message. The boot status has remained the same after subsequent cold-reboot operations and the functionality of DPU may be degraded or disabled.
records.recommended_action:
Update the operating system and firmware of the Data Processing Unit (DPU), and then restart
the server. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit
https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to
analyze the collection and recommend a resolution. For information about updating DPU operating
system, see the User Documentation supplied with the DPU or available on the support site.

messages: Processor mismatch between the Application Processors and the Boot Processor: arg1.
records.explanation: A processor mismatch has been detected between the Application Processors and the Boot Processor.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the Compute Module. For more information about replacing the Compute Module, see the
Installation and Service Manual (ISM) or other technical documentation available on the support site.

messages: Unable to log in to the BIOS Setup because an invalid password is entered.
records.explanation: Cannot log in to the BIOS Setup because an invalid password is entered.
records.cause: Cannot log in to the BIOS Setup because an invalid password is entered.
records.recommended_action:
Enter a valid BIOS Setup password and retry the operation. The system will stop responding after
three unsuccessful login attempts.

messages: The maximum number of attempts to log in to BIOS Setup by using an incorrect or invalid password is reached. The system has stopped responding.
records.explanation: The maximum number of attempts to log in to BIOS Setup by using an incorrect or invalid password is reached. The system has stopped responding.
records.recommended_action: Restart the server immediately and retry the operation.

messages: Unable to log in to the server because an incorrect BIOS password is entered.
records.explanation: Cannot log in to the server because an incorrect BIOS password is entered.
records.cause: Cannot log in to the server because an incorrect BIOS password is entered.
records.recommended_action:
Enter a valid BIOS System password or BIOS Setup password and retry the operation. The system will
stop responding after three unsuccessful login attempts.

messages: One or more uncorrectable Compute Express Link (CXL) device issues have been detected during the last boot operation.
records.explanation: One or more uncorrectable Compute Express Link (CXL) device issues have been detected during the last boot operation.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Check the System Event Log (SEL) data to identify the PCIe device. 2) Update
the device firmware. 3) Restart the server. 4) If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection
(TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic
to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: One or more correctable Compute Express Link (CXL) device issues have been detected during the Power-On-Self-Test (POST) operation.
records.explanation: One or more correctable Compute Express Link (CXL) device issues have been detected during the Power-On-Self-Test (POST) operation. The issue is detected during the current POST boot sequence.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Check the System Event Log (SEL) data to identify the CXL device. 2) Update
the device firmware. 3) Restart the server. 4) If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection
(TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic
to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: One or more uncorrectable Compute Express Link (CXL) device issues have been detected during the Power-On-Self-Test (POST) operation.
records.explanation: One or more uncorrectable Compute Express Link (CXL) device issues have been detected during the Power-On-Self-Test (POST) operation. The issue is detected during the current POST boot sequence.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Check the System Event Log (SEL) data to identify the CXL device. 2) Update
the device firmware. 3) Restart the server. 4) If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection
(TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic
to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Unable to fully homogeneously interleave Compute Express Link (CXL) memory because the CXL hardware is incorrectly configured or has issues.
records.explanation: BIOS cannot initialize the server to fully homogeneously interleave CXL memory together because the CXL hardware is incorrectly configured or has issues. The CXL memory is now operating in a mixed homogeneous interleave mode and may no longer be operating at optimal performance and capacity.
records.cause: BIOS cannot initialize the server to fully homogeneously interleave CXL memory together because the CXL hardware is incorrectly configured or has issues. The CXL memory is now operating in a mixed homogeneous interleave mode and may no longer be operating at optimal performance and capacity.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Check the CXL memory configuration and ensure that it complies with the
configurations in the Installation and Service Manual for your model. 2) Check for CXL event
messages that may indicate hardware issues and follow the recommended actions for those messages.

messages: BIOS is unable to initialize the server to use one or more CXL hardware devices installed in the server. This is because an unsupported CXL hardware configuration is used in the server.
records.explanation: BIOS is unable to initialize the system to use one or more CXL hardware devices installed in the system. This is the result of an unsupported CXL hardware configuration. The related CXL hardware not be used by the system.
records.cause: BIOS is unable to initialize the system to use one or more CXL hardware devices installed in the system. This is the result of an unsupported CXL hardware configuration. The related CXL hardware not be used by the system.
records.recommended_action:
Check the CXL hardware configuration and ensure that it complies with the configurations in the
Installation and Service Manual for your model.

messages: BIOS is unable to initialize the server to use one or more CXL hardware devices installed in the server because of hardware issues.
records.explanation: BIOS cannot initialize the server to use the CXL hardware because of hardware issues.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Make sure that all the CXL memory devices, BIOS, and iDRAC are updated
to the latest firmware version. 2) Check for CXL event messages that may indicate hardware
issues and follow the recommended actions for those messages. 3) If the issue persists, Collect
a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: Compute Express Link (CXL) hardware is not responding via the in-band management interface.
records.explanation: CXL hardware is not responding via the in-band management interface. This will result in a loss of error handling and other device management features.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Check the CXL hardware and ensure that it is supported per the Installation
and Service Manual for your model. Replace any unsupported devices with supported devices if
necessary. 2) Check for CXL event messages that may indicate hardware issues and follow the
recommended actions for those messages. 3) If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection
(TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic
to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: System is no longer configured to use CPU system memory and Compute Express Link (CXL) memory in Flat2LM mode because hardware is incorrectly configured or has issues.
records.explanation: BIOS cannot initialize the server to use CXL and CPU system memory together in Flat2LM mode because the server hardware is incorrectly configured, or the CXL hardware or native CPU memory has issues.
records.cause: BIOS cannot initialize the server to use CXL and CPU system memory together in Flat2LM mode because the server hardware is incorrectly configured, or the CXL hardware or native CPU memory has issues.
records.recommended_action:
Check the CXL memory device and the native CPU memory configuration. Ensure that the devices
comply with the configurations in the Installation and Service Manual for your model. Also check for
other CXL or MEM event messages that may indicate hardware issues.

messages: Unable to heterogeneously interleave CPU system memory and Compute Express Link (CXL) memory together because hardware is incorrectly configured or has issues.
records.explanation: BIOS cannot initialize the server to interleave CPU system memory and CXL memory together because the server hardware is incorrectly configured, or the CXL hardware or CPU system memory has issues.
records.cause: BIOS cannot initialize the server to interleave CPU system memory and CXL memory together because the server hardware is incorrectly configured, or the CXL hardware or CPU system memory has issues.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Check the CXL and CPU system memory configuration and ensure that it complies
with the configurations in the Installation and Service Manual for your model. 2) Check for CXL or
MEM event messages that may indicate hardware issues and follow the recommended actions for
those messages.

messages: The BIOS Field Service Debug (FSD) certificate is installed on BMC, but BIOS is unable to retrieve the debug key from BMC because of internal issues.
records.explanation: The BIOS Field Service Debug (FSD) certificate is installed on BMC, but BIOS cannot retrieve the debug key from BMC because of one or more of the following: 1) BMC is not available. 2) The Get debug key operation from BMC has exceeded the maximum number of attempts. 3) An attempt to set the debug key in BIOS is unsuccessful.
records.cause: The BIOS Field Service Debug (FSD) certificate is installed on BMC, but BIOS cannot retrieve the debug key from BMC because of one or more of the following: 1) BMC is not available. 2) The Get debug key operation from BMC has exceeded the maximum number of attempts. 3) An attempt to set the debug key in BIOS is unsuccessful.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following: 1) Restart BMC and server, and then retry updating the debug BIOS image
file. 2) Update the BMC firmware to the latest version and retry updating the debug BIOS image file.

messages: The UEFI driver of the arg1 (Vendor ID: arg2, Device ID: arg3) in arg4, is indicating a status that it must be configured.

messages: Resource allocation failure.

records.cause: Unable to allocate the resource because of the lack of memory or file space in the iDRAC firmware.

messages: The Baseboard Management Controller (BMC) is unable to communicate to the LCD device embedded in the panel because of connection issues in the LCD ribbon cable.
records.explanation: The Baseboard Management Controller (BMC) is unable to communicate to the LCD device embedded in the panel because of connection issues in the LCD ribbon cable.

the operation. For more information about connection procedure, see the servers Owners Manual
available on the support site.

messages: arg1 failed.
records.explanation: A storage component such as a physical disk or an enclosure has failed. The failed component may have been identified by the controller while performing a task such as a rescan or a check consistency.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the failed component. You can identify which component has failed by locating the
component that has a red "X" for its status. Perform a rescan after replacing the failed component.

messages: arg1 is unavailable because of incompatibilities with the current controller.
records.explanation: The virtual disk identified in message cannot be used because of missing features on the current controller. The features may be missing because they are not available in the firmware version on the controller or the necessary licenses are not installed.
records.cause: The virtual disk identified in message cannot be used because of missing features on the current controller. The features may be missing because they are not available in the firmware version on the controller or the necessary licenses are not installed.
records.recommended_action: Update the controller firmware and license to match the peer controller.

messages: Hot Spare Protection policy deviation with severity set at Warning level occurred for arg1.
records.explanation: The number of hot spares available for the virtual disks identified in the message are not compliant with Hot Spare Protection policy, whose severity is set at Warning level.
records.recommended_action: Make appropriate assignments of hotspares to meet the policy.

messages: Hot Spare Protection policy deviation with severity set at Critical level occurred for arg1.
records.explanation: The number of hot spares available for the virtual disks identified in the message are not compliant with Hot Spare Protection policy, whose severity is set at Critical level.
records.recommended_action: Make appropriate assignments of hotspares to meet the policy.

messages: The rebuild operation on the virtual drive (VD) arg1 is abruptly stopped.
records.explanation: The rebuild operation on the virtual drive (VD) identified in the message is abruptly stopped.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the physical drive associated with the virtual drive and retry the operation. For information
about replacing a physical drive, see the servers Installation and Service Manual available on the
support site.

messages: Unable to activate the firmware because an Online Capacity Expansion (OCE) operation is currently in progress.
records.explanation: The firmware cannot be activated because an Online Capacity Expansion (OCE) operation is currently in progress.
records.cause: The firmware cannot be activated because an Online Capacity Expansion (OCE) operation is currently in progress.
records.recommended_action:

a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: arg1 is not accessible by the host device because of an unsupported ESXi driver.
records.explanation: The virtual disk identified in the message is not accessible by the host device because an unsupported ESXi driver exists in the host device.
records.cause: The virtual disk identified in the message is not accessible by the host device because an unsupported ESXi driver exists in the host device.
records.recommended_action: Update the ESXi to the latest PERC driver version.

messages: Consistency check of arg1 failed.
records.explanation: A physical disk included in the virtual disk failed or there is an error in the parity information. A failed physical disk causes errors in parity information.
records.recommended_action:
Check that all the physical disks of the virtual disk are in a healthy condition. Replace any disks that
are not healthy and restart the operation. If this is not the problem, delete the virtual disk and restore
the data to the disk from a backup copy.

messages: arg1 format failed.
records.explanation: A physical disk included in the virtual disk failed.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the failed physical disk. Identify the failed physical disk by locating the disk that has a red "X"
for its status. Rebuild the physical disk. When finished, restart the virtual disk format operation.

messages: Initialization of arg1 has failed.
records.explanation: A physical disk included in the virtual disk has failed or was removed.
records.recommended_action: If a physical disk has failed, replace the physical disk. Restart the virtual disk initialization.

messages: Reconfiguration of arg1 has failed.
records.explanation: The reconfiguration operation was not completed. This may be due to a user action or a physical disk failure.
records.cause: The reconfiguration operation was not completed. This may be due to a user action or a physical disk failure.
records.recommended_action: Recreate the virtual disk and restore data from a backup copy.

messages: The rebuild operation on arg1 is stopped.
records.explanation: A physical drive included in the virtual disk has either failed, is faulty, or removed. You may also have cancelled the rebuild.
records.cause: A physical drive included in the virtual disk has either failed, is faulty, or removed. You may also have cancelled the rebuild.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the failed or faulty drive. A failed drive is identified by the X symbol as its status. Restart
the virtual drive rebuild operation. If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR)
report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use
the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a resolution.

messages: Controller cache is preserved for missing or offline arg1.
records.explanation: The controller is getting disconnected from its virtual disk, while Input Output (IO) is in-progress.
records.recommended_action:
Try importing foreign disks, if any. Check if the enclosure containing the Virtual Disk is disconnected
from the controller. Insert any disks that are reported missing or failed. If the enclosure or disks were
removed intentionally, the preserved cache can be discarded. See storage hardware documentation
for more information on performing these steps.

messages: Background initialization failed for arg1.
records.explanation: Background initialization of a virtual disk failed.
records.recommended_action:
Run a consistency check on the virtual disk. If that fails, check the health of the member drives of the
virtual disk and then recreate.

messages: arg1 is permanently degraded.
records.explanation: A redundant virtual disk has lost redundancy. This may occur when the virtual disk suffers the failure of more than one physical disk. In this case, both the source physical disk and the target disk with redundant data have failed. A rebuild is not possible because there is no longer redundancy.
records.cause: A redundant virtual disk has lost redundancy. This may occur when the virtual disk suffers the failure of more than one physical disk. In this case, both the source physical disk and the target disk with redundant data have failed. A rebuild is not possible because there is no longer redundancy.
records.recommended_action: Replace the failed disks and restore from backup.

messages: Background Initialization (BGI) completed with uncorrectable errors on arg1.
records.explanation: The background initialization task encountered errors that cannot be corrected. The virtual disk contains physical disks that have unusable disk space or disk errors that cannot be corrected.
records.recommended_action:
Review other messages to identify whether the physical disk that has errors. If the virtual disk is
redundant, you can replace the physical disk and continue using the virtual disk. If the virtual disk is
non-redundant, you need to recreate the virtual disk after replacing the physical disk. After replacing
the physical disk, run a consistency check to verify the data.

messages: The consistency check found inconsistent parity data on arg1.
records.explanation: The data on physical disk members of the virtual disk does not match. Redundancy may be lost.
records.recommended_action:
Rerun the consistency check task. If you receive this message again, verify the health of the
physical disks included in the virtual disk. See the storage hardware documentation for more
information. Review messages for significant messages related to the physical disks. If a physical
disk has a problem, replace it and restore from a backup copy. If the issue persists, Collect a
SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/support/incidents-
online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and recommend a
resolution.

messages: arg1 initialization has failed.
records.explanation: The controller cannot communicate with attached devices. A disk may be removed or contain errors. Cables may also be loose or defective.
records.cause: The controller cannot communicate with attached devices. A disk may be removed or contain errors. Cables may also be loose or defective.
records.recommended_action:
Verify the health of attached devices. Review the Alert Log for significant events. Make sure the
cables are attached securely. See the Cables Attached Correctly section for more information on
checking the cables.

messages: Redundancy of arg1 has degraded.
records.explanation: This message occurs when a physical disk in the disk group was removed or when a physical disk included in a redundant virtual disk fails. Because the virtual disk is redundant (uses mirrored or parity information) and only one physical disk has failed, the virtual disk can be rebuilt. Typically, the virtual disk (E.g. RAID 6) has multiple redundant disks and there is a problem with one of them.
records.recommended_action: Replace the missing or failed physical disk.

messages: Bad block medium error is detected at block arg1 on arg2.
records.explanation: Virtual disk bad blocks are due to presence of unrecoverable bad blocks on one or more member physical disks. Loss of data and/or redundancy may have occurred.
records.cause: Virtual disk bad blocks are due to presence of unrecoverable bad blocks on one or more member physical disks. Loss of data and/or redundancy may have occurred.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following and retry the operation: 1) Replace the RAID controller battery. For information about
replacing the battery, see the hardware documentation of the respective RAID card. 2) If the issue
persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://www.dell.com/
support/incidents-online/contactus/dynamic to use the Virtual Assistant to analyze the collection and
recommend a resolution.

messages: arg1 has failed.
records.explanation: One or more physical disks included in the virtual disk have failed. If the virtual disk is redundant, then more physical disks have failed than you can rebuild using mirrored or parity information.
records.recommended_action:
If the issue persists, Collect a SupportAssist collection (TSR) report using iDRAC. Visit https://

messages: The arg1 sensor has failed with a value arg2 Volts.
records.explanation: A voltage sensor identified in the message may have failed. This condition can cause system performance issues and degradation in the monitoring capability of the system.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following to resolve the issue: 1) Verify the Embedded System Management (ESM) Log
for any sensor related faults. If there is a failed sensor, replace the system board. 2) Re-configure the
system to a minimum configuration, and verify if the sensor displays a normal value, otherwise replace
the system board. 3) If the sensor identified is a processor voltage sensor, remove the processor
module and inspect processor socket, and replace if required. If the issue persists, contact your
service provider.

messages: The FAN module for cooling the Witness Server is missing from the Chassis.

records.recommended_action: Install the FAN module into the chassis to allow cooling of Witness Server.

messages: The Witness Server CPU is throttled.
records.explanation: The Witness Server processor temperature increased beyond the threshold value. The Processor thermal protection triggered the CPU throttle action. Factors external to the processor may have induced this issue.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Review the LC or SEL log data to check if there is any fan failure. If yes, replace
the fan. 2) Else, check the inlet temperature by running RACADM GetSensorInfo command or iDRAC
GUI Temperature page.

messages: The Witness Node CPU has a thermal trip (over-temperature) event.
records.explanation: The Witness Server processor temperature increased beyond the threshold value. The Processor thermal protection triggered the system shut down. Factors external to the processor may have induced this issue.
records.recommended_action:
Do the following: 1) Review the LC or SEL log data to check if there is any fan failure. If yes, replace
the fan. 2) Else, check the inlet temperature by running RACADM GetSensorInfo command or the
iDRAC GUI Temperature page.

messages: The Witness Server POST code failure is detected.
records.explanation: The Witness Server BIOS reported POST code failure.
records.recommended_action:

command. Similarly iDRAC GUI or Redfish options can be found in iDRAC User Guide.2) If the failure
persists, refer Platform Technical guide for Witness BIOS POST code description and take appropriate
steps to resolve the issue.3) If the failure persists , reach out the tech support team.
