messages: 3012 - Enet Module State FAILED
records.explanation: The module is non-functional due to a hardware or operating system failure. VC cannot configure or monitor this module. This error will impact network traffic.
records.cause:
The OA reported the module status as failed. This is due to a hardware failure or operating system
failure. The OS failure could be a kernel panic, memory exhausted, CPU overload, or OS boot failure.
records.recommended_action:
Do not attempt any configuration changes to the Virtual Connect Domain. Recommended corrective
actions:
•  Physically remove and reseat Ethernet module that was indicated as Failed.
If the module continues to be in a Failed state, replace this module.
•  If hardware replacement does not correct the issue:
1.  Export a support package from VC for Hewlett Packard Enterprise analysis.
2.  Capture the output of the OA show all command for Hewlett Packard Enterprise analysis.
3.  Contact Hewlett Packard Enterprise customer support with the previously gathered information.

messages: 3023 - Enet Module state NO_COMM
records.explanation: The VC management application has detected a problem with the communication to the VC-Enet module.
records.cause:
•  Configuration of IP addresses/network topology is preventing communication between the primary
VC-Enet module and the identified VC-Enet module.
•  An unexpected error has occurred while sending a configuration update to the module or while
requesting status information from the module. This error may be due to TCP/IP communications
interruption/timeout or due to a software generated failure.
•  The primary VC-Enet module is unable to exchange network packets with the indicated module. This
inability can occur if the Onboard Administrator has configured the internal switch that connects the I/O
modules inappropriately.
records.recommended_action:
•  Verify that the network configuration (IP address, topology, etc.) is correct. If the module is in a remote
enclosure (not located in the same enclosure as the primary VC-Enet module), reset or reboot the Active
Onboard Administrator in the remote enclosure.
•  Verify that the OA Enclosure Bay IP Addressing (EBIPA) is either disabled or is providing the correct
information to each module.

messages: 3031 - Enet Module IP is 0.0.0.0
records.explanation: The OA is reporting that an Ethernet module does not have an IP address. The module will be marked as NO-COMM.
records.cause:
•  The external DHCP server did not provide the module with an IP address.
•  There is a networking issue with the DHCP server.
•  There is an IO Module or Onboard Administrator hardware or software issue.
records.recommended_action:
•  Verify the OA is set up to provide a specific IP address.
•  Verify an external DHCP server is available on the management network.

event_names: 3101 - Port is disabled as network loop is detected
messages: 3101 - Port is disabled as network loop is detected
records.explanation: Because a network loop was detected on an Ethernet port, it has been disabled to avoid further service degradation. Possible cause 1: More than one active uplink port or uplink Link Aggregation Group (LAG) from an uplink set has been assigned to the same network from the Virtual Connect domain to the external Ethernet switching environment, causing a network loop. Possible cause 2: The incorrect configuration of the stacked links in multiple VC-Enet modules setup is causing a network loop.

records.recommended_action: Administrative action is required to reconfigure the port where the network loop is being reported.

records.explanation: The module is non-functional due to a hardware or firmware failure. VC cannot configure or monitor this module. This error will impact Fibre Channel traffic. messages: 4014 - FC Module State Incompatible
records.explanation: The Fibre Channel module in this interconnect bay is incompatible with the VCM domain.
records.cause:
•  The module is running outdated FW. It might be running either an older or newer version than Virtual
Connect manager expects.
•  The module is not compatible with a module running in an adjacent bay in either double-dense or
single-dense mode.
•  The module is not compatible with another module in the same bay group for multi-enclosure or
double-dense mode.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the module with a module type that is compatible with the bay group of the VC domain. In
the case of an incorrect FW revision, update the module to the correct FW revision.

messages: 4019 - FC Module State is NO_COMM
records.explanation: The Virtual Connect Manager is unable to communicate with the FC module.
records.cause:
•  The VC-FC module is rebooting after a FW panic and is not responding to VCM commands.
•  The VC-FC module is not responding to ISMIC commands due to a FW defect.
•  The VC-FC module fails to start the DHCP client due to a FW defect and therefore does not respond to
commands from VCM to provide the switch configuration, including the FW revision number.
•  The VC-FC module never obtains an IP address through DHCP and therefore does not respond to VCM
commands.
•  The VC-FC module never sends a COMM_OK OA event after a FW reboot due to a FW defect or
hardware problem.
records.recommended_action:
Make sure that the DHCP server is running and correctly assigning addresses. In case of a transient
error, power cycle the module to see if communication is restored. A support dump of the VC-FC module
needs to be analyzed to determine the basic cause of the problem. The module might need to be replaced.

records.cause: This occurs whenever a profile is applied to a server with Flex-10 NICs and the same Ethernet Network is on more than one Ethernet connection that is mapped to a Flex-10 physical function on the same physical port. event_names: 6021 - Profile has PXE enabled on a non-primary Flex-10 NIC
messages: 6021 - Profile has PXE enabled on a non-primary Flex-10 NIC
records.explanation: PXE is enabled on an Ethernet connection in a profile that is mapped to a non-primary physical function on a Flex-10 NIC. The current Flex-10 implementation does not allow PXE booting on any but the first physical function on a Flex-10 NIC port. Possible cause: PXE is enabled on an Ethernet connection that is mapped to the second, third, or fourth physical function on a Flex-10 NIC.
records.cause: PXE is enabled on an Ethernet connection in a profile that is mapped to a non-primary physical function on a Flex-10 NIC. The current Flex-10 implementation does not allow PXE booting on any but the first physical function on a Flex-10 NIC port. Possible cause: PXE is enabled on an Ethernet connection that is mapped to the second, third, or fourth physical function on a Flex-10 NIC.
records.recommended_action:
Use the GUI to edit the profile and disable PXE on any connections that show PXE is not supported
on them.

event_names: 6022 - Profile has iSCSI boot enabled on an unsupported Flex-10 NIC
messages: 6022 - Profile has iSCSI boot enabled on an unsupported Flex-10 NIC
records.explanation: A profile has iSCSI boot enabled on an unsupported Flex-10 NIC. Possible cause: An administrator has incorrectly configured the boot settings for the profile.
records.cause: A profile has iSCSI boot enabled on an unsupported Flex-10 NIC. Possible cause: An administrator has incorrectly configured the boot settings for the profile.
records.recommended_action:
s:
•  Correct the specified profile settings to enable the iSCSI boot on a supported NIC.
•  Remove the iSCSI configuration from profile.
•  Insert a supported NIC card to configure iSCSI boot.

event_names: 6030 - Profile could not be assigned to powered up server
messages: 6030 - Profile could not be assigned to powered up server
records.explanation: A profile was changed or assigned and some configuration required that the server be powered off to make the change. For example, if the number of Ethernet connections is changed for a profile that is assigned to a server with Flex-10 NICs, then the server must be powered off.
records.cause:
•  A user action results in a profile that requires the server be powered off to make the change or initially
assign or remove the profile.
•  VCM restarts and detects a powered on server that has a profile assigned to the bay and the profile
needs to make a change on the server that requires it to be powered off.
records.recommended_action: Power down the server and retry the change.

messages: 9012 - Unknown Module state FAILED
records.explanation: An unknown module has been labeled with a FAILED status. This status is usually indicated by the OA after a module hot-plug insert operation or when VCM is starting up. This condition is usually fatal. Possible cause: A hardware failure or corrupted firmware.
records.cause: An unknown module has been labeled with a FAILED status. This status is usually indicated by the OA after a module hot-plug insert operation or when VCM is starting up. This condition is usually fatal. Possible cause: A hardware failure or corrupted firmware.
records.recommended_action:
•  Re-insert a module of the same type back into the bay that is marked as missing.
•  Make modifications to the domain to eliminate the dependencies on the missing module. Once the
dependencies have been removed, resetting VCM should clear the missing module indication.

event_names: Redundancy has been reduced by the NIC in slot %1, port %2. Number of functional NICs in the team: %3.
messages: Redundancy has been reduced by the NIC in slot %1, port %2. Number of functional NICs in the team: %3.
records.explanation: This trap is sent any time a physical adapter in a logical adapter group changes to the Failed condition, but at least one physical adapter remains in the OK condition. This can be caused by loss of link due to a cable being removed from the adapter or the Hub or Switch. Internal adapter, Hub, or Switch failures can also cause this condition.
records.cause: This trap is sent any time a physical adapter in a logical adapter group changes to the Failed condition, but at least one physical adapter remains in the OK condition. This can be caused by loss of link due to a cable being removed from the adapter or the Hub or Switch. Internal adapter, Hub, or Switch failures can also cause this condition.
records.recommended_action:
Check the cables to the adapter and the Hub or Switch. If no cable problems are found, the
adapter, Hub, or Switch may need replacement.

event_names: Drive Array Physical Drive Threshold Exceeded.
messages: The physical drive in slot %4, port %5, bay %6 with serial number “%7”, has exceeded a drive threshold.
records.explanation: Physical Drive Threshold Passed. This trap indicates that the agent has detected a factory threshold associated with one of the physical drive objects on a drive array, has been exceeded.
records.recommended_action: Replace the physical drive.

event_names: Drive Array Spare Drive Status Change.
messages: The spare drive in slot %4, port %5, bay %6 has a new status of %2.
records.explanation: Spare Drive Status Change. This trap indicates that the agent has detected a change in the status of a drive array spare drive. The variable cpqDaSpareStatus indicates the current spare drive status.
records.recommended_action: If the spare drive status is failed, replace the drive.

event_names: Drive Array Physical Drive Status Change.
messages: The physical drive in slot %4, port %5, bay %6 with serial number “%7”, has a new status of %2.
records.explanation: Physical Drive Status Change. This trap indicates that the agent has detected a change in the status of a drive array physical drive. The variable cpaDaPhyDrvStatus indicates the current physical drive status.
records.recommended_action: If the physical drive status is failed(3) or predictiveFailure(4), replace the drive.

messages: The array accelerator board attached to the array controller in slot %4 has a new status of %2.
records.explanation: Accelerator Board Status Change. This trap indicates that the agent has detected a change in the status of an array accelerator cache board. The current status is represented by the variable cpqDaAccelStatus.
records.recommended_action:
If the accelerator board status is permDisabled(5), you may need to replace the accelerator
board.

messages: The array accelerator board attached to the array controller in slot %4 is reporting that it contains bad cached data.
records.explanation: Accelerator Board Bad Data. This trap indicates that the agent has detected an array accelerator cache board that has lost battery power. If data was being stored in the accelerator cache memory when the server lost power, that data has been lost.
records.recommended_action: Verify that no data has been lost.

messages: The array accelerator board attached to the array controller in slot %4 is reporting a battery failure.
records.explanation: Accelerator Board Battery Failed. This trap indicates that the agent has detected a battery failure associated with the array accelerator cache board.
records.recommended_action: Replace the Accelerator Cache Board.

messages: The %6 %7 storage system connected to SCSI bus %5 of the controller in slot %4 has a new status of %2.
records.explanation: Storage System fan status change. The agent has detected a change in the Fan Status of a storage system. The variable cpqSsBoxFanStatus indicates the current fan status.
records.recommended_action: If the fan status is degraded or failed, replace any failed fans.

messages: The %6 %7 storage system connected to SCSI bus %5 of the controller in slot %4 has a failed temperature status. Shut down the storage system as soon as possible.
records.explanation: Storage System temperature failure. The agent has detected that a temperature status has been set to failed. The storage system is shut down.
records.recommended_action:
Shut down the storage system as soon as possible. Insure that the storage system environment
is being cooled properly and that no components are overheated.

messages: The %6 %7 storage system connected to SCSI bus %5 of the controller in slot %4 system has a temperature outside the normal operating range.
records.explanation: Storage System temperature degraded. The agent has detected a temperature status that has been set to degraded. The storage system's temperature is outside of the normal operating range.
records.recommended_action:
Shut down the storage system as soon as possible. Be sure that the storage system
environment is being cooled properly and that no components are overheated.

messages: The side panel has been removed on the %6 %7 storage system connected to SCSI bus %5 of the controller in slot %4.
records.explanation: Storage System side panel is removed. The side panel status has been set to removed. The storage system's side panel is not in a properly installed state. This situation may result in improper cooling of the drives in the storage system due to air flow changes caused by the missing side panel.
records.recommended_action: Replace the storage system side panel.

messages: The IDE drive %4 has a degraded status and should be scheduled for replacement.
records.explanation: An IDE drive status has been set to degraded.
records.recommended_action:
The drive should be scheduled for replacement. For detailed information on a component
replacement, see the appropriate Maintenance and Service Guide.

records.recommended_action: If the logical drive status is failed, examine the array for failed drives that need replacement.

event_names: External Array Physical Drive Status Change.

event_names: SAS/SATA Physical Drive SSD Wear Status Change.
messages: The physical drive in %4, %5 with serial number "%6", has a new solid state wear status of %7. (Drive status values: 1=other, 2=ok, 3=fiftySixDayThreshold, 4=fivePercentThreshold, 5=twoPercentThreshold, 6=ssdWearOut)
records.explanation: The agent has detected a change in the SSD wear status of a SAS or SATA physical drive. The variable cpqSasPhyDrvSSDWearStatus indicates the current SSD wear status.
records.recommended_action: If the SSD wear status is ssdWearOut(6), replace the drive.

event_names: Drive Array Physical Drive SSD Wear Status Change.
messages: The physical drive in %4, %5 with serial number "%6", has a new solid state wear status of %7. (Drive status values: 1=other, 2=ok, 3=fiftySixDayThreshold, 4=fivePercentThreshold, 5=twoPercentThreshold, 6=ssdWearOut)
records.explanation: This trap signifies that the agent has detected a change in the SSD wear status of a drive array physical drive. The variable cpqDaPhyDrvSSDWearStatus indicates the current SSD wear status.
records.recommended_action: If the SSD wear status is ssdWearOut(6), replace the drive.

event_names: IDE Disk SSD Wear Status Change.
messages: The ATA disk drive with model %6 and serial number %7 has a new solid state wear status of %2. (SSD wear status values: 1=other, 2=ok, 3=fiftySixDayThreshold, 4=fivePercentThreshold, 5=twoPercentThreshold, 6=ssdWearOut)
records.explanation: This trap signifies that the agent has detected a change in the SSD wear status of a SATA physical drive. The variable cpqIdeAtaDiskSSDWearStatus indicates the current SSD wear status.
records.recommended_action: If the SSD wear status is ssdWearOut(6), replace the drive.

messages: This trap indicates that an enclosure temperature sensor has been tripped indicating an overheat condition.

working properly and that air flow in the rack has not been blocked.

event_names: The system is overheating (Temperature Sensor %1, Location %2, Temperature %3)
messages: The system is overheating. (Temperature Sensor %1, Location %2, Temperature %3).
records.cause:
1.  The processor heatsink is not installed as indicated in the server documentation.
2.  A supported fan is not installed in the server.
3.  An air baffle or blank is missing or not installed properly and causing a disruption of the airflow.
records.recommended_action:
Check fans, processor heat sink and air baffles installation.
1.  Verify that all air baffles and required blanks, such as drive blanks, processor heatsink blanks, power
supply blanks, and so on are installed.
2.  Verify that the correct processor heatsink is installed.
3.  Verify that the correct fan is installed, if the system supports both standard fans and performance
fans.
For additional information, see the system documentation.
If this issue persists create an HPE Support Case.
1.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to
https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/home, and then click Warranty Check.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed. For
specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance and service
guide.
2.  Under Support Cases, click Access Cases, and then create a support case.
HPE Support will contact you.

messages: Fan failure (Fan %1, Location %2)
records.cause:
•  One of more fans are not seated properly.
•  The fan configuration does not meet the functional requirements of the server.
•  The server is not ventilated properly.
•  One or more required fans are not installed.
•  Required fan blanks are not installed.
•  Error messages are displayed during POST.
•  One or more fans are not functioning.
records.recommended_action:
Be sure the fan configuration meets the functional requirements of the server.
1.  Be sure the fans are properly seated and working:
a.  Follow the procedures and warnings in the server documentation for removing the access
panels and accessing and replacing fans.
b.  Unseat, and then reseat, each fan according to the proper procedures.
c.  Replace the access panels, and then attempt to restart the server.
2.  Be sure the fan configuration meets the functional requirements of the server.
3.  Be sure no ventilation issues exist. If the server is operated for an extended period of time with the
access panel removed, airflow might be impeded, causing thermal damage to components.
4.  Be sure no POST error messages are displayed while booting the server that indicate temperature
violation or fan failure information.
5.  Use iLO or an optional IML viewer to access the IML to see if any event list error messages relating to
fans are listed.
6.  In the iLO web interface, navigate to the Information > System Information page and verify the
following information:
a.  Click Fans, and then verify the fan status, fan speed, and airflow requirements.
b.  Click Temperatures, and then verify the temperature readings for each location on the
Temperatures tab. If a hot spot is located, check the airflow path for blockage by cables
and other material. A hot spot is not an absolute temperature but is relative to a component
specification. Hot spot is defined as temperature on a sensor within 3°C of a Caution threshold
listed on the Temperature tab.
7.  Replace any required non-functioning fans and restart the server.
8.  Be sure all fan slots have fans or blanks installed. For airflow requirements, see the server
documentation.
9.  Verify the fan airflow path is not blocked by cables or other material.
For additional information, see the Troubleshooting Guide for HPE ProLiant Gen10 servers.
If this issue persists, create an HPE Support Case.
1.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to
https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/home, and then click Warranty Status.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed. For
specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance and service
guide.
2.  Under Support Cases, click Access Cases, and then create a support case.
HPE Support will contact you.

messages: This NVDIMM-N was selected for sanitizing/erasing, but this process was not successful.
records.cause:
The NVDIMM controller firmware is unable to perform the sanitize operation on NVDIMM. Either the error
happened temporarily or the NVDIMM hardware has completely failed.
records.recommended_action:
Retry the sanitizing process.
1.  From the System Utilities screen, select System Configuration > BIOS/Platform Configuration
(RBSU) > System Options > Memory Operations > NVDIMM Memory Options.
2.  Select NVDIMM-N Sanitize/Erase on Next Reboot Policy.
The following alert is displayed.
IMPORTANT: Sanitizing/Erasing an NVDIMM-N will result in the loss of ALL user data saved in the
NVDIMM-N. It is strongly recommended that manual backup of all user data in the NVDIMM-N(s) be
performed before sanitizing/erasing the NVDIMM-N(s).
3.  Press any key to proceed.
4.  Select one of the following menu items:
◦ Sanitize/Erase and Boot to Operating System
◦ Sanitize/Erase and Power System Off
◦ Sanitize/Erase and Boot to System Utilities
5.  Select one of the following menu items based on the NVDIMM-Ns to be sanitized/erased:
◦ Sanitize/Erase all NVDIMM-N in the System —Use this option for major system
reconfigurations.
◦ Sanitize/Erase all NVDIMM-N on Processor 1 —Use this option when all the NVDIMM-Ns on a
processor must be sanitized together, such as when enabling NVDIMM-N Memory Interleaving.
◦ Sanitize/Erase Processor 1 DIMM X —This option is available only when NVDIMM-N Memory
Interleaving is disabled. Use this option for adding individual NVDIMM-Ns, or for using an
NVDIMM-N again after errors occur.
◦ Sanitize/Erase all NVDIMM-N on Processor 2 —Use this option when all the NVDIMM-Ns on a
processor must be sanitized together, such as when enabling NVDIMM-N Memory Interleaving.
◦ Sanitize/Erase Processor 2 DIMM X —This option is available only when NVDIMM-N Memory
Interleaving is disabled. Use this option for adding individual NVDIMM-Ns, or for using an
NVDIMM-N again after errors occur.
When enabled, all user data in the selected NVDIMM-N is erased on the next reboot. The Sanitize
NVDIMM-N scope selections are available only after a sanitize policy is selected.
6.  Press the F10 key to save the changes.
7.  Reboot the server.
The server will reboot multiple times as part of the sanitize process. POST messages will also display
to indicate the NVDIMM-Ns that are being sanitized.
If the issues persists, replace the NVDIMM.
1.  Remove all power.
a.  Disconnect each power cord from the power source.
b.  Disconnect each power cord from the server
2.  Remove the DIMM.
CAUTION: Failure to properly handle DIMMs can cause damage to DIMM components and the system
board connector. See the DIMM handling guidelines on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise Library at:
http://www.hpe.com/info/enterprise/docs
3.  Install the new DIMM.

event_names: New NVDIMM(s) detected on Processor %1: All NVDIMMs on Processor %2 have been disabled
messages: New NVDIMM(s) detected on Processor %1. All NVDIMMs on Processor %2 have been disabled.
records.cause:
One or more new NVDIMMs installed on an identified processor. Addition of any new NVDIMM to the
existing functional interleaved set breaks the functionality of entire set.
records.recommended_action:
Do one of the following:
•  Remove the newly installed NVDIMMs from the identified processor to continue using existing
interleaved set.
•  A new interleave set needs to be formed with all the NVDIMMs present on the processor. Sanitize all
NVDIMMs on the identified processor to form a new interleave set.
Sanitizing DIMMs
1.  From the System Utilities screen, select System Configuration > BIOS/Platform Configuration
(RBSU) > System Options > Memory Operations > NVDIMM Memory Options.
2.  Select NVDIMM-N Sanitize/Erase on Next Reboot Policy.
The following alert is displayed.
IMPORTANT: Sanitizing/Erasing an NVDIMM-N will result in the loss of ALL user data saved in the
NVDIMM-N. It is strongly recommended that manual backup of all user data in the NVDIMM-N(s) be
performed before sanitizing/erasing the NVDIMM-N(s).
3.  Press any key to proceed.
4.  Select one of the following menu items:
◦ Sanitize/Erase and Boot to Operating System
◦ Sanitize/Erase and Power System Off
◦ Sanitize/Erase and Boot to System Utilities
5.  Select one of the following menu items based on the NVDIMM-Ns to be sanitized/erased:
◦ Sanitize/Erase all NVDIMM-N in the System —Use this option for major system
reconfigurations.
◦ Sanitize/Erase all NVDIMM-N on Processor 1 —Use this option when all the NVDIMM-Ns on a
processor must be sanitized together, such as when enabling NVDIMM-N Memory Interleaving.
◦ Sanitize/Erase Processor 1 DIMM X —This option is available only when NVDIMM-N Memory
Interleaving is disabled. Use this option for adding individual NVDIMM-Ns, or for using an
NVDIMM-N again after errors occur.
◦ Sanitize/Erase all NVDIMM-N on Processor 2 —Use this option when all the NVDIMM-Ns on a
processor must be sanitized together, such as when enabling NVDIMM-N Memory Interleaving.
◦ Sanitize/Erase Processor 2 DIMM X —This option is available only when NVDIMM-N Memory
Interleaving is disabled. Use this option for adding individual NVDIMM-Ns, or for using an
NVDIMM-N again after errors occur.
When enabled, all user data in the selected NVDIMM-N is erased on the next reboot. The Sanitize
NVDIMM-N scope selections are available only after a sanitize policy is selected.
6.  Press the F10 key to save the changes.
7.  Reboot the server.
The server will reboot multiple times as part of the sanitize process. POST messages will also display
to indicate the NVDIMM-Ns that are being sanitized.
If this issue persists, create an HPE Support Case.
1.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to
https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/home, and then click Warranty Status.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed. For
specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance and service
guide.
2.  Under Support Cases, click Access Cases, and then create a support case.
HPE Support will contact you.

event_names: NVDIMM Error: Processor %1, DIMM %2. NVDIMM is configured for a different processor type. All NVDIMMs on Processor %3 are disabled
messages: NVDIMM Error: Processor %1, DIMM %2. NVDIMM is configured for a different processor type. All NVDIMMs on Processor %3 are disabled.
records.cause:
The identified NVDIMM has been configured to work with different processor type than the installed one.
The configuration has to match for the proper function of NVDIMM.
records.recommended_action:
To enable this NVDIMM, either install previously used processor if the processor has been changed recently,
or NVDIMM needs to be sanitized to configure it with the newly installed processor type.
If manual data backup of NVDIMM is desired, try installing previously used processor to take manual data
backup of NVDIMM. Chose desired system configuration afterward.
Sanitizing DIMMs
1.  From the System Utilities screen, select System Configuration > BIOS/Platform Configuration
(RBSU) > System Options > Memory Operations > NVDIMM Memory Options.
2.  Select NVDIMM-N Sanitize/Erase on Next Reboot Policy.
The following alert is displayed.
IMPORTANT: Sanitizing/Erasing an NVDIMM-N will result in the loss of ALL user data saved in the
NVDIMM-N. It is strongly recommended that manual backup of all user data in the NVDIMM-N(s) be
performed before sanitizing/erasing the NVDIMM-N(s).
3.  Press any key to proceed.
4.  Select one of the following menu items:
◦ Sanitize/Erase and Boot to Operating System
◦ Sanitize/Erase and Power System Off
◦ Sanitize/Erase and Boot to System Utilities
5.  Select one of the following menu items based on the NVDIMM-Ns to be sanitized/erased:
◦ Sanitize/Erase all NVDIMM-N in the System —Use this option for major system
reconfigurations.
◦ Sanitize/Erase all NVDIMM-N on Processor 1 —Use this option when all the NVDIMM-Ns on a
processor must be sanitized together, such as when enabling NVDIMM-N Memory Interleaving.
◦ Sanitize/Erase Processor 1 DIMM X —This option is available only when NVDIMM-N Memory
Interleaving is disabled. Use this option for adding individual NVDIMM-Ns, or for using an
NVDIMM-N again after errors occur.

processor must be sanitized together, such as when enabling NVDIMM-N Memory Interleaving.

Update the system ROM firmware and Innovation Engine firmware.

HPE Support website:

Smart Update Manager (SUM):
1.  Download SUM from the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website (http://www.hpe.com/servers/sum).

documentation.
Smart Update Tool (SUT):
Note: To use SUT, you must have HPE OneView downloaded and installed. For more information, see the
HPE OneView documentation at http://www.hpe.com/info/ovvcenter/docs.
1.  Download SUT from the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website (http://www.hpe.com/info/hpsut).

information, see to the HP SUT documents at http://www.hpe.com/info/sut-docs.

Update the Smart Array firmware by downloading the SPP from the Hewlett Packard Enterprise
website (http://www.hpe.com/servers/spp). Refer to the SPP documentation at http://www.hpe.com/info/spp/

Note: Downloading the entire SPP can take a significant amount of time.
Online Flash components
This component provides updated system firmware that can be installed directly on supported operating
systems. Additionally, when used in conjunction with the SUM, this Smart Component allows you to update
firmware on remote servers from a central location.
This remote deployment capability eliminates the need for you to be physically present at the server to

event_names: A critical system health error requires the system to be shut down
messages: A System health error. A critical system health error requires the system to be shut down.
records.cause:
A critical health condition detected by the management processor firmware requires the system to be shut
down.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Be sure that the fans are properly seated and working: For more information, see "General fan issues"
in the troubleshooting guide for your product on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise web::
◦ HPE ProLiant Gen10 (http://www.hpe.com/info/gen10-troubleshooting)
◦ HPE Synergy (http://www.hpe.com/info/synergy-troubleshooting)
2.  Be sure the fan configuration meets the functional requirements of the server.
For more information, see the server user guide for your product on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise
website:
◦ HPE ProLiant Gen10 (http://www.hpe.com/info/proliantgen10-docs)
◦ HPE Synergy (http://www.hpe.com/info/synergy-docs)
3.  Verify that no ventilation issues exist and that the airflow path is not blocked. If the server is operated
for an extended period with the access panel removed, airflow might be impeded, damaging thermal
components.
4.  Be sure no POST error messages are displayed while booting the server that indicates temperature
violation or fan failure information. For the temperature requirements for the server, see the server
documentation.
5.  Use iLO or an optional IML viewer to access the IML to see if any event list error messages relating to
fans are listed. For more information about event list error messages, see Troubleshooting resources
at http://www.hpe.com/info/gen10-troubleshooting.
6.  In the iLO web interface, navigate to the Information > System Information page and verify the
following information:
a.  Click the Fans tab and verify the fan status and fan speed.
b.  Click the Temperatures tab and verify the temperature readings for each location on the
Temperatures tab. If a hot spot is located, then check the airflow path for blockage by cables
and other material.
A hot spot is not an absolute temperature but is relative to a component specification. Hot
spot is defined as temperature on a sensor within 3°C of a Caution threshold listed on the
Temperature tab.
7.  Replace any required non-functioning fans and restart the server. For specifications on fan
requirements, see the server documentation.
8.  Be sure all fan slots have fans or blanks installed. For airflow requirements, see the server
documentation.
9.  Verify the fan airflow path is not blocked by cables or other material.
If this issue persists, create an HPE Support Case.
1.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to
https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/home, and then click Warranty Status.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed. For
specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance and service
guide.
2.  Under Support Cases, click Access Cases, and then create a support case.
HPE Support will contact you.

access panel removed, airflow might be impeded, causing thermal damage to components. For further
requirements, see the server documentation.
4.  Be sure no POST error messages are displayed while booting the server that indicate temperature
violation or fan failure information. For the temperature requirements for the server, see the server
documentation.
5.  Use iLO or an optional IML viewer to access the IML to see if any event list error messages relating to
fans are listed. For more information about event list error messages, see Troubleshooting resources
at http://www.hpe.com/info/gen10-troubleshooting.
6.  In the iLO web interface, navigate to the Information > System Information page and verify the
following information:
a.  Click the Fans tab and verify the fan status and fan speed.
b.  Click the Temperatures tab and verify the temperature readings for each location on the
Temperatures tab. If a hot spot is located, then check the airflow path for blockage by cables
and other material.
A hot spot is not an absolute temperature but is relative to a component specification. Hot
spot is defined as temperature on a sensor within 3°C of a Caution threshold listed on the
Temperature tab.
7.  Replace any required non-functioning fans and restart the server. For specifications on fan
requirements, see the server documentation.
8.  Be sure all fan slots have fans or blanks installed. For airflow requirements, see the server
documentation.
9.  Verify the fan airflow path is not blocked by cables or other material.

messages: The TPM failed or is no longer detected.
records.cause:
•  The TPM failed.
•  The TPM is not configured properly in UEFI System Utilities.
•  The boot mode is not configured for the TPM installed on the server.
•  Chipset-TPM is disabled in UEFI System Utilities. This might happen if defaults are loaded.
records.recommended_action:
1.  When a TPM is installed and is being used with BitLocker, be sure the TPM is enabled in UEFI System
Utilities. See the TPM replacement recovery procedure in the operating system documentation.
2.  When a TPM is installed, be sure that the TPM is configured for a mode that is compatible with the OS
running on the server. Verify that the OS supports the version of TPM installed and configured on the
server.
3.  When a TPM 2.0 is installed, verify that the server is configured for UEFI boot mode.
4.  Leave the TPM installed and request a new system board and TPM from a Hewlett Packard Enterprise
authorized service provider.
5.  Verify that Chipset-TPM feature is enabled in Trusted Platform Module options menu in System
Utilities. For more information, see the UEFI System Utilities user guide at http://www.hpe.com/info/
uefi/docs.

messages: Drive array: Valid data found in write-back cache. Data will automatically be written to drive array.
records.cause:

write-back cache was flushed to the drive array.
records.recommended_action:

leaving data in the write-back cache.

event_names: Drive array: Write-back cache configuration error
messages: Drive Array: Write-back cache configuration error. Data does not correspond to this drive array. Caching is temporarily disabled.
records.cause:
Power was interrupted while data was in the cache. Data stored in the cache does not correspond to this
drive array or the drive array is missing.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Save data.
2.  Move the controller back to the original storage configuration.
3.  Power up the server and allow the controller to flush the cache.
4.  Optional: If the cached data does not need to be saved, discard the data by pressing F9 during boot to
access System Utilities.
a.  Click System Health View > System Health.
b.  Select the controller, and then click Health Status: Configuration Required.
c.  Under Logical Drives Operations, click Repair.
d.  Erase data held in Write-back cache.

messages: Drive array cache module not responding.
records.cause: Caching is temporarily disabled.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Confirm supported battery pack is installed and charged.
2.  Be sure the cache module is seated properly.
3.  Reseat the cache module.
4.  Replace the cache module.
a.  Back up all data.
b.  Close all applications.
c.  Power down the server.
d.  Remove all power:
▪ Disconnect each power cord from the power source.
▪ Disconnect each power cord from the server.
CAUTION: In systems that use external data storage, be sure that the server is the first unit to
be powered down and the last to be powered back up. Taking this precaution ensures that the
system does not erroneously mark the drives as failed when the server is powered up.
For additional information, see the system Maintenance and Service Guide at http://
www.hpe.com/info/enterprise/docs.
If this issue persists, create an HPE Support Case.
1.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to the:
Customer Self Repair website.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed. For
specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance and service
guide.
2.  Create a support case at: http://www.hpe.com/support/hpesc.
HPE Support will contact you.

event_names: Slot encryption failure: Encrypted logical drives offline
messages: The encrypted logical drives are offline and the system might not boot.
records.cause:
The management processor is unable to communicate with the Remote Key License Server due to a network
or configuration issue. SmartArray Drive Encryption cannot get the authentication keys to decrypt the
drives.
records.recommended_action:
Check the network connection between the iLO management port and the remote key manager. Ensure that
the remote key manager configuration settings in iLO are properly configured. If the issue persists, update
the iLO, SmartArray, and System ROM to the latest versions.
Update firmware
There are multiple ways to upgrade the firmware:
HPE Support website:
1.  Go to https://www.hpe.com/us/en/support.html.
2.  Click HPE Storage, Servers and Networking.
3.  Enter product name, and then click Go.
4.  Click Get drivers, software, and firmware.
5.  Select the appropriate operating system.
6.  Select the appropriate patch, and then click Download.
Smart Update Manager (SUM):
1.  Download SUM from the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website (http://www.hpe.com/servers/sum).
2.  Be sure you have the latest SPP (http://www.hpe.com/servers/spp/download).
3.  Open SUM and add the baseline that includes the Smart Array driver. For specific instructions on
updating firmware, see the Smart Update Manager User Guide, at http://www.hpe.com/info/hpsum/
documentation.
Smart Update Tool (SUT):
Note: To use SUT, you must have HPE OneView downloaded and installed. For more information, see the
HPE OneView documentation at http://www.hpe.com/info/ovvcenter/docs.
1.  Download SUT from the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website (http://www.hpe.com/info/hpsut).
2.  Be sure you have the latest SPP (http://www.hpe.com/servers/spp/download).
3.  Run SUT from the command line (On-Demand mode) to update the Smart Array firmware. For more
information, see to the HP SUT documents at http://www.hpe.com/info/sut-docs.
Service Pack for ProLiant (SPP):
Update the Smart Array firmware by downloading the SPP from the Hewlett Packard Enterprise
website (http://www.hpe.com/servers/spp). Refer to the SPP documentation at http://www.hpe.com/info/spp/
documentation for instructions on updating the firmware.
Note: Downloading an SPP requires a contract with Hewlett Packard Enterprise and an HPE Passport ID. If
you do not have an HPE Passport ID, go to http://www.hpe.com/info/insightonline.
Note: Downloading the entire SPP can take a significant amount of time.
Online Flash components
This component provides updated system firmware that can be installed directly on supported operating
systems. Additionally, when used in conjunction with the SUM, this Smart Component allows you to update
firmware on remote servers from a central location.
This remote deployment capability eliminates the need for you to be physically present at the server to
perform a firmware update.
For specific instructions on updating firmware, see the Smart Update Manager User Guide, at http://
www.hpe.com/info/hpsum/documentation.

event_names: Slot %1 Storage - Drive(s) at %2 status changed to Failed
messages: Slot %1 Storage - Drive(s) at %2 status changed to Failed.
records.cause:
Possible causes include:
•  A cable is not installed correctly.
•  The drive is not installed correctly.
•  The drive is setup as Unconfigured Bad
•  The drive is not supported by the backplane, controller, or RAID config.
•  The drive has failed.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Be sure no loose connections exist. For more information, see the Resolving loose connections
section in the Troubleshooting Guide for HPE ProLiant Gen10 servers at http://www.hpe.com/info/
Gen10-troubleshooting.
2.  Be sure the drive or backplane is cabled properly.
3.  Be sure the drive data cable is working by replacing it with a known functional cable.
4.  Be sure drive blanks are installed properly when the server is operating. Drives may overheat and
cause sluggish response or drive failure.
5.  Set drive to Unconfigured Good.
6.  Verify backplane, controller, RAID config, and drive compatibility.
7.  Power cycle the server. If the drive shows up, check to see if the drive firmware needs to be updated.
If this issue persists, create an HPE Support Case to replace the defective drive.
1.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to
https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/home, and then click Check Status under the Warranty Check
heading.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed. For
specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance and service
guide.
2.  Under Support Cases, click Access Cases, and then create a support case.
HPE Support will contact you.

systems. Additionally, when used in conjunction with the SUM, this Smart Component allows you to update
firmware on remote servers from a central location.

event_names: Processor Jitter Control failed to find a jitter-free frequency in auto- tuned mode.
messages: Processor Jitter Control failed to find a jitter-free frequency in auto-tuned mode. Jitter Control mode has been automatically switched to disabled to prevent significant performance impact.
records.cause:
When Processor Jitter Control is set into Auto mode, firmware adjusts the operating frequency until a
jitter-free frequency is found. If a jitter-free frequency cannot be found, jitter control is disabled to prevent
a significant degradation in performance. This issue is normally caused when power management features
such as C-states are not disabled through BIOS or, more commonly, under the operating system.
records.recommended_action:
Verify that C-states are disabled in the System ROM and under the operating system. For Linux, the Intel
C-state driver must be disabled by adding "intel_idle.max_cstate : 0" to the kernel command line parameter.

messages: The DIMM population on one or more processors results in a memory configuration that is invalid. This error may result in non-optimal memory performance or other unexpected behavior.
records.cause:
The DIMMs are installed in an invalid configuration. The BIOS detects these invalid configurations and
provides a warning of the possible performance impact of these configurations.
records.recommended_action:
Refer to the HPE documentation for DIMM population guidelines and any warnings in regards to
performance. It is recommended that you install supported configurations that allow optimum performance.

messages: A memory error has resulted in one or more DIMMs being mapped out resulting in a memory configuration that is not validated. This error may result in non-optimal memory performance or other unexpected behavior.
records.cause:
One or more DIMMs have been removed from the system memory map due to error conditions. These error
conditions result in a DIMM configuration that is not validated. The BIOS will detect these configurations and
warn the user of the possible performance impact of these configurations.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the failing DIMMs and restore the memory configuration to a supported configuration. See the
Integrated Management Log (IML) for information regarding the original memory error. Refer also to the
HPE documentation for DIMM population guidelines and any warnings in regards to performance. It is
recommended you install supported configurations that allow optimum performance.

messages: One-button secure erase failure for %1.
records.cause: The drive encountered a failure during the One-button secure erase operation.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Update the firmware for the PCIe boot controller.
Service Pack for ProLiant (SPP) contains server drivers, systems software, and firmware. For more
information about SPP, see the SPP website (http://www.hpe.com/servers/spp). Each SPP has an
accompanying server support guide that lists the supported servers and components available for
each of the supported servers. The server support guides and Service Pack for ProLiant Quick Start
Guide are available on the SPP Information Library (http://www.hpe.com/info/spp/documentation).
To update firmware on HPE Apollo and HPE ProLiant products, see the Smart Update Manager User
Guide and the SUM Best Practices Planning Guide at http://www.hpe.com/info/SmartUpdate/docs.
The SPP uses Smart Update Manager (SUM) to deploy firmware and system software components.
To update the firmware on HPE Synergy products, see the Best Practices for HPE Synergy Firmware
and Driver Updates at http://www.hpe.com/info/synergy-docs.
2.  Retry secure erase using Intelligent Provisioning.
For more information, see the Intelligent Provisioning User Guide for HPE ProLiant Gen10
Servers and HPE Synergy on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website (http://www.hpe.com/info/
intelligentprovisioningdocs).
CAUTION: Secure erase should be used with extreme caution, and only when a system is being
decommissioned. The secure erase process resets iLO and deletes all licenses stored there, resets
BIOS settings, and deletes all AHS and warranty data stored on the system. The secure erase process
also erases supported non-volatile storage data and deletes any deployment settings profiles. iLO
reboots multiple times during the process.
CAUTION: Disconnect any FCoE, iSCSI, external SAS, and fibre channel storage before using secure
erase.
For additional information, see Intelligent Provisioning 3.x - Using Secure Erase and Reset.
3.  If the drive did not support any erase method or HPE sanitize protocol, the data on the drive has not
been erased.
To access the troubleshooting resources, see the Hewlett Packard Enterprise Information Library (http://
www.hpe.com/info/Gen10-troubleshooting).
1.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to
https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/home, and then click Check Status under the Warranty Status
heading.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed. For
specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance and service
guide.

messages: A lot of PCIe errors are seen.
records.cause: The PCIe correctable error threshold exceeds.

event_names: Intel Optane PMem for HPE Error.
messages: Intel Optane PMem for HPE Error - Processor %1 DIMM %2 (SN: %3) - The HPE Persistent Memory Module reported a failure on the current boot (Current Boot Status Register: 0x%4).
records.cause:
The indicated Intel Optane PMem for HPE Module reported a link failure on the current boot. This can be
caused by an unknown reason that PMem controller failed to create a link with the persistent media.
records.recommended_action:
Consult the Integrated Management Log (IML) for additional information. If the issue persists, confirm the
system firmware are latest, including the System Programmable Logic Device and system ROM. Check the
PMem module and replace it if needed.

messages: Power Fault Detected - OCP %1
records.cause: The OCP device is incorrectly placed on the connector.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Shut down the server.
2.  Perform one of the following:
◦ For non-blade or non-SL-series server, unplug the server. Or,
◦ For blade or SL-series servers, remove the server.
3.  Locate and correctly place the indicated OCP device.

messages: PCIe Enhanced Downstream Port Containment (EDPC) Event detected on Slot %1. EDPC Status: 0x%2.
records.cause:

uncorrectable PCIe error with the device.
records.recommended_action: Contact HPE customer support if the issue persists.

event_names: High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) failure - uncorrectable memory error (processor %1)
messages: High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) failure - uncorrectable memory error (processor %1)
records.cause: High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) has encountered an uncorrectable error
records.recommended_action: Replace processor %1

event_names: High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) failure - correctable memory error exceeded threshold (processor %1)
messages: High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) failure - correctable memory error exceeded threshold (processor %1)
records.cause:
High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) errors occur due to component electrical degradation, where an HBM cell
fails to meet its required electrical specifications.
records.recommended_action:
Reboot the system or re-seat the HBM processor and update the system firmware. If the issue persists,
contact support.

event_names: Unsupported DIMM Configuration Detected - Processor %1 violates DIMM population rules.
messages: Unsupported DIMM Configuration Detected - Processor %1 violates DIMM population rules.
records.cause:
The DIMMs are incorrectly populated in the system. The BIOS detect these configurations and warn the user
of the possible performance impact of these configurations.
records.recommended_action: Consult the User Guide for more information on supported configurations and population rules.

event_names: HBM Uncorrectable Error Threshold Exceeded and HBM Stack Mapped Out Impacting Memory Availability and Performance
messages: High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) uncorrectable memory error threshold exceeded (processor %1, stack %2). memory modules on the same HBM stack are mapped out and are currently not available. The HBM stack map out may result in non-optimal memory performance or other unexpected behavior.
records.cause: An excessive number of uncorrectable errors were detected on the HBM stack specified in the IML
records.recommended_action:
Replace the failing HBM processor to re-map all HBM stacks back into the memory map in RBSU. If the issue
persists, contact support.

event_names: DIMM Initialization Error - All memory channels are mapped out due to memory errors except for one to allow the system to boot.
messages: DIMM Initialization Error - All memory channels are mapped out due to memory errors except for one to allow the system to boot. Additional errors may be present on the remaining DIMMs. System is booting in a degraded state.
records.cause:
All the memory channels in the system have exceeded the acceptable threshold of UC errors. This could be
the result of faulty DIMM modules or an issue with one or more system board components.
records.recommended_action: Re-seat the processor and memory. If the issue persists, replace the memory or contact support.

event_names: %1 %2 Port %3 NVMe-oF Error - Failed to acquire DHCP initiator network address.
messages: %1 %2 Port %3 NVMe-oF Error - Failed to acquire DHCP initiator network address.
records.cause:
An attempt to acquire initiator configuration using DHCP failed because of connection or configuration
issues.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Check network cable and DHCP server configuration.
2.  Reboot the server.

event_names: %1 %2 Port %3 NVMe-oF Error - Failed to acquire DHCP target network address.
messages: %1 %2 Port %3 NVMe-oF Error - Failed to acquire DHCP target network address.
records.cause:
An attempt to acquire the NVMe-oF target configuration using DHCP failed because of connection or
configuration issues.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Check if the network cable is connected to this port.
2.  Check if the DHCP server is reachable from the system.
3.  Check if the DHCP server is configured to provide the target settings required for the system such as
IP address, port number, target NQN, and so on.
4.  Check if the DHCP server is not busy.
5.  Reboot the system and retry.

event_names: %1 %2 Port %3 NVMe-oF Error - Boot Namespace ID is not available.
messages: %1 %2 Port %3 NVMe-oF Error - Boot Namespace ID is not available.
records.cause: Unable to access the NVMe-oF Namespace ID because of configuration issues.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Check if the NVMe-oF configuration on the target is correct and the initiator has permissions to
access the disk or the namespace ID.
2.  Reboot the system.

records.recommended_action: Retry Firmware Update. If the issue persists, contact customer service.

event_names: %1 %2 Port %3 NVMe-oF Error - NVMe-oF login failed.
messages: %1 %2 Port %3 NVMe-oF Error - NVMe-oF login failed.
records.cause:
Unable to login to the NVMe-oF target using the provided configuration because of connection or
configuration issues.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Check if the network cable is connected to this port.
2.  If the settings are configured to be provided by a DHCP server, ensure that it is reachable from the
system and is not busy.
3.  If the settings on the system are configured manually, check that the controller settings, initiator
configuration and target configuration, including any authentication settings, are correct.
4.  Check that the target is configured correctly.
5.  Restart the system and try again.

messages: The power supply is not functioning.
records.cause: Redundant power supplies are configured, but the power supplies are not compatible.
records.recommended_action:
If running a redundant configuration, be sure that all of the power supplies in the system have the same
spare part number and are supported by the server.
•  For a list of supported power supplies, see the server documentation.
•  You can disable these messages by turning off the Mismatch Power Supply Reporting in the system
BIOS settings.

event_names: Power supply or power backplane detection error
messages: LEDs on the power supplies are lit, but power supplies are not being detected.
records.cause:
•  No power supplies were detected by the management processor.
•  Indicates an issue with the system CPLD not detecting power supplies.
•  For chassis controlled servers, it may indicate an issue with the chassis firmware not detecting power
supplies.
records.recommended_action:
Update the system CPLD and, if applicable, the chassis firmware to the latest version.
There are multiple ways to upgrade the firmware:
HPE Support website:
1.  Go to https://www.hpe.com/us/en/support.html.
2.  Click HPE Storage, Servers and Networking.
3.  Enter product name, and then click Go.
4.  Click Get drivers, software, and firmware.
5.  Select the appropriate operating system.
6.  Select the appropriate patch, and then click Download.
Smart Update Manager (SUM):
1.  Download SUM from the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website (http://www.hpe.com/servers/sum).
2.  Be sure you have the latest SPP (http://www.hpe.com/servers/spp/download).
3.  Open SUM and add the baseline that includes the Smart Array driver. For specific instructions on
updating firmware, see the Smart Update Manager User Guide, at http://www.hpe.com/info/hpsum/
documentation.
Smart Update Tool (SUT):
Note: To use SUT, you must have HPE OneView downloaded and installed. For more information, see the
HPE OneView documentation at http://www.hpe.com/info/ovvcenter/docs.
1.  Download SUT from the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website (http://www.hpe.com/info/hpsut).
2.  Be sure you have the latest SPP (http://www.hpe.com/servers/spp/download).
3.  Run SUT from the command line (On-Demand mode) to update the Smart Array firmware. For more
information, see to the HP SUT documents at http://www.hpe.com/info/sut-docs.
Service Pack for ProLiant (SPP):
Update the Smart Array firmware by downloading the SPP from the Hewlett Packard Enterprise
website (http://www.hpe.com/servers/spp). Refer to the SPP documentation at http://www.hpe.com/info/spp/
documentation for instructions on updating the firmware.
Note: Downloading an SPP requires a contract with Hewlett Packard Enterprise and an HPE Passport ID. If
you do not have an HPE Passport ID, go to http://www.hpe.com/info/insightonline.
Note: Downloading the entire SPP can take a significant amount of time.
Online Flash components
This component provides updated system firmware that can be installed directly on supported operating
systems. Additionally, when used in conjunction with the SUM, this Smart Component allows you to update
firmware on remote servers from a central location.
This remote deployment capability eliminates the need for you to be physically present at the server to
perform a firmware update.
For specific instructions on updating firmware, see the Smart Update Manager User Guide, at http://
www.hpe.com/info/hpsum/documentation.

messages: Server is not powering on.
records.cause:
•  The current power supply configuration is not sufficient to operate the server.
•  Unable to read a mezzanine card or the baseboard FRU (field-replaceable unit) to determine the
power requirements.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Verify that the power supplies installed support the power requirements for the server configuration.
For more information, see the Power Advisor (http://www.hpe.com/info/poweradvisor).
2.  Verify that all power supplies are supported for this server. For more information, see the product
QuickSpecs at http://www.hpe.com/info/enterprise/docs.
3.  Be sure the system has enough power, particularly if you recently added hardware, such as drives.
Remove the newly added component and if the issue is no longer present, then additional power
supplies are required.
4.  If the power supplies have LEDs, be sure they indicate that each power supply is working properly.
a.  If the LEDs indicate an issue with a power supply (red, amber, or off), then check the power
source.
b.  If the power source is working properly, then replace the power supply.
5.  If there is a baseboard FRU read error:
◦ Remove and reinsert the blade and attempt to power on the system.
6.  If there is a mezzanine card read error:
a.  Remove and re-seat the failing mezzanine card and attempt to power on the system.
b.  Remove the failing mezzanine card and attempt to power on the system.
If this issue persists, create an HPE Support Case.
1.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to the:
Customer Self Repair website.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed. For
specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance and service
guide.
2.  Create a support case at: http://www.hpe.com/support/hpesc.
HPE Support will contact you.

messages: System power supply: %1 (Power Supply %2)
records.cause:
1.  The power supply might not be fully seated.
2.  AC power is unavailable.
3.  The power supply failed.
4.  The power supply is in standby mode.
5.  The power supply has exceeded the current limit.
6.  The power supply is not supported on the server.
7.  The power is not sufficient for the hardware installed.
8.  Redundant power supplies are configured but the power supplies are not compatible.
records.recommended_action:
Replace the power supply.
1.  Be sure no loose connections exist. For more information, see "Resolving loose connections" in the
HPE ProLiant Gen9 Troubleshooting Guide, Volume 1.
2.  If the power supplies have LEDs, be sure they indicate that each power supply is working properly.
a.  the LEDs indicate an issue with a power supply (red, amber, or off), then check the power
source.
b.  If the power source is working properly, then replace the power supply.
3.  Be sure the system has enough power, particularly if you recently added hardware, such as drives.
Remove the newly added component and if the issue is no longer present, then additional power
supplies are required. Check the system information from the IML.
For product-specific information, see the server documentation at (http://www.hpe.com/info/
enterprise/docs).
For more information on Power Advisor, go to(http://www.hpe.com/info/poweradvisor).
Refer to the Integrated Management Log for details.
4.  If running a redundant configuration, be sure that the installed power supplies in the system
meet system redundancy requirements. For a list of supported power supplies, see the server
documentation (http://www.hpe.com/info/enterprise/docs).
5.  For further troubleshooting, see the "Power-on issues flowchart" in the HPE ProLiant Gen
10Troubleshooting Guide. For more information, see the server documentation (http://www.hpe.com/
info/enterprise/docs).
If this issue persists, create an HPE Support Case.
1.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to the:
Customer Self Repair website.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed. For
specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance and service
guide.
2.  Create a support case at: http://www.hpe.com/support/hpesc.
HPE Support will contact you.

event_names: The system power supply or power source is malfunctioning
messages: System power supply or power source is malfunctioning.
records.cause:
•  The power source is providing too high a voltage to the power supply.
•  The power supply fan stopped rotating, but the supply is still operational.
records.recommended_action:
Check if an object is preventing the power supply fan from rotating properly.
Check the power supply:
1.  Press the Power On/Standby button to be sure it is on. If the server has a Power On/Standby button
that returns to its original position after being pressed, be sure you press the switch firmly. For
more information about system power LED status, see the System Power LED definitions section
in the Troubleshooting Guide for HPE ProLiant Gen10 servers at http://www.hpe.com/info/Gen10-
troubleshooting.
2.  Be sure no loose connections exist. For more information, see the Resolving loose connections
section in the Troubleshooting Guide for HPE ProLiant Gen10 servers at http://www.hpe.com/info/
Gen10-troubleshooting.
3.  Verify that the power LEDs are on the power supplies are illuminated.
4.  Plug another device into the grounded power outlet to be sure the outlet works. Also, be sure the
power source meets applicable standards.
5.  Replace the power cord with a known functional power cord to be sure it is not faulty.
6.  Replace the power strip with a known functional power strip to be sure it is not faulty.
7.  Be sure the proper circuit breaker is in the On position.
8.  Have a qualified electrician check the line voltage to be sure it meets the required specifications.
9.  If Enclosure Dynamic Power Capping or Enclosure Power Limit is enabled on supported servers, be
sure there is sufficient power allocation to support the server. For more information, see the following
documents:
◦ HPE Power Capping and HPE Dynamic Power Capping for ProLiant servers technology brief on
the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website (http://www.hpe.com/support/hpdpc).
◦ HPE BladeSystem Onboard Administrator User Guide on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise
website (http://www.hpe.com/support/BladeSystem/docs)

Smart Update Manager (SUM):

Smart Update Tool (SUT):

1.  Download SUT from the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website (http://www.hpe.com/info/hpsut).

information, see to the HP SUT documents at http://www.hpe.com/info/sut-docs.

www.hpe.com/servers/spp). Refer to the SPP documentation at http://www.hpe.com/info/spp/documentation
for instructions on updating the firmware.

you do not have an HPE Passport ID, go to http://www.hpe.com/info/insightonline.
Note: Downloading the entire SPP can take a significant amount of time.
Online Flash components
This component provides updated system firmware that can be installed directly on supported operating
systems. Additionally, when used in conjunction with the SUM, this Smart Component allows you to update
firmware on remote servers from a central location.
This remote deployment capability eliminates the need for you to be physically present at the server to
perform a firmware update.
For specific instructions on updating firmware, see the Smart Update Manager User Guide, at http://
www.hpe.com/info/hpsum/documentation.

event_names: Storage system fan status changed to %1 for location %2 connected to controller %3
messages: Storage system fan status changed to %1 for location %2 connected to controller %3
records.cause:
•  One of more fans are not seated properly.
•  The fan configuration does not meet the functional requirements of the server.
•  The server is not ventilated properly.
•  One or more required fans are not installed.
•  Required fan blanks are not installed.
•  Error messages are displayed during POST.
•  One or more fans are not functioning.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Be sure the fans are properly seated and working:
a.  Follow the procedures and warnings in the server documentation for removing the access
panels and accessing and replacing fans.
b.  Unseat, and then reseat, each fan according to the proper procedures.
c.  Replace the access panels, and then attempt to restart the server.
2.  Be sure the fan configuration meets the functional requirements of the server.
3.  Be sure no ventilation issues exist. If the server is operated for an extended period of time with the
access panel removed, airflow might be impeded, causing thermal damage to components.
4.  Be sure no POST error messages are displayed while booting the server that indicate temperature
violation or fan failure information.
5.  Use iLO or an optional IML viewer to access the IML to see if any event list error messages relating to
fans are listed.
6.  In the iLO web interface, navigate to the Power & Thermal page and verify the following information:
a.  Click Fans, and then verify the fan status, fan speed, and airflow requirements.
b.  Click Temperatures, and then verify the temperature readings for each location on the
Temperatures tab. If a hot spot is located, check the airflow path for blockage by cables
and other material. A hot spot is not an absolute temperature but is relative to a component
specification. Hot spot is defined as temperature on a sensor within 3°C of a Caution threshold
listed on the Temperature tab.
7.  Replace any required non-functioning fans and restart the server.
8.  Be sure all fan slots have fans or blanks installed. For airflow requirements, see the server
documentation.
9.  Verify the fan airflow path is not blocked by cables or other material.
For additional information, see the Troubleshooting Guide for HPE ProLiant Gen10 servers.
If this issue persists, create an HPE Support Case.
1.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to the:

•  AC power is unavailable.
•  The power supply failed.
•  The power supply is in standby mode.
•  The power supply has exceeded the current limit.
•  The power supply is not supported on the server.
•  The power is not sufficient for the hardware installed.
•  Redundant power supplies are configured but the power supplies are not compatible.
records.recommended_action:
Restore power or replace the failed power supply.
1.  Be sure no loose connections exist.
2.  If the power supplies have LEDs, be sure they indicate that each power supply is working properly.
◦ If the LEDs indicate an issue with a power supply (red, amber, or off), then check the power
source.
◦ If the power source is working properly, then replace the power supply.
3.  Be sure the system has enough power, particularly if you recently added hardware, such as
drives.Remove the newly added component and if the issue is no longer present, then additional
powersupplies are required. Check the system information from the IML. Click here for more
information on HPE Power Advisor
4.  If running a redundant configuration, be sure that all of the power supplies in the system have
thesame spare part number and are supported by the server.
If this issue persists, create an HPE Support Case.
1.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to the:
Customer Self Repair website.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed. For
specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance and service
guide.
2.  Create a support case at: http://www.hpe.com/support/hpesc.
HPE Support will contact you.

If the firmware is not configured for automatic recovery, or if the recovery does not succeed, then the
firmware must be updated.
Update to the latest firmware version.

information about SPP, see the SPP website (http://www.hpe.com/servers/spp). Each SPP has an
accompanying server support guide that lists the supported servers and components available for each
of the supported servers. The server support guides and Service Pack for ProLiant Quick Start Guide are
available on the SPP Information Library (http://www.hpe.com/info/spp/documentation).
To update firmware on HPE Apollo and HPE ProLiant products, see the Smart Update Manager User Guide
and the SUM Best Practices Planning Guide at http://www.hpe.com/info/SmartUpdate/docs. The SPP uses
Smart Update Manager (SUM) to deploy firmware and system software components.
To update the firmware on HPE Synergy products, see the HPE Synergy Firmware Update Overview at
http://www.hpe.com/info/synergy-docs.

To update firmware on HPE Apollo and HPE ProLiant products, see the Smart Update Manager User Guide

event_names: %1 Inadequate power to power on: %2 (Enclosure Serial Number %3, Bay %4)
messages: %1 Inadequate power to power on: %2 (Enclosure Serial Number %3, Bay %4)
records.cause:
•  The power being supplied is not sufficient for the server blades installed in the enclosure.
•  A possible communication failure between management processor and the enclosure manager is
causing the server blade to wait for permission to power on.
•  Insufficient power in the enclosure to allow the system to turn on at this time.
records.recommended_action:
If the server is now on and this event is seen, the server was previously denied due to insufficient power, but
everything is working correctly now. If not, complete the following:
1.  Press the Power On/Standby button to be sure it is on. If the server has a Power On/Standby button
that returns to its original position after being pressed, be sure you press the switch firmly.
2.  Be sure no loose connections exist.
3.  Verify that the power LEDs are on the power supplies are illuminated.
4.  Plug another device into the grounded power outlet to be sure the outlet works. Also, be sure the
power source meets applicable standards.
5.  Replace the power cord with a known functional power cord to be sure it is not faulty.
6.  Replace the power strip with a known functional power strip to be sure it is not faulty.
7.  Be sure the proper circuit breaker is in the On position.
8.  Have a qualified electrician check the line voltage to be sure it meets the required specifications.
9.  If Enclosure Dynamic Power Capping or Enclosure Power Limit is enabled on supported servers, be
sure there is sufficient power allocation to support the server.
For additional information, see Power Issues in the Troubleshooting Guide for HPE ProLiant Gen10 servers.
If this issue persists, create an HPE Support Case.
1.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to the:
Customer Self Repair website.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed. For
specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance and service
guide.
2.  Create a support case at: http://www.hpe.com/support/hpesc.
HPE Support will contact you.

event_names: %1 Power request denied: %2 %3 (Enclosure Serial Number %4, Bay %5)
messages: %1 Power request denied: %2 %3 (Enclosure Serial Number %4, Bay %5)
records.cause:
•  The server blade is not properly installed in the enclosure.
•  The server blade is not configured to automatically power on.
•  The power being supplied is not sufficient for the server blades installed in the enclosure.
•  The power cap is not configured properly for the enclosure.
•  The OA module is not properly installed in the enclosure.
•  A possible communication failure between the management processor and the OA is causing the
server blade to wait for permission to power on.
•  The server blade has a mismatched fabric installed on the mezzanine 1 connector or the mezzanine2
connector.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Press the Power On/Standby button to be sure it is on. If the server has a Power On/Standby button
that returns to its original position after being pressed, be sure you press the switch firmly.
2.  Be sure no loose connections exist.
3.  Verify that the power LEDs are on the power supplies are illuminated.
4.  Plug another device into the grounded power outlet to be sure the outlet works. Also, be sure the
power source meets applicable standards.
5.  Replace the power cord with a known functional power cord to be sure it is not faulty.
6.  Replace the power strip with a known functional power strip to be sure it is not faulty.
7.  Be sure the proper circuit breaker is in the On position.
8.  Have a qualified electrician check the line voltage to be sure it meets the required specifications.
9.  If Enclosure Dynamic Power Capping or Enclosure Power Limit is enabled on supported servers, be
sure there is sufficient power allocation to support the server.
For additional information, see Power Issues in the Troubleshooting Guide for HPE ProLiant Gen10 servers.
If this issue persists create an HPE Support Case.
1.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to the:
Customer Self Repair website.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed. For
specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance and service
guide.
2.  Create a support case at: http://www.hpe.com/support/hpesc.
HPE Support will contact you.

event_names: Power-Off signal sent to the host server by iLO due to insufficient PSUs
messages: Power-Off signal sent to the host server by iLO due to insufficient PSUs
records.cause:
The management controller initiated a protective system power-off to prevent hardware damage. This
occurs when the operational Power Supply Units (PSUs) cannot provide adequate power for the current
hardware configuration or required redundancy levels.
records.recommended_action:
Verify that all PSUs are correctly seated, functioning properly, and connected to a stable AC power source.
Replace any faulty power supplies, and ensure the total PSU capacity is sufficient to load hardware
components installed in the server.
