event_names: Processor operating at reduced performance level due to a low power cap.
messages: Processor operating at reduced performance level due to a low power cap.
records.cause:
The processor performance has been reduced. After reducing the processor performance, the power cap is
able to be met.
records.recommended_action:
Check if the server power supply capacity or allocated server power is suitable for the workload. Consider
increasing the power cap and adding power capacity if necessary to prevent the reduced performance.
1.  Check the server power supply capacity in the management processor Web GUI, under Power and
Thermal -> Power, or Chassis Information for servers with chassis controlled power supplies.
2.  Compare with the power consumption in the Power and Thermal -> Power page, or if applicable, the
Power Meter page which provides up to 24 hours of power history.
3.  Increase the configured power cap value. If additional hardware has been added to the server, power
calibration during the next server boot might resolve this issue.

event_names: Power cap cannot be reached with current system configuration
messages: The power cap cannot be reached.
records.cause:
•  The processor performance has been reduced.
•  After reducing the processor performance, the power cap is not able to be met.
records.recommended_action:
Check if the server power supply capacity or allocated server power is suitable for the workload.
1.  Check the server power supply capacity, for example, in the management processor Web GUI, under
Power and Thermal -> Power, or Chassis Information for servers with chassis controlled power
supplies.
2.  Compare with the power consumption in the Power and Thermal -> Power page, or if applicable, the
Power Meter page which provides up to 24 hours of power history in a graphical form.
3.  Increase the configured power cap value. If additional hardware has been added to the server, power
calibration during the next server boot may resolve this issue.
If this issue persists, create an HPE Support Case.
1.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to the:
Customer Self Repair website.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed. For
specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance and service
guide.
2.  Create a support case at: http://www.hpe.com/support/hpesc.
HPE Support will contact you.

messages: The drive will not boot from the USB drive key.
records.cause:
•  The USB drive key is not enabled in the UEFI System Utilities.
•  The drive boot order is not set to boot from the USB drive key.
•  The USB drive key is not seated properly.
records.recommended_action:
Re-seat the USB drive key.
1.  Be sure that USB is enabled in the UEFI System Utilities.
2.  Be sure the drive boot order in the UEFI System Utilities is set so that the server boots from the USB
drive key.
3.  Re-seat the USB drive key.
4.  Move the USB drive key to a different USB port, if available.

event_names: Secure Erase of the management processor's embedded media device has failed
messages: Secure Erase of the management processor's embedded media device has failed.
records.cause:
•  Unable to perform the Secure Erase operation on the embedded media device due to possible
hardware or controller firmware issue.
•  After the initiation of secure erase, verify that the license is not expired.
records.recommended_action:
Retry secure erase using Intelligent Provisioning.
CAUTION: Secure erase should be used with extreme caution, and only when a system is being
decommissioned. The secure erase process resets iLO and deletes all licenses stored there, resets BIOS
settings, and deletes all AHS and warranty data stored on the system. The secure erase process also erases
supported non-volatile storage data and deletes any deployment settings profiles. iLO reboots multiple
times during the process.
CAUTION: Disconnect any FCoE, iSCSI, external SAS, and fibre channel storage before using secure erase.
For additional information, see Intelligent Provisioning 3.x - Using Secure Erase and Reset.
If this issue persists, create an HPE Support Case.

Customer Self Repair website.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed. For

messages: A POST error message displays: Trusted Platform Module (TPM) self-test error.
records.cause:
•  The TPM failed.
•  The TPM is not configured properly in UEFI System Utilities.
•  The boot mode is not configured for the TPM installed on the server.
•  Chipset-TPM is disabled in UEFI System Utilities. This might happen if defaults are loaded.
records.recommended_action:
1.  When a TPM is installed and is being used with BitLocker, be sure the TPM is enabled in UEFI System
Utilities. See the UEFI System Utilities user guide for your product, and see the TPM replacement
recovery procedure in the operating system documentation.
2.  When a TPM is installed, be sure that the TPM is configured for a mode that is compatible with the OS
running on the server. Verify that the OS supports the version of TPM installed and configured on the
server.
3.  When a TPM 2.0 is installed, verify that the server is configured for UEFI boot mode.
4.  Leave the TPM installed, and request a new system board and TPM from a Hewlett Packard
Enterprise authorized service provider.
a.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to https://support.hpe.com/
hpesc/public/home, and then click Warranty Check.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed.
For specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance
and service guide.
b.  Under Support Cases, click Access Cases, and then create a support case.
HPE Support will contact you.
5.  Verify that Chipset-TPM feature is enabled in the Trusted Platform Module options menu in System
Utilities.

event_names: Server Platform Services Authentication Failure - The Server Platform Services (SPS) firmware image could not be authenticated because the image is out of date.
messages: Server Platform Services Authentication Failure - The Server Platform Services (SPS) firmware image could not be authenticated because the image is out of date.
records.cause:
The SPS firmware image needs to pass the cryptographic signature checking process for it to be
authenticated. Use a version of the SPS firmware that includes this support.
records.recommended_action:
Update the SPS firmware image.
Update firmware
There are multiple ways to upgrade the firmware:
HPE Support website:
1.  Go to https://www.hpe.com/us/en/support.html.
2.  Click HPE Storage, Servers and Networking.
3.  Enter product name, and then click Go.
4.  Click Get drivers, software, and firmware.
5.  Select the appropriate operating system.
6.  Select the appropriate patch, and then click Download.
Smart Update Manager (SUM):
1.  Download SUM from the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website (http://www.hpe.com/servers/sum).
2.  Be sure you have the latest SPP (http://www.hpe.com/servers/spp/download).
3.  Open SUM and add the baseline that includes the Smart Array driver. For specific instructions on
updating firmware, see the Smart Update Manager User Guide, at http://www.hpe.com/info/hpsum/
documentation.
Smart Update Tool (SUT):
Note: To use SUT, you must have HPE OneView downloaded and installed. For more information, see the
HPE OneView documentation at http://www.hpe.com/info/ovvcenter/docs.
1.  Download SUT from the Hewlett Packard Enterprise website (http://www.hpe.com/info/hpsut).
2.  Be sure you have the latest SPP (http://www.hpe.com/servers/spp/download).
3.  Run SUT from the command line (On-Demand mode) to update the Smart Array firmware. For more
information, see to the HP SUT documents at http://www.hpe.com/info/sut-docs.
Service Pack for ProLiant (SPP):
Update the Smart Array firmware by downloading the SPP from the Hewlett Packard Enterprise
website (http://www.hpe.com/servers/spp). Refer to the SPP documentation at http://www.hpe.com/info/spp/
documentation for instructions on updating the firmware.
Note: Downloading an SPP requires a contract with Hewlett Packard Enterprise and an HPE Passport ID. If
you do not have an HPE Passport ID, go to http://www.hpe.com/info/insightonline.
Note: Downloading the entire SPP can take a significant amount of time.
Online Flash components
This component provides updated system firmware that can be installed directly on supported operating
systems. Additionally, when used in conjunction with the SUM, this Smart Component allows you to update
firmware on remote servers from a central location.
This remote deployment capability eliminates the need for you to be physically present at the server to
perform a firmware update.
For specific instructions on updating firmware, see the Smart Update Manager User Guide, at http://
www.hpe.com/info/hpsum/documentation.

event_names: Intel Optane PMem for HPE Configuration Error - (Major Code:%1, Minor Code:%2)
messages: Intel Optane PMem for HPE Configuration Error - (Major Code:%1, Minor Code:%2)
records.cause: An Intel Optane PMem for HPE population rule was violated.
records.recommended_action:

guide. For DIMM population, see the Population rules for HPE DDR4 memory with HPE ProLiant and
Synergy Gen10 servers at (http://www.hpe.com/docs/memory-population-rules).

event_names: Unsupported DIMM Configuration detected - Processor %1 DIMM %2 violates DIMM population rules. (Major Code:%3, Minor Code:%4).
messages: Processor %1 DIMM %2 violated the DIMM population rules.
records.cause:
The DIMMs are incorrectly populated in the system. The BIOS will detect these configurations and warn the
user of the possible performance impact of these configurations.
records.recommended_action:
This DIMM has population rule violation. Do not replace this DIMM. Check the installation of the DIMMs in
the system. Verify they are populated in compliance with the User Guide. Consult the User Guide for more
information on supported configurations.

event_names: HPE Persistent Memory Initialization Error: Processor %1 DIMM %2 (SN: %3)
messages: HPE Persistent Memory Initialization Error: Processor %1 DIMM %2 (SN: %3). The PMM media is not available for use. The PMM controller is still operational.
records.cause:
The system ROM failed to train the Persistent Memory Module (PMM), and thus the media device has been
disabled. The module's controller is still enabled.
records.recommended_action:
1.  Review documentation for more information on supported configurations.
For more information, see the HPE Persistent Memory User Guide for HPE ProLiant Gen10 servers
and HPE Synergy.
2.  If the issue persists, check if there is a newer version of the firmware available for the PMM controller
and the system ROM, otherwise replace the PMM.
To update firmware:
Service Pack for ProLiant (SPP) contains server drivers, systems software, and firmware. For more
information about SPP, see the SPP website (http://www.hpe.com/servers/spp). Each SPP has an
accompanying server support guide that lists the supported servers and components available for
each of the supported servers. The server support guides and Service Pack for ProLiant Quick Start
Guide are available on the SPP Information Library (http://www.hpe.com/info/spp/documentation).
To update firmware on HPE Apollo and HPE ProLiant products, see the Smart Update Manager User
Guide and the SUM Best Practices Planning Guide at http://www.hpe.com/info/SmartUpdate/docs.
The SPP uses Smart Update Manager (SUM) to deploy firmware and system software components.
To update the firmware on HPE Synergy products, see the Best Practices for HPE Synergy Firmware
and Driver Updates at http://www.hpe.com/info/synergy-docs..
3.  If the issue still presists, replace the Persistent Memory Module.
1.  Remove all power.
1.  Disconnect each power cord from the power source.
2.  Disconnect each power cord from the server.
2.  Remove the Persistent Memory Module.
CAUTION: Failure to properly handle DIMMs can cause damage to DIMM components and the
system board connector. See the DIMM handling guidelines on the Hewlett Packard Enterprise
Library at http:// www.hpe.com/info/enterprise/docs.
3.  Install the new Persistent Memory Module.
1.  Verify the component is either under warranty or contract. Go to
https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/home, and then click Check Status under the Warranty Status
heading.
This enables HPE to ship replacement parts directly to you once a failure has been confirmed. For
specific information about customer replaceable parts, refer to the product maintenance and service
guide.
2.  Under Support Cases, click Access Cases, and then create a support case.
HPE Support will contact you.

event_names: Hardware Installation Error - Cabling to cable riser slot %1 is incorrectly installed. Riser functionality may be impaired.
messages: Hardware Installation Error - Cabling to cable riser slot %1 is incorrectly installed. Riser functionality may be impaired.

event_names: Processor Firmware Update Failure - Processor %1. The processor's %2 image failed to update to version %3.
messages: Processor Firmware Update Failure - Processor %1. The processor's %2 image failed to update to version %3.
records.cause:
The BIOS image has a newer version of the indicated firmware from the one that is present on the processor
but it failed to update correctly.
records.recommended_action:
Update to the latest BIOS. If the problem persists, contact support.

Library at https://sml-csr.ext.hpe.com/.

event_names: Uncorrectable memory error threshold exceeded (%1 %2, DIMM %3): Memory Channel DIMMs Unavailable
messages: Uncorrectable memory error threshold exceeded (%1 %2, DIMM %3). The DIMMs on the same memory channel are mapped out and are currently not available.
records.cause:
Excessive number of uncorrectable errors is detected on the Memory module specified in the IML
description.
records.recommended_action:
Take corrective action for the failing DIMM. Re-map all DIMMs back into the memory map in RBSU. If the
issue persists, contact support.

event_names: Unsupported processor configuration detected - One or more installed processors cannot be used in a multi-processor configuration.
messages: Unsupported processor configuration detected - One or more installed processors cannot be used in a multi-processor configuration.
records.cause:

initialization failed.
records.recommended_action: See the User Guide for more information on supported configurations.

event_names: DIMM power fault detected - processor %1 DIMM %2. %3 (major code:%4, minor code:%5)
messages: DIMM power fault detected - processor %1 DIMM %2. %3 (major code:%4, minor code:%5)

event_names: CXL Configuration error - CXL devices installed on processor %1 exceed the lane limitation.
messages: CXL Configuration error - CXL devices installed on processor %1 exceed the lane limitation.
records.cause:
The current processor has a limit of 64 lanes for CXL 2.0 devices. The number of lanes used by the installed
CXL devices exceeds this limitation.
records.recommended_action: Remove the additional CXL devices from the indicated processor.

event_names: CXL Configuration error - the CXL cache device installed on processor %1 slot %2 is disabled.
messages: CXL Configuration error - the CXL cache device installed on processor %1 slot %2 is disabled.
records.cause: The CXL cache device installed in this slot is less than the required x8 width. The device is disabled.
records.recommended_action: Remove the CXL cache device from the processor %1 slot %2.

event_names: CXL configuration error - Number of CXL devices installed on processor %1 exceeds the limitation for the root port.
messages: CXL configuration error - Number of CXL devices installed on processor %1 exceeds the limitation for the root port.
records.cause: The current processor allows only one CXL 1.1 device per root port.
records.recommended_action:
Remove the CXL 1.1 devices, in compliance with the population guidelines present in the user
documentation.

event_names: Component Integrity Failure. System boot proceeding according to the Component Integrity Policy. Check the the security log for more information.
messages: Component Integrity Failure. System boot proceeding according to the Component Integrity Policy. Check the the security log for more information.
records.cause:
Failure is caused as at least one option card is unable to be authenticated using SPDM, either because it
lacks support or because authentication failed.
records.recommended_action:
No action needed. To require authentication of all device options prior to boot, change the Component
Integrity Policy in iLO.

event_names: Component Integrity Failure. Installed devices did not meet the Component Integrity Policy and resulted in a system freeze. For more details, check the security log.
messages: Component Integrity Failure. Installed devices did not meet the Component Integrity Policy and resulted in a system freeze. For more details, check the security log.
records.cause:
One or more devices failed to authenticate with iLO. The system is in a freeze state based on the current
Component Integrity Policy.
records.recommended_action: Reboot the system. If the failure persists, update the system firmware and iLO firmware.

records.cause: The limit for secure encryption drive keys is reached.
records.recommended_action: Remove any unused keys from the key store and retry.
